records.title: Fast prediction and optimization of oxy-fuel combustion in a MW-scale circulating fluidized bed: an integrated CFD and machine learning approach
records.verified_abstract: Oxy-fuel circulating fluidized bed (CFB) technology demonstrates significant potential for efficient carbon capture; however, its pilot-scale investigations entail substantial costs. To reduce time and costs associated with pilot-scale testing, this study presents an efficient methodology that integrates numerical simulation with machine learning for fast prediction and parameter optimization. First, a computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model for a MWth-scale CFB oxy-fuel combustor was developed based on the multiphase particle-in-cell (MP-PIC) method. The model was validated using experimental data from the MWth-scale facility, and the simulation results elucidated the distribution and evolution of key parameters governing gas-solid flow, heat transfer, and reaction processes in the furnace. Then, by integrating numerical simulation and design of experiment, a database of 120 operating conditions of oxy-fuel CFB combustion characteristics was constructed for training and testing of a neural network model. The key parameters predicted by the neural network are in good agreement with those predicted by CFD model. Correlation analysis of variables indicates that the biomass blending ratio is negatively correlated with furnace temperature and CO2 concentration, while positively correlated with NO emissions. Finally, a genetic algorithm of multi-objective optimization was performed to maximize CO2 concentration and minimize pollutant emissions, resulting in a set of optimal solutions. The combined CFD simulation and machine learning method developed in this study aids engineers in fast assessment and optimization of oxy-fuel CFB combustion.
records.scientific_rationale: 实验验证MW级CFD生成120工况，训练神经代理燃烧过程并多目标优化CO2及污染物。

records.title: A transferable deep learning framework for cross-chemistry and cross-scale state of health estimation in lithium-ion batteries
records.verified_abstract: Accurate state of health (SOH) estimation of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) is a key function of battery management systems (BMSs) for ensuring safety and efficient energy utilization. However, most existing data-driven methods are trained on single battery chemistries or cell-level datasets, which limits their robustness and generalization across different chemistries and scales. This study proposes a transfer learning (TL)-based deep learning framework that enables SOH estimation for LIBs at both cell and pack levels. First, health features across electrochemical and temporal scales are extracted to capture battery degradation dynamics. Next, a transferable deep learning framework is proposed by integrating Transformer and bidirectional long short-term memory networks. The framework is trained and validated on 119 cells across LFP, NMC, and NCA chemistries and two battery pack datasets, demonstrating its cross-chemistry and cross-scale applicability. Furthermore, Gaussian perturbations, missing values, and outliers are systematically introduced into the feature space to evaluate the model robustness under non-ideal operating conditions. The experimental results demonstrate that the framework, when transferred to the NMC and NCA datasets, achieves an MAE of 0.20% and 0.50% and RMSE of 0.24% and 0.56%, respectively. In the cell-to-pack cross-scale transfer, the MAE is maintained within 1.04%. Furthermore, under the three types of noise perturbations, the model achieves average MAE and RMSE of 1.06% and 1.21%, respectively. This study validates the potential of TL for cross-chemistry and cross-scale adaptation in battery health modeling, providing a methodology for intelligent BMSs with enhanced generalizability and robust practical applicability.
records.scientific_rationale: Transformer-BiLSTM迁移学习119电芯及两个电池包，跨化学体系/尺度验证SOH与噪声鲁棒性。

records.title: A novel photovoltaic power forecasting model based on multidimensional Mycielski and artificial intelligence
records.verified_abstract: Within the scope of the study, an innovative Mycielski based multidimensional method was developed to estimate the output power of photovoltaic panels. In this context, the hybrid integration of the developed method with artificial intelligence based prediction models was achieved, and thus, it was aimed to estimate the output power of solar energy systems more accurately. The developed Mycielski based approach enables the identification of similar patterns within historical time series data and allows the utilization of information embedded in the most analogous sequence for prediction tasks. In addition, within the scope of the study, the time series was considered multidimensionally and the information obtained by the Mycielski method was integrated into artificial intelligence-based algorithms to create advanced forecasting models. In this context, electrical quantities such as current and voltage and meteorological parameters such as temperature, radiation and humidity measured from the region were recorded during the study through the experimental system established at Afyon Kocatepe University and the success of the newly developed prediction models was evaluated with various performance criteria. The findings demonstrated that the multidimensional Mycielski model was successful in predicting the output power of photovoltaic panels and that its hybrid integration with artificial intelligence algorithms improved forecasting performance. M/Mycielski-LSTM yielded the best overall performance for both datasets, achieving RMSE, MAE, R2, R values of 4.957,1.807,0.905,0.951 for Solar Radiation–Output Power and 5.538,2.009,0.881,0.939 for Temperature–Output Power.
records.scientific_rationale: Mycielski时序匹配实际融合LSTM预测光伏功率，以大学光伏实验电气/气象数据验证。

records.title: Quantum physics-informed neural network with multi-source data fusion for prediction in PV-driven water heating systems
records.verified_abstract: Real-time prediction of stratified photovoltaic (PV)-driven water heating (PVWH) storage systems remains challenging because fluctuating PV power induces strongly nonlinear storage-state evolution through buoyancy-driven transport and thermocline migration. To address this problem, a quantum-inspired physics-informed neural network (QPINN) is developed for direct multi-step prediction of the transient temperature field in a stratified storage tank over a 60 min horizon. The framework integrates CFD-resolved fields, sparse thermocouple measurements, and PV electrical and meteorological variables within a unified learning architecture. PV-thermal coupling is established by representing electrical power supplied to the heater under both constant-power and PV-driven dynamic conditions as distributed heat generation in the heater region. In addition, a shallow quantum-circuit-inspired embedding is introduced to strengthen nonlinear feature representation and stabilize long-horizon prediction. Compared with a classical PINN, QPINN reduces RMSE by 64%–76% under constant-power heating and by 81%–87% under PV-driven dynamic heating. Under an unseen highly dynamic cloudy-day forcing case, it still achieves an RMSE reduction of 59%–64% while preserving the plume-thermocline structure. These results demonstrate that QPINN enables fast and physically grounded short-horizon forecasting of PVWH storage states, providing a practical basis for online monitoring and energy-efficient operation.
records.scientific_rationale: 量子启发嵌入PINN融合CFD/热电偶/气象数据，预测PV热水箱瞬态温度场与羽流-热跃层；不夸为实量子硬件。

records.title: Model order reduction of CFD spray field based on large language model
records.verified_abstract: Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) captures complex physical processes with high precision, but its high computational cost hinders real-time prediction in digital twin applications. Conventional reduced-order models and regression methods are constrained b y fixed input–output dimensions, which restricts their flexibility in adapting to variable and dynamic mappings between operating conditions and flow field characteristics. Benefiting from advances in large language models (LLMs), this study proposes a fast prediction framework integrating Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) and an LLM. POD is first employed to decompose high-dimensional spray fields into low-dimensional modes and coefficients to construct a reduced-order model (ROM). The mapping from operating parameters to modal coefficients is learned by an LLM via LoRA fine-tuning, with a weighted cross-entropy loss specially designed for numerical regression tasks. The proposed method outperforms Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), Decision Tree (DT), and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) in prediction accuracy, spray morphology recovery, and gaseous penetration length prediction. The predicted spray fields are physically consistent with strong generalization ability in extrapolation cases, validating the high potential of Pretrained-Tuning frame of LLM on regression tasks in specialized domains, and provides a novel, efficient pathway for real-time modeling and fast reconstruction of complex physical fields in engineering digital twins.
records.scientific_rationale: LLM实际LoRA微调学习POD喷雾模态系数，验证物理形态/贯穿长度和外推，非泛用语言性能。

records.title: A transformer-based framework with spatially adaptive embedding and meta-feature bank for wind power forecasting
records.verified_abstract: Accurate wind power forecasting (WPF) is crucial for scientific scheduling and ensures the safe integration of wind energy into the grid. Current deep learning-based wind power forecasting methods have made significant progress in extracting spatial and temporal features of the data. However, difficulty in representing spatial information of wind turbines and the high volatility of wind power lead to suboptimal performance. In this paper, we design a novel Transformer-based method integrating spatial feature embedding and meta-feature bank matching for wind power forecasting. For spatial modeling, we design identity-based spatiotemporal feature embedding mechanism. This assigns unique spatial embeddings to each turbine and combines it with other identity features. By leveraging the Transformer’s attention mechanism, it dynamically captures complex spatial relationships between turbines, addressing the challenge of modeling spatial information. Moreover, a meta-feature bank module is introduced to store representative wind power features and enhance turbine feature representation via dynamic feature retrieval and fusion. This effectively handles the high volatility of wind power and improves the model’s adaptability to complex weather patterns. Experiments on public and private datasets demonstrate that our proposed model significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving approximately 19.2% MAE reduction on the public dataset. It excels in handling the high volatility and complex spatial relationships of wind power, thereby greatly advancing the development of sustainable energy solutions. Code is available at .
records.scientific_rationale: 空间适配嵌入和元特征库Transformer实际学习风机间关系及功率时空波动，公私数据比较验证。

records.title: Self-supervised learning for electric vehicle battery remaining useful life prediction using real-world unlabeled data
records.verified_abstract: Accurate and cost-effective prediction of remaining useful life (RUL) is critical for reliable health management of electric vehicle (EV) batteries. However, most data-driven approaches for RUL prediction rely on fully supervised learning and extensive labeling, which is expensive and difficult to scale under heterogeneous operating conditions. This study proposes a contrastive-enhanced variational autoencoder–long short-term memory (VAE–LSTM) framework that leverages large-scale unlabeled charging data in a self-supervised learning paradigm. The framework is pretrained using joint reconstruction and contrastive objectives to learn monotonic degradation representations, and subsequently fine-tuned for RUL regression with limited labeled vehicles. The approach is evaluated on three real-world EV operational datasets, including one heterogeneous fleet dataset comprising passenger cars, taxis, and city buses, as well as two taxi fleets with different scales and operating characteristics. The proposed framework achieves a root-mean-square-error (RMSE) of 27 cycles, outperforming supervised and semi-supervised baselines. Label-efficiency and cross-fleet transfer studies further quantify robustness to domain shift and irregular sampling in field data. With labels from only 30% of vehicles, the pretrained model transfers to two target fleets with RMSE values of 43 and 50 cycles, respectively. A deployment-oriented cost analysis shows that the framework achieves an RMSE within 5% of the fully supervised model while reducing RUL labeling costs by about 70%. Latent factors learned during pretraining are correlated with physically meaningful voltage and energy-throughput signatures, improving interpretability. The proposed VAE–LSTM enables an accurate, interpretable, and economically scalable pathway for real-world EV battery RUL predictions.
records.scientific_rationale: VAE-LSTM以真实车队无标注充电数据重构/对比自监督学习，再少标签微调RUL，验证跨车队退化物理签名。

records.title: A novel non-dimensional multiple operating conditions physics-informed neural networks for wind turbine wake and power prediction in complex terrains
records.verified_abstract: Accurate prediction of turbine wakes in complex terrains is of great importance for the design and operational optimization of wind farms. Terrain effects not only cause significant deflection of the turbine wake but also substantially alter its recovery rate. These complex interactions go beyond the fundamental assumptions of traditional models, making it challenging for existing models to accurately predict wake velocity deficits and additional turbulence intensity. In this study, a physics-data hybrid non-dimensional multiple operating conditions physics-informed neural network (ND-MOC-PINN) wake model is proposed. The results demonstrate that inconsistencies between physical constraints and supervised data reduce the prediction accuracy of the model, whereas nondimensionalizing both the physical equations and the supervised data can significantly improve its predictive performance. The proposed ND-MOC-PINN model is employed to predict the three-dimensional turbine wake under different terrain heights. The maximum relative errors of the predicted wake velocity and turbulence intensity are within 5% and 2%, respectively. By combining the ND-MOC-PINN model with a wake superposition model, the power performance of wind farms in complex terrain is further evaluated. The results show that the proposed model achieves significantly higher accuracy than the analytical wake model, with a maximum relative error of only 5.91% in single turbine power prediction. This study can provide reliable technical support for power forecasting, layout optimization, and coordinated control in complex terrain wind farms.
records.scientific_rationale: 无量纲多工况PINN实际预测复杂地形风机三维尾流/湍强及功率，测试地形高度和外推。

records.title: A novel mesoscopic multi-head PI-DeepONet framework for generalized phase change prediction of porous composite PCMs in multi-dimensional parameter spaces
records.verified_abstract: Porous composite phase change materials (PCMs) are frequently used in latent heat thermal energy storage systems. The phase change process of these materials is influenced by multiple parameters. In practical applications, optimal parameter combinations are usually determined within a multi-dimensional space. To enable rapid prediction of these processes across various parameter combinations in multi-dimensional parameter space, a mesoscopic multi-head PI-DeepONet model is constructed. Two validation scenarios and three performance types are evaluated. The results indicate the model exhibits strong generalized prediction performance within the defined space and reliable extrapolation capabilities at representative external points. Furthermore, through a systematic evaluation of out-of-distribution test sets, reliable extrapolation directions are quantitatively determined. This establishes a unified physical criterion based on combined convection intensity to recommend safe multi-dimensional generalization boundaries. Under Validation Scenario 2, involving altered boundary conditions, the model maintained high predictive accuracy after retraining without requiring network framework modifications. Further testing in this scenario reveals an anomalous trend in which the complete melting time initially increases and then decreases with a rising Rayleigh (Ra) number. The model's rapid prediction capability is utilized to verify this trend's universality across a broader domain. Complete melting times for 10,000 parameter combinations on the Rayleigh-Stefan plane are obtained in just 145 s. The critical transition ridge on this parameter plane is revealed accordingly. This study not only demonstrates the model's strong predictive and computational acceleration capabilities but also verifies its significant potential in global optimization and practical applications.
records.scientific_rationale: 多头物理DeepONet预测多孔相变材料熔融，实际发现/验证Rayleigh-Stefan空间临界转变脊而非通用算子演示。

records.title: A novel aggregation modeling method for lithium-ion batteries based on artificial intelligence and digital twin
records.verified_abstract: Accurate prediction of lithium-ion battery End-of-Discharge (EoD) points is critical for optimizing battery operation and ensuring the safety and reliability of critical missions. However, the aging trajectories of cells in a battery pack exhibit strong spatiotemporal heterogeneity, and full life cycle discharge data are often unavailable under real operating conditions, making accurate generalized prediction difficult for traditional models. To address these issues, this article introduces the Artificial Intelligence Digital Twin (AI-DT) concept and proposes an AI-based aggregation modeling method for lithium-ion battery packs to predict voltage discharge trajectories and obtain EoD points. Firstly, the proposed Dynamic Time Warping Algorithm Based on Interpolation Method (IDTW) is used to capture time-series features from the battery discharge trajectory. Subsequently, a Discharge Trajectory Prediction (DTP) model is trained using the proposed Transformer-Length (Transformer-L) algorithm, which infers aging characteristics from partial discharge data to forecast full voltage trajectories. Considering the significant spatiotemporal differences in the aging of individual cells in the battery pack, Sliding Window based Drift Detection Method (SW-DDM) and Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) algorithm are further constructed to optimize the simulation output of the DTP model, ultimately resulting in high-precision EoD prediction. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed modeling method exhibits strong generalization capability. With only partial discharge data of an individual battery, it can achieve high-precision and highly transferable discharge trajectory prediction for the same type of cells in the battery pack throughout its entire lifecycle, thereby enabling accurate EoD estimation and providing robust support for enhancing battery reliability.
records.scientific_rationale: 实际Transformer-L与LoRA适应退化偏移，从局部电芯放电推完整轨迹及EoD，实验跨电芯寿命验证。

records.title: Physics-informed coarse-mesh method for thermohydraulic analysis: Two-phase model extension and validation against flow boiling in tubes and rod bundles with mixing vane spacers
records.verified_abstract: Accurate and efficient analysis of flow and heat transfer within energy equipment is crucial for optimizing energy systems and improving energy utilization efficiency. Two-phase flow boiling, as the core mechanism for thermal management in energy systems, ensures the efficient and safe operation of equipment. However, given the extensive application of large-scale complex tube bundles in energy equipment, efficient and accurate analysis of two-phase flow boiling within these structures remains computationally prohibitive. To address this challenge, a two-phase Physics-Informed Coarse-Mesh (PICM) method is proposed. In detail, the PICM method employs coarse meshes for calculations to minimize computational costs. To ensure accuracy, empirical correlations for flow and heat transfer based on lumped parameters are employed to model wall effects. A flow regime map is employed to classify flow structures, and regime-specific correlations are selected to model interphase interactions. To account for detailed structure effects, the cross-flow model, additional pressure loss model, and heat transfer enhancement model are introduced. Validation demonstrates that the PICM method accurately simulates two-phase flow boiling in rod bundles with mixing vane spacers. It can also regress to a 1D system method. Compared to the CFD method, the mesh size and computational time of the PICM method are reduced by three orders of magnitude. A full-core thermohydraulic analysis of a small modular pressurized water reactor with mixing vane spacers further demonstrates its practical applicability. This study provides an effective method for the refined analysis of large-scale complex tube bundles and a foundational framework for multi-scale coupling in energy systems.
records.scientific_rationale: 原摘要为粗网格守恒求解、经验关联和流型图/结构修正；physics-informed并非神经学习，现有证据不支持实质AI方法。

records.title: CGForecast: Radar conditioned graph neural network for ultra-short-term wind power forecasting
records.verified_abstract: Deep learning methods have shown promising results in multi-station ultra-short-term wind power forecasting yet remain challenging under extreme convective weather conditions due to over-reliance on coarse-resolution numerical weather prediction (NWP). To tackle this limitation, we propose CGForecast, a multimodal dual-branch framework for probabilistic forecasting across multiple wind farms. First, to address the insufficient utilization of NWP field data, CGForecast employs a graph convolutional network (GCN) to learn time-varying inter-site relations while injecting regional NWP wind field features into node states to couple local measurements with large-scale meteorological forecasts. To improve forecast stability, a Transformer-based branch is accompanied to extract global features across stations for deterministic forecasts. Then, to enhance responsiveness to convective events, we condition the GCN features by real-time radar observations via a conditional variational autoencoder, enabling the model to adjust its internal type representation according to ongoing weather without resorting to discrete event classification. Finally, we jointly optimize two branches to gain probabilistic forecasts. Extensive experiments on a year-long dataset from 10 wind farms in the Hubei Province of 2024 indicate that CGForecast improves aggregate probabilistic accuracy relative to strong baselines in most seasons where CRPS is slightly worse than scalar-input baselines in an Autumn regime, together with competitive gains under convective and rapidly changing weather types.
records.scientific_rationale: GCN学习风场空间关系，Transformer及条件VAE融合实时雷达，湖北10风场一年极端对流概率功率预测验证，保留秋季不足。

records.title: Physics-informed unified network for robust and interpretable SOH estimation of lithium-ion batteries
records.verified_abstract: Accurate and reliable estimation of lithium-ion battery state of health (SOH) is essential for battery management systems (BMSs), directly affecting safety, lifetime prediction, and energy efficiency. Although data-driven models have achieved promising accuracy, their practical deployment is often limited by insufficient physical consistency, weak cross-chemistry generalization, and poor interpretability. In this work, we propose a physics-informed unified network (PIUN) for single-step SOH estimation, which integrates physically consistent constraints into a compact gated backbone termed the Update–Candidate Branch Network (UCBNet). By jointly enforcing data fidelity and degradation-aware physical regularization, PIUN captures both static health indicators and dynamic aging behaviors within a unified framework. The PIUN is evaluated on four public battery datasets (XJTU, TJU, MIT, and HUST). Across 11 evaluation subsets, PIUN reduces MAPE and RMSE by an average of 11.5% and 7.4%, respectively, compared with the strongest baseline. Under noise-augmented training, the average improvement further increases to approximately 16%, demonstrating enhanced robustness to measurement perturbations. Cross-dataset experiments additionally confirm superior zero-shot and few-shot generalization capability. To improve interpretability, SHAP analysis is conducted and reveals strong consistency between learned feature contributions and electrochemical degradation mechanisms. Guided by SHAP-derived importance within interpretable physical dimensions, a compact subset of 7 representative features is constructed. Experimental validation demonstrates performance comparable to the full 17-feature model, thereby experimentally confirming the reliability of the SHAP-based interpretations while enabling lightweight deployment. Overall, PIUN provides a physically consistent, interpretable, and generalizable SOH estimation framework with strong practical potential for real-world BMS applications.
records.scientific_rationale: 门控神经架构加退化物理约束，四电池数据集11子组及跨集零/少样本验证SOH，SHAP与电化学机制对应。

records.title: An attentional deep learning model based on improved crested porcupine optimizer for state of health prediction of lithium-ion batteries
records.verified_abstract: This paper aims to accurately predict and effectively manage the state of health (SOH) of lithium-ion batteries to maximize their utilization. Traditional SOH prediction models based on deep learning frequently encounter issues like inadequate representation capabilities of health features (HFs) and improper hyper-parameter settings. An improved deep learning approach is developed to predict the SOH of lithium-ion batteries, leveraging a channel attention mechanism and improved Crested Porcupine Optimizer (ICPO). Firstly, a channel attention mechanism is incorporated into convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to emphasize crucial feature information, regardless of input conditions, enhancing the representation capabilities of HFs. Additionally, to overcome the shortcoming of recurrent neural network (RNN)-based single models, which ignore long-term dependencies between battery aging and HFs, a deep learning method based on the combination of gated recurrent unit (GRU) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) is developed. Furthermore, an ICPO is integrated into the model to optimize hyper-parameters for SOH prediction. Two laboratory datasets and an on-road vehicle dataset are used to validate the developed method, with all SOH prediction errors of no more than 2.2% for laboratory datasets and root mean square errors of no more than 1.0% for on-road vehicle dataset, outperforming other methods such as LSTM and its improved variants in terms of SOH prediction accuracy. These results indicate that the developed method can not only address the phenomenon of battery capacity regeneration but also delivers highly accurate and robust SOH estimation in real-world scenarios.
records.scientific_rationale: CNN通道注意与GRU-LSTM实际学习电池SOH，实验室/道路车辆验证容量再生和时序退化。

records.title: Probabilistic transfer learning for lithium-ion battery capacity estimation based on the sparse sample case
records.verified_abstract: Accurate estimation of the State of Health (SOH) for lithium-ion batteries is crucial for ensuring their safe and reliable operation. However, data-driven models often face the challenge of scarce labeled aging data in real industrial settings, which is typically difficult to obtain in industrial practice. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel probabilistic transfer learning framework based on bayesian convolutional neural networks (PTL-BCNN). The core of this approach lies in transferring knowledge from the source domain—rich in data across diverse battery types—to the target domain, which has sparse data. Its mechanism extends beyond fine-tuning deterministic parameters to adjusting the overall probability distribution of model weights. This method inherently provides uncertainty estimation alongside capacity prediction. The framework was comprehensively validated on two public datasets (Oxford and CALCE) and a custom sparse sample dataset. The proposed PTL-BCNN achieves remarkably low Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 0.71%, 1.21%, and 0.79% on these datasets, significantly outperforming traditional deep learning and transfer learning benchmark models. Crucially, the model maintains robust performance even when using only partial charging segment data, demonstrating strong practical applicability. This work establishes a probabilistic transfer learning paradigm, providing a fundamental solution for achieving reliable and data-efficient battery health estimation across different battery types.
records.scientific_rationale: 贝叶斯CNN迁移权重分布，同时估计电池容量/不确定性，Oxford/CALCE和稀疏自建实验验证。

records.title: A physics-informed neural network enhanced by fuzzy inference for remaining useful life prediction of lithium-ion batteries
records.verified_abstract: Accurate prediction of the remaining useful life (RUL) of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) is essential for ensuring the safety and reliability of energy storage systems. However, this task remains highly challenging due to measurement noise and the difficulty of maintaining physical consistency in purely data-driven models. To reconcile electrochemical physical fidelity with data adaptability, a physics-informed neural network (PINN) incorporating fuzzy inference system (FIS) enhancement is proposed, where a Takagi-Sugeno-Kang neuro-fuzzy (TSK-FIS) inference system is employed as a surrogate network to improve feature representation of nonlinear battery degradation. The resulting features are then fed into a Deep Hidden Physics Model (DeepHPM), the core physics-constrained component of the framework, within which an adaptive gated residual connection (AGRC) is embedded to tightly couple latent degradation dynamics with the network architecture. This structure effectively alleviates the error accumulation issue commonly encountered in long-horizon RUL prediction. Furthermore, to improve robustness against noise and outliers in battery data, a SoftAdapt-driven Cauchy–HawkEye loss function is designed. By introducing a small insensitive zone around the zero-residual region and adaptively balancing multiple loss components, the training stability and optimization robustness are significantly improved. Experimental results across multiple datasets indicate that the proposed method achieves superior overall predictive performance compared with baseline models, yielding a substantial reduction in RMSE while maintaining strong robustness and generalization capability.
records.scientific_rationale: TSK神经模糊代理接DeepHPM物理PINN，门控残差与鲁棒损失用于长程电池退化/RUL并实验比较。

records.title: An integrated surrogate and material optimization framework for PCM-enhanced energy piles based on EC-DeepONet
records.verified_abstract: Phase change material (PCM)-enhanced energy piles can improve subsurface heat exchange through latent-heat storage, but their transient thermal response is strongly nonlinear and difficult to optimize by large-scale high-fidelity simulation alone. To address this challenge, this study develops an integrated surrogate-based evaluation and optimization framework for PCM-enhanced energy piles. A three-dimensional transient dataset is first generated using COMSOL Multiphysics and then used to train an energy-consistency-enhanced DeepONet (EC-DeepONet) for predicting continuous-time outlet-temperature curves and cumulative heat exchange. An ensemble of five sub-models is further used to screen 25,000 candidate PCM combinations in an uncertainty-aware manner. On the validation set, EC-DeepONet reduces the root mean square errors of temperature and energy prediction to 0.0508 °C and 9.87 MJ, representing reductions of approximately 20.6% and 17.8% relative to the standard DeepONet. The Spearman rank correlation coefficient reaches 0.925, indicating good consistency in material ranking. High-fidelity re-evaluation confirms that the selected optimal PCM scheme achieves a cumulative heat exchange of 436.51 MJ over 1-100 h. The results further suggest that performance improvement is associated with coordinated matching among latent heat, heat capacity, thermal conductivity, and phase-change temperature parameters, rather than the extreme value of a single variable. The entire optimization workflow requires only ∼25.55 min, which is approximately 847 times faster than exhaustive high-fidelity scanning, providing a practical route for rapid PCM preselection and design in shallow geothermal systems.
records.scientific_rationale: 能量一致DeepONet代理热能桩热响应，训练COMSOL数据筛选25000相变材料组合并高保真复验。

records.title: A physics-informed neural network method for predicting the remaining life of energy pipelines
records.verified_abstract: The safe and stable operation of energy pipelines is directly related to energy supply security and public security. Accurate remaining service life (RSL) prediction for energy pipelines is critical to improving transmission system safety, reducing operational risks, and maintaining stable, efficient operation of the energy supply chain. However, conventional methods struggle with complex corrosion environments, limited data, poor physical consistency, and low interpretability, limiting their practical use in pipeline operation and maintenance. This paper proposes a physics-informed neural networks prediction method synergistically guided by physical consistency and feature confidence. The method uses a convolutional residual neural network as the base architecture and introduces a semi-empirical physical consistency loss function based on normative corrosion mechanisms. By constraining the model through learnable physical parameters, it ensures that both the prediction trends and numerical magnitudes conform to the physical laws of corrosion. Meanwhile, a feature confidence guidance mechanism based on gradient sensitivity is integrated to implement directional constraints on the model's dependence on key corrosion features, enhancing the interpretability of the model's feature-based decision-making. Research results indicate that compared to conventional models, the proposed model achieves a mean absolute percentage error of 9.3% and a coefficient of determination of 0.94, representing the best prediction performance. Furthermore, the model output and physical feature constraints demonstrate excellent physical consistency and interpretability. This model can effectively provide reliable technical support for the life-cycle planning, condition-based maintenance scheduling, risk prevention, and efficient stable operation of integrated energy transmission systems, thereby improving the overall safety, economy, and sustainability of integrated energy systems planning and management.
records.scientific_rationale: 卷积残差PINN加腐蚀机理/特征可信度约束，实际预测能源管道寿命并验证物理一致性。

records.title: AI-driven climate-resilient HVAC control: A scalable framework for grid-Interactive buildings
records.verified_abstract: Residential cooling systems in extreme temperature regions often operate at maximum capacity for extended periods and creating significant challenges for conventional control strategies. Conventional control strategies fail to manage the extreme diurnal temperature variations (>19°C) and rapid environmental transitions characteristic of these regions, resulting in excessive energy consumption and compromised thermal comfort. This study presents a field-validated framework integrating Digital Twin modeling, Graph Neural Networks, and Deep Reinforcement Learning for adaptive building energy management under extreme climatic conditions. The methodology was evaluated through a 14-month field study across five residential buildings in Hail, Saudi Arabia (BWh climate classification), experiencing summer temperatures exceeding 45°C. The DT model achieves high-fidelity thermal predictions (temperature RMSE: 0.62°C; energy RMSE: 0.35 kWh), enabling realistic virtual commissioning of control strategies. The GNN component models inter-zone thermal dynamics with 0.28°C RMSE for 1-h forecasts, capturing spatial dependencies conventional approaches neglect. The DRL controller optimizes HVAC operations through continuous learning, adapting to occupancy patterns and environmental conditions. Results demonstrate 35.3% energy reduction compared to conventional thermostatic control (95% CI: 32.1–38.5%), while maintaining thermal comfort within acceptable ranges for 92.0% of occupied hours versus 68.2% for baseline systems. Performance remains robust during extreme events, achieving 42.5% savings during dust storms through anticipatory control strategies. Economic analysis indicates a 26.3-month payback period with 143% five-year return on investment. The framework demonstrates scalability potential, with coordinated control across 100 buildings increasing savings to 38.0% through load balancing and demand coordination.
records.scientific_rationale: GNN建模区域热动态、DRL控制HVAC，五建筑14月现场实验验证极端气候与电网协调节能。

records.title: Novel physics informed neural network based power-thermal integrated control for extended-range electric tractor
records.verified_abstract: Power and thermal systems are critical components of hybrid tractors, where effective energy and thermal management can substantially enhance both fuel economy and thermal performance. However, the asynchronous control timescales of energy and thermal management may lead to performance degradation under prolonged high-load operations. Thus, this article presents a power-thermal integrated control strategy based on a physics-informed neural network (PINN). First, a bidirectional power-thermal coupling model is established to clarify the mutual influence relationship between power and thermal systems. Then, with the model predictive control strategy of multi-structured physics-informed neural network (MPINN-MPC), a power-thermal integrated control strategy is developed to synchronize power and thermal management within a unified time domain, which can optimize the energy flow distribution, improve the fuel economy, and maintain the critical components within the best thermal states. Finally, the effectiveness as well as performance of the proposed integrated control strategy is verified by using comparative hardware-in-the-loop tests.
records.scientific_rationale: 多结构PINN嵌入MPC，同步增程拖拉机功率/热管理并硬件在环比较验证。

records.title: Net-zero ready building control: Benchmarking Decision Transformers against deep reinforcement learning for PV–battery buildings
records.verified_abstract: The integration of Building-Integrated Photovoltaic and Battery (BIPVB) systems is a critical pathway toward carbon-neutral buildings, yet their optimal control is challenged by the stochastic nature of renewable generation and complex load dynamics. While Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has emerged as a promising model-free control approach, traditional value-based and policy-gradient methods often suffer from training instability and lack explicit long-horizon optimization capabilities. This study explores the application of the Decision Transformer (DT) to Building-Integrated Photovoltaic and Battery (BIPVB) control by reformulating the task as a return-conditioned sequence modeling problem. By leveraging the Transformer architecture, the proposed method treats the control problem as a supervised learning task, predicting optimal actions based on historical states and desired future returns (Return-to-Go). We conduct a comprehensive benchmark using the CityLearn dataset, comparing DT against a Rule-Based Controller (RBC) and six state-of-the-art DRL algorithms, including SAC, PPO, and TD3. Simulation-based benchmark results show that the DT agent achieves the lowest operational cost across the tested scenarios, yielding an 18.5% cost reduction compared to RBC and outperforming the strongest DRL baseline. Furthermore, the DT shows competitive and relatively consistent performance under varying initial battery conditions. These results suggest that sequence-modeling approaches are a promising direction for offline building energy control and merit further investigation in broader settings.
records.scientific_rationale: 实际Decision Transformer对PV电池建筑控制，与规则和六DRL算法CityLearn全面比较，科学对象与约束明确。

records.title: A physics-informed artificial intelligence framework for virtual operational data generation to enhance planning and scheduling abilities in expanding district heating systems
records.verified_abstract: To address the key challenges in urban district heating network expansion—the absence of historical data for new heat exchange stations, complex hydraulic coupling effects, and inherent system imbalance—this paper proposes a physics-informed generative AI framework for virtual operational data generation. The framework develops a graph theory-driven topology-lag fusion modeling method to accurately quantify the spatiotemporal lag correlation between stations and fully characterize the global hydraulic coupling mechanism; puts forward a Building-Thermal-Informed Liquid Neural Network (BTI-LNN) model with both strong physical interpretability and superior dynamic time-series fitting capability; and establishes a data generation system constrained by both national engineering standards and fundamental physical equations, a design that breaks the strong dependence of traditional methods on historical data. Case studies verify that, under high and low load conditions, the coefficient of determination (R2) between the data generated by the proposed method and the measured values exceeds 0.960 and 0.953, respectively, with the generation errors of water supply flow rate and temperature being less than 1.4 t/h and 0.8°C, respectively. The method thus holds significant engineering application and promotion value.
records.scientific_rationale: 建筑热物理液态神经网络生成供热站虚拟水流/温度数据，实测高低负荷验证并保留水力耦合约束。

records.title: Physics-informed soft actor-critic for constraint-aware combustion control of methanol/diesel dual-fuel engines
records.verified_abstract: Cycle-resolved combustion control of methanol/diesel dual-fuel engines under dynamic operating conditions is challenging due to strong nonlinearity, actuator coupling, and combustion safety constraints. To address these challenges, a physics-informed Soft Actor-Critic (PISAC) framework is proposed by integrating a physics-informed neural network (PINN) surrogate, an SAC-based control policy, and a constraint-aware reward formulation. The PINN embeds thermodynamic constraints into neural-network training to achieve physically consistent prediction of in-cylinder pressure and combustion indicators, providing a reliable interaction environment for reinforcement learning. Based on the surrogate environment, the SAC agent learns coordinated multi-variable control actions through offline policy optimization. Results show that the proposed PINN achieves a pressure reconstruction RMSE of 3.2 bar, while the R2 values above 0.98 for CA50, IMEP, MPRR, and COVIMEP prediction. Under dynamic operating conditions, the proposed controller reduces CA50 and IMEP RMSE from 0.075°CA to 0.271 bar to 0.026°CA and 0.099 bar, respectively, compared with a conventional PI controller. Meanwhile, MPRR violations are eliminated and COVIMEP decreases from 3.41% to 2.97%, indicating improved combustion robustness and stability. Compared with MPC, the proposed framework further improves transient response and actuator coordination under rapidly varying operating conditions. In addition, the trained policy achieves real-time feasibility with an inference time of 3 ms per cycle. These results demonstrate that the proposed PISAC framework provides an accurate, robust, and computationally efficient approach for constraint-aware combustion control of nonlinear dual-fuel engines.
records.scientific_rationale: PINN缸压燃烧指标代理供SAC离线学习双燃料控制，动态工况实证物理安全、稳定性与延迟。

records.title: Machine learning-based multi-objective optimization of hydrogen-enriched water hyacinth biodiesel–tri ethylene glycol monomethyl ether fuelled compression ignition engine with selective catalytic reduction
records.verified_abstract: Compression ignition engines fuelled with conventional diesel contribute substantially to greenhouse gas and NOx emissions, necessitating the development of cleaner and more sustainable fuel strategies. This study investigates on a blended fuel strategy that combines water hyacinth biodiesel, tri-ethylene glycol monomethyl ether, and hydrogen enrichment, with urea-based selective catalytic reduction (SCR) for NOx control. Tests were carried out on a single-cylinder engine at 1500 rpm across compression ratios of 12, 15, and 18, and brake power levels of 0.7, 2.1, and 3.5 kW under steady-state conditions with three repeated trials. The work is novel by evaluating waste-derived biodiesel, an oxygenated additive, hydrogen enrichment, and SCR alongside ANN-based prediction and multi-objective optimization in a single framework. Hydrogen–TGMEA addition shortened ignition delay to 7.5 °C A and raised peak in-cylinder pressure to 75 bar at CR 18. Brake thermal efficiency reached 31.28%, 8.2% above the biodiesel baseline, while fuel and energy consumption dropped to 0.31 kg/kWh and 12.8 MJ/kWh. NOx rose to 628 ppm but was brought down to 402 ppm by the SCR system. HC and CO2 fell to 81 ppm and 2.14% respectively. A Bayesian-regularised feedforward ANN achieved R2 values close to 0.99 across both performance and emission outputs. Coupling the ANN with a multi-objective genetic algorithm identified CR 15 and 3.1 kW as the optimal operating point, returning a BSFC of 0.3838 kg/kWh, BTE of 25.46%, CO2 of 2.418%, HC of 100.7 ppm, and NOx of 301.9 ppm, a practical balance between efficiency and emissions for sustainable CI engine operation.
records.scientific_rationale: 发动机重复实验训练贝叶斯正则ANN燃烧效率/排放预测，遗传多目标优化替代燃料和SCR运行点。

records.title: DeepWind: A foundation model for zero-shot wind power forecasting
records.verified_abstract: Wind power forecasting suffers from poor cross-regional generalization, as existing models require site-specific retraining and fail to capture the non-stationary, multi-regime nature of wind dynamics. To address these challenges, we propose DeepWind, a domain foundation model pre-trained on a newly curated corpus of approximately 560 billion time-series data points from diverse wind sites across different climates and terrains. DeepWind employs a decoder-only Transformer with a Regime-Aware Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) framework, enabling automatic specialization across distinct physical operating states (idle, ramping, and saturation) without explicit supervision. Decoupled Time and Variate Attention mechanisms further enable effective integration of heterogeneous meteorological covariates for improved zero-shot generalization. To benchmark generalization rigorously, we introduce WindBench, an eight-dataset evaluation suite covering diverse climates, resolutions, and operational scales, ensuring no overlap between training and evaluation data to guarantee unbiased zero-shot assessment. In zero-shot evaluation across WindBench, DeepWind-Base reduces nMAE by 20.86% on average over the best competing foundation model and outperforms fully supervised baselines across all forecasting horizons (1–12 h), while few-shot adaptation of DeepWind-Small with less than 3% of parameters updated achieves an average of 5.0% improvement in accuracy over full-shot baselines. The code and model weights are publicly available at https://github.com/Hexian-2001/DeepWind.
records.scientific_rationale: 风电时序基础Transformer/MoE学习多气候物理运行态，构建WindBench无重叠零样本跨区域实测评价。

records.title: Hybrid temporal fusion transformer and quantum long short-term memory network for typhoon forecasting at a wind power farm
records.verified_abstract: Typhoons pose a significant risk to wind power generation and power grid stability, exacerbating wind resource losses and causing substantial economic damage. Therefore, accurate typhoon prediction is crucial for both onshore and offshore wind farms. In this study, a novel forecasting framework, termed the Temporal Fusion Transformer–Quantum Long Short-Term Memory (TFT-QLSTM) network, is proposed to enhance forecasting performance for wind farms, particularly those located in Gaomei, Taichung, Taiwan. The QLSTM component is based on variational quantum circuits (VQCs), which replace classical linear transformations. The proposed framework generates joint 24-h-ahead forecasts across seven typhoon and wind farm variables, optimized via Chaos Quantum Energy Valley Optimization (CQEVO) and interpretable through the TFT's variable selection network. Quantitatively, for the highly volatile wind gust at Gaomei, the proposed method reduces the MAE by approximately 31% compared with the hybrid baseline (TFT-LSTM) and by more than 77% compared with the standard Extreme Learning Machine. These improvements are averaged over 20 typhoon test events and are statistically significant according to the Diebold–Mariano (DM) test. Furthermore, the ablation study demonstrates that the performance gains are attributable to the QLSTM architecture rather than merely an increase in the number of model parameters. NVIDIA CUDA-Q is employed to enable GPU-accelerated simulation of the quantum circuits within the QLSTM component, with quantum circuit execution performed on an NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU.
records.scientific_rationale: TFT+变分量子电路QLSTM实际联合预测7个台风/风场变量，20台风事件显著性/消融检验；量子电路A100模拟非实量子设备。

records.title: Machine learning optimized integration of a transcritical CO2 heat pump for sustainable and simultaneous heating-cooling in lithium-ion battery electrode drying
records.verified_abstract: Lithium-ion battery electrode drying, a pivotal yet highly energy-consuming step in manufacturing, predominantly relies on inefficient electric heating, resulting in significant carbon emissions and energy waste. The concurrent need for high-grade heating for drying and deep cooling for solvent recovery in industrial ovens presents a critical thermodynamic challenge that conventional systems fail to address efficiently. Here, we integrate a transcritical CO2 heat pump into an industrial battery electrode drying oven, exploiting the temperature glide of supercritical CO2 to simultaneously provide high-temperature drying air, recover N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) solvent, and generate byproduct hot water. Using machine-learning-assisted multi-objective optimization with a back-propagation neural network and the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II, the optimal system achieves a coefficient of performance of 3.85, a solvent recovery rate of 90.9%, and produces byproduct hot water at 65.4°C. A comprehensive 4E (Energy, Exergy, Economic, Environmental) evaluation demonstrates compelling practical viability: the system attains a ‌dynamic payback period of only 2.28 years‌ and reduces ‌carbon emissions by 74.0%‌ compared to the traditional electric heating baseline. Exergy diagnosis identifies the evaporator and compressor as primary sources of irreversibility, offering clear guidance for future technological refinement. This work presents a novel industrially viable integration of a transcritical CO2 heat pump into infrared-hot air combined battery electrode drying process, resolving the fundamental heating-cooling conflict through intelligent design and advanced optimization. It establishes a scalable, economically attractive blueprint for deep decarbonization in advanced manufacturing, applicable not only to battery production but also to a wide range of industrial drying and thermal processes.
records.scientific_rationale: BPNN代理及NSGA-II设计超临界CO2热泵电池极片干燥，研究耦合供热/溶剂回收及火用。

records.title: Physics-informed sparse regression for multi-energy load modeling of integrated energy system under extreme temperature events
records.verified_abstract: With the increasing frequency of extreme temperature events, abnormal fluctuation of multi-energy loads present significant challenges to the accuracy for multi-energy load modeling of integrated energy systems. To address these issues, a model based on physics-informed sparse regression (PISR) for multi-energy load of integrated energy systems (MEL-IES) is proposed to improve the accuracy, interpretability and data requirements of the load model under extreme temperature events for energy dispatch control. An expert database is developed to incorporate diverse dynamic characteristics of the load model, thereby enabling the construction of a control-oriented load model. Specifically, a temperature-dominated comprehensive meteorological index is proposed for the first time to enrich the diversity of elements within the expert database and to facilitate pre-screening of MEL-IES inputs. Subsequently, the double-layer model-based χ2 detection unit is improved to identify extreme temperature events, with the outputs serve as prior knowledge to trigger adaptive regulation of the MEL-IES model. Building upon this prior knowledge, a requirement-driven PISR (RD-PISR) method is developed for MEL-IES. To refine the critical physics-informed elements, the RD algorithm is employed to dynamically adjust the parameters of the PISR model for order reduction and to construct a multi-parameter fitting model, thereby achieving a balance between model simplicity and accuracy. Finally, experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves better performance than benchmark models, lowers data dependence and shortens training time by 52.3%-71.4%. Ablation experiments further indicate that this framework obtains an RMSE of 0.84%, an R2 of 0.973 and the best interpretability.
records.scientific_rationale: 实际物理稀疏回归动态拟合多能负荷、阶次学习与极温先验联动，实验/消融验证，不因基础线性回归一概排正则稀疏学习。

records.title: Building retrofitting towards net zero energy under climate change: Application of a machine learning model
records.verified_abstract: The challenge in retrofitting to achieve Net Zero Energy Building (NZEB) lies in identifying the most effective retrofit measures to optimize energy performance and reduce carbon emissions. So far, weather data from meteorological stations have mostly been used in simulations, but these do not account for future weather conditions that may result from climate change. The primary objective of this work is to develop a robust, machine-learning-driven optimization framework to identify climate-adaptive retrofit measures for residential NZEBs across diverse global locations, accounting for both current and future climate change scenarios. Thirty-five combinations of climate zones and time frames are simulated using a machine learning model, leveraging its low computational time. The non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA-III) is applied to the building model to optimize the energy consumption and the predicted percentage of dissatisfaction (PPD), while maintaining NZE balance. The Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to the Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) is then employed to identify a unique, robust optimal solution from the Pareto front. Using future scenarios defined by the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways framework, lower insulation values are recommended for the Fossil Fuel-dependent Future scenario compared to the Sustainable Future scenario, with reductions of up to 20%, 10%, and 13% in climate types C (Warm Temperate Climate), D, (Snow Climate) and E (Polar Climate), respectively. Additionally, the results indicate that building energy consumption and PPD can be reduced by up to 81% and 67%, respectively, compared to the base case through the integration of passive and renewable retrofit measures.
records.scientific_rationale: 实际ML建筑代理耦合NSGA-III在35气候时间情景优化净零改造，量化未来保温/能耗/舒适变化。

records.title: Physics-informed deep learning for combustion instability diagnosis in an acoustically forced spray swirling flame
records.verified_abstract: Combustion instability (CI) threatens the safe and efficient operation of fuel-flexible gas turbines, making reliable diagnosis critical. Although conventional deep-learning models have advanced flame-image-based CI diagnosis, their accuracy remains limited when different states exhibit highly similar visual patterns. More importantly, it remains unclear whether these models exploit superficial image cues or capture the coherent modal dynamics underlying CI. This paper develops a deep-learning framework integrating accurate diagnosis with physics-informed interpretation using high-speed OH* chemiluminescence images of an ethanol spray swirling flame. To our knowledge, this is the first application of a fine-tuned multimodal large language model (MLLM, Qwen) to CI diagnosis. Qwen achieves a mean test accuracy of 99.67%, compared with 97.29%, 98.96%, and 83.69% for CNN, CNN-LSTM, and CNN-Transformer, respectively. POD modal retention and removal are then used as controlled physical perturbations to identify the flame structures supporting model decisions. The CNN mainly relies on medium- and high-order local structures, whereas the CNN-LSTM further exploits their temporal evolution. By contrast, Qwen exceeds 80% accuracy using only the first 10 POD modes, which contain approximately 55% of the fluctuation energy, and is highly sensitive to Modes 2-4, which capture the forcing-induced advancement of longitudinal modes and the redistribution from spiral-like to longitudinal structures. These results show that modal energy does not determine diagnostic relevance and that different architectures rely on distinct physical evidence. Qwen's superior performance is associated with its joint use of coherent modal reorganization and multiscale local flame information. The proposed framework improves both diagnostic accuracy and physical interpretability, providing a basis for active control of low-carbon gas turbines.
records.scientific_rationale: Qwen多模态模型实际微调诊断喷雾旋焰不稳定性，POD控制物理扰动解释不同架构利用的火焰结构。

records.title: Physics-informed large language model with contrastive temporal embedding for transient thermal-hydraulic prediction in loss-of-coolant accidents
records.verified_abstract: Reliable transient assessment during loss-of-coolant accidents (LOCAs) is essential for maintaining the safety and flexibility of nuclear energy systems, yet remains challenging because the underlying two-phase thermal-hydraulic process is highly nonlinear, rapidly varying and expensive to resolve numerically. This study proposes a physics-informed large language model, termed PI-LLM, for fast assessment of LOCA parameters with limited accident data. The model integrates three complementary components. First, a suffix-aware contrastive embedding strategy aligns textual physical priors with critical temporal segments, enabling the model to emphasize abrupt changes during coolant loss. Second, a multi-scale wavelet convolutional neural network extracts coupled trend and transient features from pressure, flow, void fraction, velocity, density and internal-energy signals. Third, a self-supervised signal-to-text reconstruction module regularizes hidden representations by recovering masked physical variables and their first-order temporal variations. Physics-informed residuals derived from the two-fluid six-equation model are incorporated into the training objective to improve physical consistency. Experiments on a multi-pipeline LOCA simulation dataset show that PI-LLM achieves an average MAE of 0.0027, RMSE of 0.0159 and R2 of 0.9984, outperforming PINN, KAN and Time-LLM baselines. Ablation and sensitivity analyses further confirm that contrastive temporal alignment, multi-scale frequency-domain extraction and self-supervised reconstruction jointly improve accuracy and robustness near accident-induced transients. These results indicate that PI-LLM can serve as an efficient surrogate for real-time thermal-hydraulic assessment and decision support in low-carbon nuclear energy systems.

records.title: Cross-scale regime-aware physics-informed forecasting for reliable wind-speed prediction in risk-aware wind power operation
records.verified_abstract: Reliable wind-speed forecasting is essential for risk-aware wind power operation, but aggregate accuracy can be dominated by normal samples and conceal large errors under gust-dominated regimes. To address this pseudo-accuracy problem, this study proposes the Adaptive Gated Physics-informed Network (AGruPn), a cross-scale regime-aware forecasting framework that links fine-grained operating-condition recognition, regime-adaptive physical prediction, and uncertainty quantification. AGruPn first reconstructs high-frequency wind-speed dynamics from sparse observations, then identifies operating regimes through a cross-scale statistical trigger, and finally activates a gated adaptive physical-guided network with learnable spline parameterization, Partial Differential Equation (PDE)-inspired temporal residuals, Genetic Programming (GP)-based gust closure, and physics-guided quantile learning. Unlike a single global predictor, AGruPn uses the recognized regime to switch the active physical residual and to modulate the interaction between data loss, physical consistency, symbolic gust correction, and interval generation. Experiments on National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL), Open Renewable Energy Systems (ORES), Site1–3, Aventa, and Mountain Distributed Generation Test (MDGT) datasets show that AGruPn improves both point and interval forecasting against recurrent, decomposition-based, physics-informed, and contemporary long-sequence baselines. On Site1–3 and Aventa, AGruPn obtains the lowest overall symmetric mean absolute percentage error (SMAPE) values of 2.709, 2.719, 2.789, and 11.849, respectively. On NREL and ORES, AGruPn achieves SMAPE values of 3.728 and 3.639, improving over the best competing methods by 4.95% and 1.65%. Condition-specific and ablation analyses further show that regime-aware physical constraints improve interval reliability and reveal remaining challenges under high-frequency gust subsets.

records.title: An attention-guided residual block-based physics-informed neural network for interpretable SOH estimation of lithium-ion batteries
records.verified_abstract: Data-driven approaches are commonly used for estimating the state of health (SOH) of lithium-ion batteries, but their lack of interpretability and high data dependence limit practical use. To address this, we propose ARPINN, an Attention-Guided Residual block-based Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN). ARPINN enhances transparency and reliability in SOH estimation. It uses the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) film growth model to simulate battery degradation and incorporates Deep Hidden Physics Modeling (DeepHPM) within the PINN framework to approximate the partial differential equations (PDEs) governing degradation. The network includes residual block connections to handle nonlinearity and multi-scale aging dynamics. A physics-based monotonic constraint is embedded in ARPINN to relate peak areas of incremental capacity (IC) curves to SOH, ensuring consistency with electrochemical degradation mechanisms like active material loss. Additionally, ARPINN introduces an Initial State Attention (ISA) mechanism to capture temporal features by computing similarity to the initial charging cycle. Combining physical modeling, residual design, and attention-guided learning enables ARPINN to achieve high interpretability. Experimental evaluations on TJU and CALCE datasets show that ARPINN improves prediction accuracy, achieving an average Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of less than 2% across different datasets. Furthermore, extensive validation demonstrates its superior robustness and generalization capability in small-sample learning and cross-system transfer scenarios.

records.title: Physics-informed dynamic environmental footprint assessment and intelligent energy management for PV–heat pump sustainable building energy systems in hot-arid climates
records.verified_abstract: Hybrid photovoltaic (PV)–heat pump building systems can reduce fossil-fuel dependence, but their environmental performance is difficult to evaluate when PV generation, heat-pump efficiency, storage states, grid import, and recovered heat vary hourly. This study develops an EnergyPlus–physics-informed neural network (PINN)–adaptive life cycle assessment (LCA)–deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework for dynamic environmental-footprint evaluation and control of a PV–air-to-water heat pump (A2WHP)–thermal energy storage (TES)/battery energy storage system (BESS)–hydrogen waste heat recovery (H2-WHR) building system in the hot-arid climate of Najran, Saudi Arabia. EnergyPlus generated hourly reference data, while the PINN provided fast physics-constrained surrogate predictions of PV output, heat-pump thermal output, TES temperature, H2-WHR contribution, and grid exchange. Adaptive LCA converted hourly operational flows into carbon, water, energy, and natural resource footprints, which were aggregated into a normalized Environmental Footprint Index (EFI). DRL optimized operating actions using EFI, cost, comfort, and operational-constraint terms. The PINN achieved R2 values above 0.90 for PV output and 0.99 for heat-pump thermal output, with physics residuals below 12% of system power. Compared with the S1 rule-based baseline, the selected environmental-priority DRL policy reduced EFI from 1.00 to 0.74 and decreased annual operating cost by 18% while keeping comfort violations below 1.1%. Pareto and sensitivity analyses identified cost–environment trade-offs, heat-pump COP, and H2 recovery ratio as key performance drivers. Practical H2-WHR implementation requires short-distance access to low-grade heat through insulated district-scale networks with acceptable exergy losses.

records.title: A spatiotemporal physics-informed deep learning framework incorporating wake interference modeling for enhanced wind farm power prediction performance
records.verified_abstract: With the increasing scale of wind farms, the impact of wake effects on turbine safety and power generation efficiency becomes increasingly significant. In practical engineering applications, ultra-short-term wind farm power prediction requires reliable prediction accuracy, generalization performance, and computational efficiency. To this end, this paper proposes a comprehensive power prediction framework integrating physical information and deep learning. By spatiotemporally decoupling the physical process of power generation into three stages of flow field reconstruction, wake topological inference, and power mapping, the proposed framework establishes physics-data coupled models for single-turbine wakes, multi-turbine wake interactions, and power prediction, respectively. To ensure that prediction results comply with the fundamental laws of fluid evolution and energy conversion, the Navier-Stokes equations, the vorticity equation, inter-turbine influence relationships, and theoretical power curves are embedded as physical constraints, enabling the framework to adapt to dynamic operating conditions. Furthermore, a closed-loop error correction mechanism based on transfer learning is introduced to mitigate cumulative errors of turbines, and a gradient-based normalization and loss weight training strategy is adopted to resolve optimization conflicts between data and physical equations, ensuring stable model convergence. Validation based on simulated and measured data demonstrates that the mean absolute error and mean absolute percentage error of the framework are 73.67 kW and 3.06%, respectively, with a millisecond-level computational speed. This work provides model support for digital wind farm operations and intelligent power grid dispatching.

records.title: Unsupervised early warning of thermal runaway in electric vehicle batteries via a hierarchical multi-scale Transformer and extreme value theory
records.verified_abstract: Early detection of battery thermal runaway (TR) is critical for timely intervention and improved occupant safety. However, early TR signals are often weak, and real fault samples are extremely scarce, which limits the practical use of supervised learning. Conventional unsupervised methods, meanwhile, often produce high false-positive rates during long-term monitoring. To address these challenges, this study proposes an unsupervised early-warning framework for electric vehicle batteries that combines a hierarchical multi-scale Transformer (HMS-Transformer) with extreme value theory (EVT). The framework determines the temporal memory length through autocorrelation analysis and captures both transient voltage fluctuations and cross-scale temporal dependencies through a hierarchical multi-branch architecture. Further analysis shows that conventional attention tends to become overly diffused in long-cycle battery monitoring, reducing its ability to discriminate weak fault-related anomalies. To improve thresholding under non-Gaussian residual distributions with pronounced upper-tail behavior, an automated EVT strategy with parameter-stability screening is developed to generate tail-adaptive decision thresholds. Experiments on three months of long-term real-world BMS records with a nominal 10-s upload interval show that, within the available held-out test set, the proposed method detects all three fault vehicles and produces no false-positive warning among the two normal-test vehicles under an EVT-based point-wise decision rule. The first warning triggers occur well before the final valid prediction points of the fault-vehicle sequences, indicating early risk-associated abnormal operating-state deviations. These warnings are intended to support early inspection and intervention rather than direct time-to-TR prediction.

records.title: FNO-FiLM: A geometry-conditioned neural operator for rapid transient simulation of undulating gas-condensate pipelines
records.verified_abstract: Online monitoring and flow assurance of offshore gas-condensate gathering pipelines under sparse field instrumentation depend on rapid and accurate transient simulation. The undulating geometry of these pipelines drives gravity redistribution along the pipe axis, which together with phase change shapes a strongly coupled two-phase transient. However, conventional physics-based simulators rely on fine discretization and empirical closures, precluding real-time use. Data-driven surrogates avoid this limitation but typically learn mappings on fixed discretizations, and existing applications to pipeline transients remain confined to single-phase flow on simple geometries. To address this gap, the transient simulation of gas-condensate two-phase flow in undulating pipelines is formulated as a geometry-conditioned operator learning problem. To solve it, Fourier Neural Operator with Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FNO-FiLM) injects the geometric prior into a Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) backbone through a dual-path mechanism combining shallow input concatenation with deep feature-wise modulation at every Fourier layer. A high-fidelity transient database is generated with OLGA, covering diverse geometries, boundary perturbations, and initialization strategies. FNO-FiLM achieves an overall MAPE of 0.607% and consistently attains the lowest errors on all five target outputs among eight representative baselines, while delivering three orders of magnitude speedup over OLGA. Even under autoregressive rollouts of thirty times the training horizon, FNO-FiLM reduces MAPE by up to 75% relative to a plain FNO, while preserving resolution invariance under refined grids and keeping errors below 0.26% across four typical engineering scenarios. These results suggest a promising surrogate paradigm for online transient prediction in offshore oil and gas pipeline operation.

records.title: Standalone and physics-informed machine learning for inline decoupling of non-ideal biofuel blends to optimize engine control
records.verified_abstract:
Biofuels are viable alternatives for climate mitigation; however, their combustion performance varies with feedstock sources and production processes. Dielectric sensors have been used to decrypt fuel blend compositions, transmitting the information to ECU for optimizing engine performance.
In this study, multi-component alternative fuel networks encompassing gasoline, diesel, biodiesels, and alcohols were evaluated across five commercial sensors at 20 °C. Furthermore, moisture stress triggered unphysical multi-phase fluid stratification and hard signal clamping. Eighteen standalone AIML architectures were applied for data processing. While top standalone algorithms like KNN delivered deceptively flawless marks, tracking paths exposed unphysical staircase artifacts across sparse training gaps. Erasing these artifacts via brute-force data augmentation achieved global convergence but imposed severe over 100-fold data penalties.
To bypass brute-force scaling, a physics-informed integrated framework was formulated by integrating piecewise multi-zone calibration curves with a thermodynamic model embedding localized activity coefficients to capture intense non-ideal fluid boundaries. Utilizing only the original sparse training matrix, this integrated white-box framework completely suppressed local over-fitting, yielding an outstanding global frequency-domain R2 of 0.99638 paired with an exceptional MAE = 1.03832 Hz and SMAPE = 1.2438%. This paradigm establishes a highly hardware-compatible, resource-efficient pathway for real-time onboard fuel decryption under severe data-scarce and hardware-clamping constraints.

records.title: Physics-informed feature reconstruction integrated with selective freezing transfer strategy for cross-domain fuel consumption prediction of heterogeneous ships
records.verified_abstract: Accurate ship fuel consumption prediction is vital for maritime decarbonization. However, conventional ships are severely constrained by sparse operational data, while applying conventional transfer learning across heterogeneous vessels induces severe negative transfer due to intrinsic physical discrepancies between hybrid systems containing electrical/battery parameters and traditional diesel ships relying entirely on mechanical-thermal characteristics. To address these data scarcity and negative transfer challenges, this work proposes a physics-informed decoupled transfer learning framework to predict fuel consumption for a data-scarce conventional inland bulk carrier (300 target samples) using operational data from a data-rich modern hybrid tugboat (2500 source samples) under steady-state navigation. First, a Physics-Informed Feature Reconstruction (PIFR) algorithm transforms complex electromechanical coupling features of the hybrid source ship into isomorphic mechanical load feature spaces, eliminating domain differences. Second, a dual-branch attention network combined with an asymmetric selective parameter freezing strategy retains universal hydrodynamic prior knowledge of the source domain while fine-tuning the mechanical feature mapping for the target domain. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively mitigates the negative transfer observed in direct transfer, improving ${\mathrm{R}}^{2}$ from a negative value to 0.96 and reducing RMSE to 0.12, outperforming the evaluated machine-learning, deep-learning, and direct-transfer baselines. This work bridges the gap in cross-domain energy prediction between heterogeneous marine power systems under data scarcity.

records.title: Multi-objective optimization of biomass and waste gasification for hydrogen production using physics-informed multi-fidelity data fusion and NSGA-II
records.verified_abstract: Effective regulation of biomass and waste gasification is crucial for optimizing hydrogen production. However, traditional mechanistic models lack adaptability to complex real-world conditions, and purely data-driven approaches are severely constrained by data scarcity, hindering robust model construction. To address this, an optimization framework integrating physics-informed multi-fidelity data fusion and the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) is proposed to optimize operating parameters of biomass and waste gasification to produce hydrogen-rich syngas. Initially, extensive Aspen Plus simulation data are used to train a base neural network. A Bayesian calibration network subsequently fuses this pre-trained model with limited experimental samples guided by physical rules, significantly enhancing cross-domain generalization and interpretability. Using this fusion model, the NSGA-II is employed to precisely optimize multi-objective parameters tailored to biomass and waste gasification. The framework's effectiveness was validated through three case studies: cross-feedstock application, simulation-to-experiment inverse optimization, and hydrogen-rich syngas production via municipal solid waste (MSW) gasification. Demonstrating robust optimization capabilities, the framework identified optimal conditions for the complex MSW scenario (850 °C and a steam-to-biomass ratio of 1.19), successfully achieving an optimal hydrogen yield of 1.246 Nm3/kg. Ultimately, through comparison with literature-reported experimental results, this framework achieves better predictive accuracy and optimizes hydrogen yield and carbon conversion efficiency, advancing beyond current models.
