records.title: Experimental investigation of thermal performance and artificial neural network prediction of a phase change material-based battery thermal management system
records.verified_abstract: Efficient thermal management is essential to ensure the safety, reliability, and performance of lithium-ion battery (LIB) packs operating under high discharge conditions. This study experimentally investigates a phase-change material (PCM) based battery thermal management system (BTMS) for a 48 V, 10 Ah battery pack composed of 52 cylindrical cells. Thermal behavior of the battery pack was evaluated at discharge rates of 1C, 2C, and 3C under ambient conditions, both without cooling and with cooling using a paraffin wax (PW) base PCM. Key performance metrics include maximum temperature (Tmax), maximum temperature difference (ΔTmax), average temperature (Tavg), and temperature uniformity. Without cooling, Tmax reached 53.75, 56.89, and 58.92 °C at 1C, 2C, and 3C, respectively. With PCM cooling, Tmax reached 48.77, 52.09, and 54.25 °C. Similarly, without cooling, the ΔTmax values were 5.64, 13.58, and 18.7 °C at discharge rates of 1C, 2C, and 3C, respectively. With PCM cooling, these values were reduced to 3.73, 5.81, and 6.6 °C, respectively, indicating enhanced thermal uniformity. Additionally, Tavg declined from 51.21 °C to 48. 86 °C at 1C, with consistent reductions observed at high discharge rates. Temperature uniformity improved correspondingly, decreasing from 2.30 to 1.50 °C. Overall, the system achieved a maximum temperature reduction of 64.7 % under higher-discharge conditions. An Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model was developed for temperature prediction, achieving prediction errors within ±1 °C and a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.99. The results confirm that integrating PCM-based BTMS with ANN modelling significantly enhances the thermal safety of LIBs and predictive capability.

records.title: Polymer-concrete-rock composite structure for compressed air energy storage caverns: airtightness evaluation and random forest-based leakage prediction
records.verified_abstract: Air leakage is a major constraint on the long-term operation of hard-rock compressed air energy storage (CAES) caverns under cyclic thermo-mechanical loading. Existing studies mainly focus on unlined or conventional single-lined caverns, while the coupled response of polymer–concrete–rock multilayer linings remains insufficiently understood. This study develops a fully coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical (THM) numerical framework to investigate cavern thermodynamics, deformation, gas migration, and leakage behavior. The framework is evaluated against three complementary benchmark cases representing concrete-lined rock, unlined hard-rock, and commercial salt-cavern conditions. Under the adopted material properties, constitutive assumptions, and interface conditions, the polymer–concrete–rock configuration reaches a peak operating pressure of 14.8 MPa and an average leakage percentage of 0.21% over the 72-h three-cycle period. Relative to the unlined cavern, the average leakage metric is reduced by 63.79%, while the 72-h cumulative leakage mass decreases by 84.4 t (49.62%). Compared to the concrete-rock structure, the leakage rate is reduced by 51.16%, with a cumulative gas loss reduction of 56.2 tons. Furthermore, to overcome the high computational cost and low efficiency of traditional numerical simulations, a Random Forest surrogate model is trained using 72,000 sets of simulation samples, enabling millisecond-level leakage prediction on low-cost hardware. The integrated analysis framework combining physical mechanisms and data-driven methods established in this paper provides a theoretical foundation and technical support for the structural optimization and long-term safe operation of high-pressure hard rock CAES caverns.

records.title: Deep Learning-Based Framework for Energy Control and Management in Commercial Smart Buildings and Hot and Arid Climate
records.verified_abstract: This study proposes a robust and smart predictive framework for estimating the indoor thermal environment and cooling load demand in a commercial office unit located in a hot and arid climate, during extreme weather conditions. To ensure the generalizability and robustness of the proposed framework, the model was evaluated using onother climatic datasets with temperate highland climate. The office unit consists of five distinct sections with different uses. The framework is a hybrid model combined gated recurrent unit (GRU) neural networks enhanced with a self-attention mechanism to improve time-series prediction accuracy for cooling load demand, indoor temperature, humidity, and residents' thermal comfort. The occupational behavior, along with environmental data and HVAC technical information, was used to enhance the model accuracy. The proposed GRU-Attention model significantly outperformed the standalone GRU model across all prediction tasks. The results showed that in predicting the cooling load, the proposed hybrid model succeeded in achieving RMSE values of 0.5669 and R^{2} of 0.9918 in the concentrated sections, which shows a significant improvement compared to the values of 1.1603 and 0.9657 for the standard GRU model. In addition, in estimating the thermal comfort indices, the accuracy of the model was significantly improved; so that the RMSE for the PMV index decreased from 0.0920 to 0.0580 and for the PPD index from 1.1210 to 0.8900. The GRU-Attention model provides a robust platform for implementing a controller by providing highly accurate predictions with minimal noise. This approach can lead to energy savings, which is a fundamental step towards realizing net-zero carbon buildings and improving energy resilience in smart urban contexts.

records.title: Physics-informed circumferential graph variational autoencoder for exhaust gas temperature anomaly detection in gas turbines
records.verified_abstract: Exhaust gas temperature (EGT) anomaly detection is essential for monitoring gas turbine hot components. However, distinguishing condition-induced EGT fluctuations from weak fault deviations remains challenging. This paper proposes an uncertainty-aware physics-informed circumferential graph variational autoencoder (PICG-VAE) for EGT anomaly detection. Operating-condition and historical EGT measurements are independently encoded and fused within the variational latent space. A hybrid EGT graph combines the fixed circumferential topology with a learnable adjacency matrix. Physics-informed circumferential structure loss and spectral consistency loss are designed to preserve local circumferential gradients and multiscale spectral characteristics. Uncertainty-normalized residuals are adopted as the monitoring statistic for anomaly detection. Across eight independent runs, PICG-VAE achieves a false alarm rate of 0.86 ± 0.42% and an average recall at 5°C (AR@5°C) fault magnitude of 91.8 ± 3.95%. Ablation studies identify graph modeling as the most influential architectural component, with its removal reducing AR@5°C by 51.6 percentage points. The learnable graph connectivity improves AR@5°C by 16.0 percentage points with only a 0.5% increase in parameters. Compared with state-of-the-art methods, PICG-VAE improves average recall by 2.5 percentage points, and reduces parameters by 36.56%. Additionally, PICG-VAE can adapt to gas turbines with different numbers of EGT sensors. Overall, PICG-VAE balances weak-anomaly sensitivity, false-alarm control, and efficiency.

records.title: Thermal-safety-constrained cooling energy optimization for data centers using a physics-informed graph surrogate model
records.verified_abstract: The rapid growth of data center electricity demand has increased the need for energy-efficient cooling operation while maintaining local thermal safety. However, high-fidelity thermal simulation is computationally expensive, and purely data-driven surrogate models often neglect the physical topology of rack-level heat transfer and air supply paths. To address this issue, this study proposes a thermal-safety-constrained cooling energy optimization framework for non-uniformly loaded data centers. A physics-informed thermal graph is constructed to explicitly represent rack operating states, adjacent rack thermal coupling, and directed air-supply relationships from cooling units. Based on high-fidelity thermal environment simulations, a graph neural network surrogate is developed to rapidly estimate rack-level outlet temperature distributions and hotspot risks. The trained surrogate is further embedded into a differential-evolution-based optimization framework to identify energy-efficient cooling setpoints under rack outlet temperature constraints. The results show that the proposed surrogate achieves accurate rack-level temperature estimation, with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.379 °C and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.523 °C. Compared with the baseline operation, the optimized cooling strategy reduces the average local power usage effectiveness (PUE) from 1.798 to 1.603, corresponding to an energy efficiency improvement of 10.82%, an average daily electricity saving of 255.3 kWh, and a carbon emission reduction of 148.3 kg CO2. The proposed framework provides a fast and physically interpretable tool for cooling energy management and local thermal safety control in data centers.

records.title: Physics-informed safe reinforcement learning with adaptive PID–Lagrangian control for long-term cascade reservoir scheduling
records.verified_abstract: Cascade hydropower scheduling under stochastic inflows requires coordinated generation decisions subject to coupled hydraulic and operational constraints. This study develops PI–RPPO–PID by adapting and integrating established physics-informed action projection, recurrent proximal policy optimization, and PID-Lagrangian regulation for sequential cascade-reservoir scheduling. A normalized pre-projection Safety Cost aggregates the constraint violations implied by raw policy actions across reservoirs and constraint categories, retaining a learning signal even when action projection corrects the executed decisions. The framework is assessed using the lower Jinsha River cascade through staged parameter screening, multi-seed algorithm comparisons, fixed-multiplier comparisons, and frozen-policy replay under observed and empirical-frequency inflows. Under the evaluated settings, RPPO achieves lower pre-projection constraint pressure and higher incremental generation than feedforward PPO. Adaptive PID regulation meets the prescribed Cost target while retaining substantial generation benefits relative to the three selected fixed-multiplier settings. Historical replay and additional P01 and P99 scenarios illustrate dispatch responses under interannual variability and extreme frequency-based inflow conditions. Executed-dispatch compliance is assessed separately from pre-projection Cost attainment. These findings demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively integrates physical constraint handling, temporal policy learning, and adaptive constraint regulation, providing an effective and interpretable approach to safe cascade hydropower scheduling under the investigated stochastic inflow conditions.

records.title: Physics-guided feature synergy transformer for battery state of health estimation
records.verified_abstract: Accurately estimating the state of health (SOH) is paramount for ensuring the safety and reliability of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). While existing methods employ multiple health features (HFs) for battery SOH estimation, their generalization across varying operating conditions and chemical compositions remains limited, as the synergistic interactions among these features are often neglected. To address these limitations, a physics-guided feature synergy transformer (PGFS-Former) is proposed for robust and interpretable SOH estimation with a multi-feature fusion strategy. Specifically, degradation-informed and physically interpretable HFs, including the constant current (CC) charging time, the mean CC charging voltage, and the peak value of the incremental capacity (IC) curve, are selected to provide physics guidance at the feature-construction level. In PGFS-Former, an adaptive feature fusion module initialized with the Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) is designed to dynamically integrate multiple features during model training, while the multi-head cross-attention (MHCA) mechanism is responsible for capturing the complex synergistic interactions among HFs. The PCC algorithm is used to quantify the linear association between each feature and the SOH of LIBs for initializing the feature weights, thereby providing a transparent and statistically informed starting point for subsequent data-driven optimization. The comparative experiments and ablation experiments on batteries across different chemical compositions and charge-discharge protocols are conducted to demonstrate the performance of PGFS-Former for battery SOH estimation.

records.title: A method for quantifying fuel cell degradation power loss mechanisms based on an identifiability-driven physics-informed neural network
records.verified_abstract: The output power of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFC) decreases after long-term operation. Existing diagnostic methods require shutdown testing or dedicated equipment, which severely disrupts production operations; consequently, the entire stack is often replaced directly in engineering practice, resulting in substantial economic waste. To address these issues, this paper proposes an identifiability-driven physics-informed neural network (ID-PINN) method. Specifically, a multi-mechanism coupled electrochemical model covering five degradation pathways is embedded as a differentiable physics-constrained layer. A dual-branch architecture comprising a monotonic baseline and operating-condition residuals separates irreversible aging from operating-condition disturbances, identifies the evolutionary trajectories of 5 degradation-sensitive parameters using only routine operational data, and decomposes mechanism-level power losses under a unified rated operating condition. Validation using 994.88 h of long-term test data from an in-house stack and a public dataset from Tongji University shows that the test-segment voltage-prediction MAPEs of the two datasets are 1.89% and 1.39%, respectively. The ohmic, activation, and mass-transfer degradation trends reflected by 83 measured impedance spectra are consistent with the model identification results. The cumulative stack power loss is approximately 282.84 W, of which the model attributes 92.2% to catalyst activity decay, providing priority directions for stack inspection and maintenance.

records.title: A region-aware physics-informed deep neural network for temperature-field reconstruction and cooling optimization of electric-vehicle liquid-cooled SiC power modules
records.verified_abstract: Rapid prediction of temperature and pressure fields is needed to balance thermal protection and pumping demand in liquid-cooled silicon carbide (SiC) traction inverters. A region-aware physics-informed deep neural network (PI-DNN) is developed to convert high-fidelity conjugate thermal-fluid simulations into a fast, physically consistent surrogate, trained on 60 operating cases spanning loss, coolant flow rate, and inlet temperature, generated by coupling an electrothermal loss model with a three-dimensional model. The network encodes material regions explicitly, applies Fourier feature encoding to the spatial coordinates, and embeds conservation, boundary, and solid-fluid interface constraints in the training loss. On the test set, the PI-DNN reconstructs the temperature field with a mean absolute error of 0.933 °C and an R^{2} of 0.9931, outperforming Kriging and support vector regression baselines. In three representative experimental cases, the largest absolute difference between the predicted SiC chip-top and infrared-reported surface-temperature maxima is approximately 2.6 °C. The PI-DNN also reconstructs the pressure field with an R^{2} of 0.9937. Each field evaluation takes 0.349 s, more than three orders of magnitude faster than COMSOL. Coupled with multi-objective optimization, the surrogate reveals a diminishing thermal return of increasing coolant flow: raising the flow rate from 8 to 11 L/min lowers the maximum junction temperature by 5.88 °C, but a further 1.02 L/min yields only an additional 1.82 °C reduction. The resulting Pareto front provides a quantitative basis for selecting flow rates that balance thermal margin against pumping power, providing a practical tool for steady-state thermal assessment and cooling-strategy selection of SiC inverters.

records.title: Advanced exergy analysis and machine learning assisted multi-objective optimization of a CO2/R32-based mixture cycled Carnot battery
records.verified_abstract: Carnot battery is a promising grid-scale energy storage technology for facilitating the integration of a high proportion of renewable electricity into power grids. To further improve its thermodynamic performance, this study proposes a Carnot battery system using a CO_{2}/R32 mixed working fluid and cascaded thermal storage to reduce irreversibility through improved temperature matching between the working and heat-transfer fluids. Energetic, exergetic, and economic models are developed and integrated with a machine-learning-assisted multi-objective optimization framework. The conventional exergy analysis is complemented by advanced exergy analysis to reveal the interaction mechanisms among system components and identify their real potential for improvement. The multi-objective optimization results show that the Pareto front achieves a maximum exergy efficiency of 62.99%, with minimum LCOE and avoidable exergy destruction values of 160.24 USD·MWh^{−1} and 1.55 MW, respectively. The optimal trade-off solution selected by TOPSIS yields an LCOE of 170.32 USD·MWh^{−1} and a system avoidable exergy destruction of 2.08 MW, while eliminating the avoidable irreversibilities would increase the exergy efficiency from 62.20% to 68.63%. Furthermore, based on the optimal condition, conventional exergy analysis shows that Cooler 2 is the largest source of exergy destruction, reaching 1.76 MW and accounting for 21.60% of the total exergy destruction. In contrast, advanced exergy analysis identifies the turbine as the component with the greatest optimization potential, as it exhibits the highest avoidable endogenous exergy destruction of 0.658 MW, accounting for 43.46% of the total avoidable endogenous exergy destruction. Finally, the endogenous exergy destruction is greater than exogenous exergy destruction for most components, indicating that component interactions within the system are complex but relatively insignificant. This finding demonstrates that the thermodynamic performance of the system is governed primarily by the intrinsic irreversibilities of individual components.

records.title: Physics-informed data-driven bidding strategy for wind power producers in the electricity spot market under imperfect information
records.verified_abstract: Strategic bidding enables wind power producers (WPPs) to improve their profits in electricity spot markets. However, designing effective bidding strategies remains challenging under imperfect information, limited historical samples, and wind power uncertainty. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a physics-informed data-driven bidding framework for WPPs, consisting of lower-level market clearing reconstruction and upper-level bidding optimization. At the lower level, directional priors of the power transfer distribution factor (PTDF) are extracted from congestion prices, and structural priors of market clearing critical regions (CRs) are derived from multi-parametric linear programming (MPLP) theory. These priors are embedded into a physics-informed competitive support vector machine (PI-CSVM) and a physics-informed affine regression model (PIARM) for CR boundary identification and market clearing reconstruction, respectively. At the upper level, a risk-integrated stepwise offer curve is designed to determine offer quantities under wind power uncertainty, and a bidding optimization model is developed to optimize the corresponding offer prices. The proposed method is validated on the IEEE 30-bus system and a 144-bus system from a Chinese province. Numerical results demonstrate its effectiveness in market clearing reconstruction and WPP profit improvement.

records.title: Kinetic anchoring for interpretable machine learning of thermal performance in catalytic hydrogen combustion microchannel reactors
records.verified_abstract:
Catalytic hydrogen combustion (CHC) microchannel reactors are compact heat sources for hydrogen energy conversion, but their thermal performance is difficult to analyze because surface kinetics, inlet organization, U-bend intensification, and coupled transport act simultaneously. This work develops a kinetic anchoring strategy for interpretable machine learning by combining a low-fidelity Cantera reference with high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) responses through linear calibration and residual learning. Implemented as physics-guided machine learning (PGML), the framework uses calibrated kinetic discrepancy to support thermal performance analysis within the present CHC design domain. The resulting first-order thermal performance map organizes 𝑁𝑈=0
 and 𝑁𝑈=1
 as mainly mechanism-led, 𝑁𝑈=2
 as a coupled transition region, and 𝑁𝑈=5 as more strongly flow/structure-led; response matrices, threshold sweeps, indicator ablations, and weight perturbations constrain this ordering. Prediction tests show improved sparse-sample data efficiency: across the Gradient Boosting Regressor 𝑇𝑤 learning curve, PGML reduces the mean absolute error from 27.51 K to 12.57 K on average. Shapley additive explanations further show that kinetic anchors are major inputs within the learned temperature and conversion residual corrections In a fixed CFD-valued candidate set, PGML gives a compact predicted Pareto subset, lowers highlighted-candidate 𝑇𝑤 and 𝑋 prediction errors relative to Direct machine learning, and quantifies the thermal gain together with the pressure-drop cost. Experimental temperature data indicate that calibrated kinetic anchoring provides a useful sparse-data reference for temperature assessment. Overall, the framework provides a data-efficient and physically interpretable route for analyzing compact hydrogen combustion reactors and supporting early-stage thermal design decisions.

records.title: A reduced-input physics-informed machine learning framework for cross-room indoor temperature prediction using short-term thermal-state calibration
records.verified_abstract: Reliable indoor-temperature forecasts in free-running dwellings are needed for residential overheating assessment, but detailed physics-based models require construction information that is rarely available, whereas data-driven models may transfer poorly across thermally heterogeneous rooms. This study develops a reduced-input physics-informed machine-learning (PIML) framework that combines a simplified transient heat balance with Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). An initial target-room record is used to identify effective indoor thermal capacity (ITC) and initialize residual heat load (RHL); after calibration, RHL is forecast hourly from weather, time, and available building attributes. The framework was evaluated using approximately 40 days of field measurements from nine non-air-conditioned apartment rooms under leave-one-room-out validation, without subsequent indoor-temperature feedback. Calibration windows of 0, 24, 48, and 72 h were compared. With a 48-h calibration window, the PIML framework reduced mean room-level RMSE from 0.74 to 0.61 °C relative to bias-corrected XGBoost (17.8%; all nine rooms) and reduced daily-maximum-temperature MAE from 0.90 °C to 0.62 °C (30.3%; eight rooms). Extending calibration to 72 h produced no further improvement. Dynamic RHL and effective ITC together accounted for approximately 19% of mean absolute SHAP attribution. These results indicate that short target-room calibration combined with dynamic physics-informed thermal states can improve cross-room prediction beyond a fixed mean-bias correction and provide a data-efficient basis for dwelling-scale overheating assessment without detailed building blueprints.

records.title: Extracting technical problems from patent texts to support innovation: Integrating human intelligence with machine learning for electric vehicle battery technologies
records.verified_abstract: Technological advancements are accelerating at an unprecedented rate, making it imperative for companies to maintain their own competitiveness by rapidly developing an understanding of evolving innovation trends. Patents, as rich sources of technological knowledge, contain not only solutions but also valuable information on the technical problems that drive innovation. However, extracting and structuring such problem-oriented information is challenging due to the vast and complex characteristics of patent texts. This study highlights the significance of systematically identifying and analyzing technical problems in patent texts to enhance innovation intelligence. By integrating expert knowledge with machine learning, we propose a methodology to extract and categorize technical problems in such texts, thus enabling the construction of a structured database. The proposed approach was applied to the field of electric vehicle battery technologies. We demonstrate its effectiveness identifying cross-sectoral solutions and discovering potential collaboration partners. The findings underscore the importance of systematically structuring technical problem data to enhance technology intelligence, support R&D decision-making, and facilitate strategic planning. Thus, the proposed methodology can be a valuable tool for supporting innovation.

records.title: The effects of generative AI usage on employee innovation: Collaboration modes, idea journey, and decline in creative psychological ownership
records.verified_abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is increasingly used by employees to support creative idea generation, yet less is known about its psychological consequences for employees’ subsequent willingness to remain engaged with those ideas. Drawing on psychological ownership theory, we examine whether GAI usage is associated with lower creative psychological ownership (CPO)—the extent to which employees perceive creative ideas as “theirs”—and, in turn, weaker intentions to elaborate, champion, and implement those ideas. We further propose that this relationship varies across human–GAI collaboration modes, with the negative relationship between GAI usage and CPO being more pronounced under GAI-centric collaboration than under human-centric or symbiotic collaboration. Across two scenario-based experiments (Studies 1–2), two task-based studies involving actual GAI interaction (Studies 3–4), and a multi-wave field study (Study 5), the findings provide converging, although not uniform, evidence for the proposed relationships. A mini meta-analysis further indicates an overall negative association between GAI usage and CPO and positive associations between CPO and downstream innovation-related intentions. Overall, the findings identify a potential psychological cost of GAI-assisted idea generation. They also show how collaboration modes may shape employees’ perceived ownership of ideas and their intentions to continue developing and advancing them.

records.title: Autonomous alloy composition optimization using molecular dynamics guided by a large language model
records.verified_abstract: We present an autonomous materials discovery framework that couples a large language model (LLM) with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to optimize Fe–Cr–Mn alloy compositions for tensile strength. Starting from six distinct compositions, the LLM operated as an intelligent agent, iteratively proposing changes based on prior simulation results and constraints. Over 50 iterations per case, the LLM adaptively explored the composition space, identifying high-strength regions, not easily accessible by conventional methods. The highest strength, 18.7 GPa, was achieved with Fe71Cr25Mn4 composition, identified from a Fe75Cr20Mn5 starting point. The LLM autonomously adjusted its strategy in real time, demonstrating closed-loop decision-making using commodity hardware. This approach showcases the potential of LLMs as scientific co-pilots, capable of accelerating materials discovery and generalizable to other domains like biology and drug design.

records.title: Predicting time-dependent demagnetization behavior of permanent magnetic materials by a physics-informed neural network-based strategy
records.verified_abstract: Based on physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), this work proposed a prediction strategy for the time-dependent demagnetization of SmCo magnets to address challenges in evaluating their stability and lifespan in complex and extreme environments. The PINN model was trained to predict the demagnetization rate and was integrated with numerical simulations to forecast time-dependent demagnetization behavior. Experimental validation demonstrated that this strategy effectively predicted both short-term and long-term demagnetization behavior of permanent magnets in high-temperature environments. Furthermore, it enabled predictions of demagnetization during temperature increasing and cycling in real time scale, offering greater accuracy compared to traditional M-H loop-based methods. This work is promising for various types of permanent magnets and is expected to significantly reduce the verification cost for permanent magnet devices, providing new insights and approaches for evaluating the lifespan of permanent magnet materials.

records.title: Data-Driven thermodynamic model optimization and uncertainty quantification via physics-informed machine learning and bootstrap ensembles
records.verified_abstract: Parameter assessment for thermodynamic models is a bottleneck, especially for inequality-based data from high-throughput methods. Existing Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) approaches are computationally demanding and can be biased. We present an integrated, data-driven framework that automates and accelerates parameter optimization and uncertainty quantification (UQ). The methodology combines three innovations: (1) a physics-informed machine learning (PIML) module to convert low-information single-point data into high-value equality constraints; (2) an efficient parameter-solving module using a deterministic weighted least squares (WLS) solver enabled by model linearization; and (3) a robust parametric bootstrap committee model to propagate uncertainty without linear approximations. This automated, closed-loop workflow refines parameters to self-consistency. A case study on the Fe–Co–Ni system validates the framework, demonstrating rapid convergence and superior topological accuracy. The framework produces physically consistent models and credible intervals, guiding future experiments and accelerating materials discovery.

records.title: Accuracy and Uncertainty Quantification of Phase Diagrams Calculated from Universal Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
records.verified_abstract: State-of-the-art universal machine learning interatomic potentials (UMLIPs) provide accurate surrogate potential energy surfaces based on density functional theory (DFT) data and enable rapid and efficient calculations of phase diagrams and the prediction of thermodynamic stability. In this work, we evaluate the performance of the most recent UMLIPs for phase diagram prediction in different representative binary systems and compare them with phase diagrams from both DFT calculations and experimental assessments. While DFT results are more robust, we show that the best-performing UMLIPs achieve comparable average accuracy to DFT for phase diagrams in the tested binary systems, as their errors are similar in magnitude. Errors in finite-temperature free energies from MLIP calculations are assessed, and uncertainty quantification is used to evaluate their impact on phase boundaries. We demonstrate that uncertainty quantification can reveal potentially stable phases within MLIP uncertainties, leading to more robust predictions and systematic integration with experimental data.

records.title: Generative AI as a psychological Empowerer: The central role of self-efficacy in developing pre-service teachers’ instructional design skills
records.verified_abstract: Background A core theoretical debate persists regarding whether generative artificial intelligence (GAI) serves as a "psychological empowerer" or a "cognitive substitute" in teacher education. Moving beyond prevailing research that focuses on end products or attitudes, this study investigates the internal psychological mechanisms through which GAI influences professional competency. Methods Grounded in social cognitive theory, a between-subjects experiment (N = 240) was conducted with pre-service teachers, randomly assigned to one of three conditions: a GAI-assisted condition, a search engine-assisted condition, or a no-technology condition. All participants independently designed a 45-min technology-enhanced lesson plan within their major discipline. Results Key findings show the GAI group had significantly higher instructional design self-efficacy, lower cognitive load, and superior designs in pedagogical soundness, technology integration, and—most notably—innovativeness. Crucially, mediation analyses identified self-efficacy as the core mechanism (full mediator for pedagogical soundness; partial mediator for technology integration/innovativeness), while cognitive load's mediating role was non-significant.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in soil ecotoxicology: A critical review and perspective on micro/nanoplastic exposure to earthworms
records.verified_abstract: The widespread accumulation of micro/nanoplastics (MNPs) in terrestrial ecosystems poses an increasing risk to soil fauna and their mediated ecological functions. However, conventional ecotoxicity assays remain labor-intensive and low-throughput, and their limited phenotypic and molecular resolution can constrain a comprehensive mechanistic understanding. While direct empirical evidence specifically linking artificial intelligence (AI) to MNP-exposed earthworms remains in its initial stages, advanced computational methodologies established in adjacent ecotoxicological domains offer a transferable toolkit to overcome these bottlenecks. In this Review and Perspective, we synthesize the current state and prospective applications of AI in evaluating MNP toxicity in earthworms across four key domains: (1) AI-driven digital image analysis for sub-lethal histological alterations; (2) video tracking to quantify kinematic and behavioral shifts under soil matrix interference; (3) machine learning approaches to decode non-linear dose-response relationships and prioritize omics-associated toxicological pathways; and (4) the emerging assistive role and governance requirements of Large Language Models. Furthermore, we critically appraise domain-specific constraints, explicitly distinguishing empirically demonstrated models from transferred and prospective frameworks, while addressing dataset fragmentation, soil physical opacity, and the interpretability limits of black-box algorithms. Ultimately, we outline a roadmap integrating Explainable AI with standardized, open-access databases to transition terrestrial ecotoxicology toward predictive and mechanistic risk assessment of emerging contaminants.

records.title: Actinobacteria, mycorrhizae, and the biology of soil aggregate stability
records.verified_abstract: Soil macroaggregate stability is an essential component of soil health. Microbes can enhance macroaggregate stability; however, which microorganisms are responsible remains poorly understood. Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) have long been credited as the primary biological stabilizers despite conflicting information. Soil bacteria, particularly Actinobacteria, can also possess mycelial-like, filamentous growth and many bacteria produce substantial extracellular polymeric substances that may enhance soil macroaggregate stability. Using a novel combination of phospholipid fatty acid (PLFA) profiling and the SLAKES application, we evaluated microbial PLFA biomarker composition and macroaggregate stability in pasture soils across Appalachia. Here, we show the best predictors of macroaggregate stability to be Actinobacteria, gram-negative bacteria, and gram-positive bacteria. These findings challenge prevailing scientific narrative and highlight the need to further investigate bacteria as a source of macroaggregate stability in soil.

records.title: Defining early human developmental identity: A curated, cross-platform marker framework
records.verified_abstract: Early human development involves dynamic cell-state transitions, complicating distinction between transient transcriptional changes and stable lineage commitment in human pluripotent stem cell models. To address this challenge, we establish a curated, cross-platform marker framework for pluripotency and early germ-layer identity. Starting from an unbiased RNA-seq discovery set, we validated candidates by qPCR and evaluated the panel across independent bulk RNA-seq and embryonic single-cell and spatial transcriptomic datasets. This yielded 67 validated markers, of which 66 were retained for downstream transcriptomic analyses. Our framework identified early developmental states across heterogeneous datasets and showed lineage-associated enrichment in human and macaque embryonic references despite substantial transcriptional variability. Protein-level concordance was observed for detectable targets in KOLF2.1J proteomic data. To enable broad application, we introduce DeepDiff, a web-based resource integrating the marker framework and enabling automated fate classification. Together, this work provides a transferable framework for assessing early developmental identity across experimental contexts.

records.title: Tracing scientific knowledge flow in patents: An explainable machine learning study of citation types and their temporal dynamics
records.verified_abstract: Patent references to scientific publications provide essential evidence of knowledge flow from science to technology, yet existing studies have rarely examined three citation types (front-page, in-text, and overlapping) or assessed how their knowledge characteristics change over time. Prior research also tends to focus on static comparisons at the level of a limited number of features, overlooking their combined contributions to knowledge flow. This study analyzes 581,684 scientific articles in biochemistry and molecular biology from 2011 to 2020, along with 230,431 patent-paper citation links involving these articles. We integrate the three citation types into a real-versus-virtual citation framework and apply XGBoost combined with SHAP and the Gini-Simpson index to assess feature contributions and their temporal dynamics. Results indicate that paper authority (normalized citation impact) and knowledge relevance (title similarity) are consistently the most influential drivers across all citation types. Front-page citations emphasize knowledge relevance, in-text citations highlight academic prestige, and overlapping citations combine both. From 2011 to 2020, all three types shift from relevance-driven to authority-driven citation behavior, with overlapping citations exhibiting intermediate trajectories. These findings provide new evidence on heterogeneous and evolving science-technology linkages and offer methodological guidance for evaluating knowledge flows in innovation studies.

records.title: Relationship between peer review quality and scientific impact: Insights from LLMs-assessed reviews
records.verified_abstract: The significant rise in scientific publications has made pre-publication peer review crucial for safeguarding research quality and enhancing scientific impact. Yet, correlation between peer review quality, indicative of a rigorous peer review procedure, and the subsequent scientific impact is rarely investigated. Here, this study leverages Google’s large language model (LLM) named Gemini 2.0 Flash along with the few-shot prompt to automatically evaluate peer review quality, and investigate the correlation between the automatically assessed peer review quality (indicated by review scores) and scientific impact (measured by post-publication citations). First, the subsample reliability analysis reveals excellent agreement between review scores evaluated by humans and those generated by Gemini 2.0 Flash, underscoring the potential of LLMs in automatically assessing peer review quality. Then, empirical analysis indicates a positive association between automatically assessed review scores and citations. Specifically, a one-point increase in the review score is associated with an average increase of approximately five citations (coefficient = 5.440, p < 0.01). This positive effect remains robust in several robustness analyses, including transforming citation counts into logarithmic form, excluding papers within the top 1% of citations, and applying a negative binomial regression model. In addition, all analyses remain robust when using the average and “year-normalised” citations as dependent variables, when using first-author information to proxy control variables, and when employing a zero-shot prompt for Gemini 2.0 Flash responses, despite the relatively lower estimated effect. These findings highlight the importance of peer review quality in enhancing the scientific impact and the potential of using LLMs to automatically assess the review quality. Despite the promise, the widespread adoption of LLMs in automatically assessing peer review relevant tasks warrants further investigation.
records.scientific_rationale: 初筛漏筛补录：官网原摘要、Data/Results/Discussion公开片段确认Gemini 2.0 Flash少样本提示按RQI测量eLife生物医学论文评审质量，与人工子样本作一致性检查，再研究评分与发表后三年引文的关联并作稳健性分析。AI实质构造社会科学测量变量，非只讨论LLM影响/未来愿景；回归系数5.440为相关估计而非评审导致引用增加的因果效应。仅调用现成模型，不标预训练/微调，不据医学论文语料误标生命科学；语言校对声明与研究用Gemini分开。

records.title: The hierarchical structure of research teams and its association with performance
records.verified_abstract: With the rapid growth of interdisciplinary collaboration and large-scale scientific teams, modern research increasingly depends on well-structured collaboration networks. As teams expand in both size and complexity, it becomes essential to understand how internal organizational structures, especially hierarchical configurations, are associated with research productivity and scientific impact. Most existing studies investigate team hierarchies using co-authorship teams, typically inferred from author order or contribution statements, but this approach often fails to reflect the long-term, organic collaboration structures that characterize real scientific teams. To address this limitation, community-based research teams are identified from large-scale co-authorship networks in computer science, and their topological structures are modeled using hyperbolic graph neural networks (HGCNs). To capture the latent hierarchical organization within these teams, a novel metric termed Hyperbolic Hierarchical Entropy (HHE) is introduced, which quantifies both the depth and distribution of hierarchical roles based on node embeddings in hyperbolic space. Empirical analysis indicates that hierarchical structure is correlated with team performance. Specifically, early-stage and mid-stage teams tend to exhibit deeper hierarchical structures alongside higher levels of productivity and research quality, whereas long-established teams often show diminishing returns, potentially due to increased structural rigidity. These findings provide a quantitative framework for understanding the role of hierarchical structures in scientific collaboration and offer quantitative reference for optimizing team composition and organizational design across different stages of team development.

records.title: Unveiling thematic evolution and R&D opportunities through knowledge inheritance networks: A case study in telecommunications
records.verified_abstract: Academic papers and patents constitute the dual pillars of scientific and technological advancement, with their citation linkages tracing paths of knowledge inheritance that are crucial for mapping developmental trajectories and forecasting future trends. This study introduces a novel analytical framework based on knowledge inheritance networks that integrate citation-based mapping with computational topic modeling. This integration facilitates the quantification of cross-domain knowledge transfer intensity and the identification of thematic recombination patterns across scientific and technological domains. Applying this framework, we systematically pinpoint key evolutionary pathways to uncover latent R&D opportunities. Empirical validation in the field of telecommunications—a domain marked by intensive citation interactions between science and technology—reveals that science-driven technological evolution exhibits significantly stronger cross-domain knowledge inheritance than purely scientific trajectories. Subfields such as "wireless sensor networks" and "performance and resource optimization" demonstrate particularly robust knowledge integration, achieved through the recombination of foundational scientific principles with emerging technologies. Furthermore, the convergence of materials science with physical modeling, coupled with advances in wireless sensor networks, emerges as a critical driver of technological growth. Methodologically, this research improves knowledge inheritance network analysis by measuring topic-level inheritance strength and embedding topic spatial vectors, thereby boosting the ability to predict R&D opportunities. By clarifying the evolutionary dynamics of cross-field knowledge flows, our analytical method offers empirical insights and strategic guidance for science and technology management.

records.title: Influence of various novelty types on delayed scientific recognition: Insights from citation classics essays
records.verified_abstract: The diffusion of novel ideas in science is frequently constrained by established actors, resulting in delayed recognition of innovative work. However, it remains unclear whether the theoretical, methodological, and results-based novelty of scientific articles, as retrospectively reported by authors, distinctly influences recognition delays and how the compositional characteristics of author teams moderate these effects. Accordingly, this study examines the correlation between different types of ex post commentary-based scientific novelty and recognition delays, while assessing how team size and the average academic age of team members moderate these relationships. Using 2565 Citation Classics articles and their corresponding commentaries, we identify ex post novelty types from author commentaries with large language models and quantify recognition delay through awakening time. The results indicate that theoretical and methodological novelty are associated with longer recognition delays, particularly the theoretical type, whereas results-based novelty is associated with earlier recognition. Importantly, the positive effect of methodological novelty appears to depend on the specific delayed-recognition metric used. Larger teams and those with higher average academic age are associated with expedited recognition, specifically for theoretical and results-based novelty. Subsequent analyses reveal that theoretical novelty typically extends recognition for papers situated at the upper end of the awakening-time distribution, methodological novelty exhibits latency at both ends of the distribution, and results-based novelty consistently accelerates recognition. These findings enhance our understanding of how retrospectively narrated scientific novelty relates to varied recognition among eventually highly cited papers.

records.title: Active or silent? The spiral of silence in social bots
records.verified_abstract: Despite the profound ability of social bots in influencing information dissemination, they may contrarily coincide with online users remaining silent regarding the spiral of silence theory. Therefore, it is essential to explore how social bots are associated with user engagement—specifically, whether their presence corresponds with more active or more restrained user behavior, and which characteristics of bots relate to these patterns. This study collects 35,575 blog posts from Weibo and their 81,586 associated comments about Typhoon Doksuri in 2023 and investigates the association between social bot participation and user engagement through a set of methods, including social bot detection, BERTopic model, sentiment analysis, regression analysis, etc. The findings indicate that threads with higher user engagement tend to have a greater presence of social bots, but silence could still be associated with factors, such as a high level of bot proportion, greater bot–user textual and sentiment similarity, and so on. This study will support governments, enterprises, and social media users in better understanding the mechanism of social bots in information dissemination, with enhanced capabilities in public policy and administration for public awareness, disaster control, public health, and broad social media topics.

records.title: Revealing patterns of strategic knowledge evolution with BERTopic: Semantic–temporal trajectories via transparent adjacent-year linking in strategic management
records.verified_abstract: Strategic management research is theoretically plural and continuously reconfigures through the appearance, persistence, branching, and merging of ideas. Yet most large-scale mappings rely on citations or bag-of-words topic models, offering limited support for tracking semantic drift and summarizing cross-temporal change as reproducible, event-like patterns. We address this gap with an unsupervised semantic-temporal pipeline that couples BERTopic with adjacent-year Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) matrices, which are used strictly as a transparent linkage rule. Using a PRISMA-screened Web of Science query (search window 1980–2025), we analyze 25,907 English-language journal articles spanning 1984–2025. BERTopic produces 222 fine-grained topics for temporal-network construction; a coherence-screened subset of 33 topics (topic coherence score above 0.8) is used separately for high-confidence Fish-Scale theory mapping. Yearly centroids of the 222 topics are linked across adjacent years, and five descriptive event signatures–Inheritance, Differentiation, Convergence, Emergence, and Extinction-are classified using explicit threshold and configuration criteria. The 222-topic trajectories reveal four eras (IO/Porter → RBV → KBV-DCV → Digital/Ecosystem) and a long-run shift from early topic-population churn toward stronger branching and recombination. This dual-resolution design preserves structural coverage for evolutionary analysis while reserving the most coherent topics for disciplinary interpretation.

records.title: Presentation styles in academic videos: Unveiling their relationships with scholarly impact and research novelty
records.verified_abstract: Academic videos (AcVs) have emerged as a critical medium in multi-modal scholarly communication. Authors’ presentation styles in AcVs, operationalized as multimodal design strategies through temporal allocation, spatial distribution, and presentation speed across modality types and functional structures, provide valuable insights into how scientific knowledge is communicated and disseminated. However, existing studies have primarily focused on static, text-based communication, leaving multi-modal videos largely unexplored. To address this gap, we develop a dedicated analytical framework that applies AI techniques to understand and analyze AcVs. Furthermore, we introduce novel metrics to characterize presentation styles across temporal, visual, and speed dimensions. We also measure scholarly impact using citation-based indicators and assess research novelty using both embedding-based similarity and large language model (LLM) evaluations. Drawing on a dataset comprising 438 papers from ACL 2021 and their corresponding videos, we conduct a systematic analysis of authors’ presentation styles and examine their associations with both scholarly impact and perceived novelty. The results indicate that AcVs prioritize methodological and empirical sections through longer, multi-modally coordinated presentation. Our regression analyses further reveal that structured and balanced delivery is positively associated with higher impact, while visually rich and well-paced presentations, particularly in the method and experiment & conclusion sections, are linked to greater research novelty. This study represents the first attempt to quantitatively analyze presentation styles in AcVs and examine their associations with scholarly impact and novelty.

records.title: Score increases, author–reviewer communication, and subsequent citations in open peer review: Evidence from ICLR
records.verified_abstract: Communication between authors and reviewers in peer review is widely viewed as contributing to manuscript improvement. In computer science, open peer review (OPR) introduces direct exchanges during the rebuttal stage, and upward score revisions are often interpreted as evidence of substantive improvement. Whether such revisions carry the same informational value as scores that were high from the outset, however, remains unclear. Using large-scale review records from a leading AI conference, ICLR, we examine how score improvements relate to subsequent citations and author–reviewer communication. We find that reviewers’ initial scores are positively associated with subsequent citations, while the corresponding estimate for final scores is smaller and less precisely estimated. Papers with score increases receive approximately 16.39% fewer expected citations than papers without score increases at the same final-score level. Further analyses show that score increases are associated with more intensive exchanges; DeBERTa-v3 classification of the messages also links score increases to academic, evaluative, and procedural communication. These findings document conditional associations between score trajectories, communication patterns, and subsequent scholarly uptake in forum-based OPR.

records.title: Revealing country-level disparities in researchers’ transition to artificial intelligence: A two-stage analytical framework
records.verified_abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) has become a general tool for scientific research, researchers’ transition to AI from diverse disciplinary backgrounds reflects the adaptability of national research systems to this transformative technological change. Descriptive comparisons of country-level transition rates can be misleading, as they may reflect differences in the composition of individual researchers rather than systematic contextual influences. This study proposes a two-stage analytical framework to estimate country-level disparities in researchers’ transition to AI under high-dimensional individual heterogeneity. In the first stage, a deep learning model based on publication sequences and collaboration networks estimates each researcher’s transition propensity, capturing the expected likelihood of transition given each researcher’s profile. In the second stage, these estimates are used in a country fixed-effects regression model to estimate residual cross-country disparities among researchers with comparable profiles. Analyzing 1,599,440 researchers across 18 countries, we find substantial disparities in transition to AI that remain after adjustment, with South Korea and Russia at the positive and negative extremes, respectively. The overall pattern is robust across alternative adjustment models but heterogeneous across disciplines. These findings indicate that cross-country differences in transition to AI persist beyond research trajectories or collaboration networks. We provide a composition-adjusted basis for comparing national research systems, informing science policy strategies.
