records.title: Distant but bridgeable: how geographic and cognitive distance jointly shape interdisciplinary knowledge production
records.verified_abstract: We introduce a distance mismatch perspective and examine how geographic and cognitive distance jointly influence interdisciplinarity. Using a large-scale dataset of over 31 million team-authored publications from the OpenAlex database, we measure interdisciplinarity using the Rao–Stirling index based on the disciplinary composition of references. Team cognitive distance is constructed from time-aware author embeddings derived from SPECTER2, while geographic distance is measured using institutional affiliation coordinates. We find that both geographic and cognitive distance are positively associated with interdisciplinarity when considered independently. However, their joint effect reveals a more nuanced pattern. Geographic distance enhances interdisciplinarity only when teams are cognitively diverse. When cognitive distance is low, geographically local teams perform equally well or better. Decomposing interdisciplinarity into variety, balance, and disparity further shows that geographic distance amplifies the breadth and cognitive reach of knowledge integration, but at the cost of reduced balance. These findings demonstrate that the benefits of geographic dispersion are conditional on cognitive structure, highlighting the importance of aligning spatial and intellectual dimensions in scientific collaboration.
records.scientific_rationale: 初筛漏筛补录：官网原摘要明确从SPECTER2生成时间感知作者嵌入，构造团队认知距离，结合机构坐标、参考文献学科Rao–Stirling指标研究超过3100万合作论文中的地理/认知距离与跨学科性关系。AI实际构造社会科学测量变量，不是只讨论距离或地理系统，故标社会科学而非地球科学。模型表示不是思想/能力的直接真值，相关及交互不作地理分散因果增益；未公开具体聚合/训练设置不猜微调或防泄漏保证。

records.title: The role of interdisciplinary funding in supporting impactful interdisciplinary research
records.verified_abstract: Funding interdisciplinary research (IDR) has long been contested. Funders rely on interdisciplinary projects (IDPs) to address complex problems, yet IDPs often face lower funding success and are perceived as riskier. Empirical understanding of how interdisciplinary funding shapes IDR remains limited, leaving it unclear whether interdisciplinary funding designs effectively improve the impact of IDR. We investigate this issue using a unique dataset covering 604,618 projects funded by the world's three largest public funders—NSF, NSFC, and NIH—between 1965 and 2024, and 3,892,779 publications supported by these projects. We train a deep learning model on the scientific text of more than one million publications to capture the semantic signatures of disciplinary knowledge, and use it to identify IDPs, showing that it can reliably infer the disciplinary distribution of funded projects and predict the interdisciplinarity of resulting publications. Our results indicate that, on average, the interdisciplinarity of funded papers is negatively associated with their citation performance. However, it translates into citation gains only when a paper is supported through an IDP—especially IDPs that recombine atypical and more distant disciplines. These associations remain robust after partly addressing selection effects; a funded-versus-unfunded comparison further points to a distinct IDP—but not monodisciplinary projects—funding effect. Overall, our findings suggest that IDP funding is closely associated with the scientific impact of IDR, and that funders may be able to use interdisciplinary funding designs to support high-impact IDR. Meanwhile, our findings also highlight that both funders and researchers should attend to the alignment between a project's interdisciplinary strategy and its research practice when making funding and application decisions.
records.scientific_rationale: 初筛漏筛补录：官网原摘要及Identifying interdisciplinary projects片段明确在百万科学文本上训练深度模型，给604618个资助项目分配26个OpenAlex学科概率并识别跨学科项目，再研究3892779篇受资助论文的跨学科性及引文关联。AI是项目知识结构识别的实际工具，不是资助议题中泛提AI。训练模型的架构/预训练来源未见不猜；PSM只部分处理选择效应，不把资助观察关联夸为无偏因果收益，也不把语言校对ChatGPT当研究方法。

records.title: A novel knowledge-entity-grounded scholarly retrieval framework in full-text academic documents
records.verified_abstract: Entity-centric retrieval in full-text scholarly documents remains underdeveloped, despite the growing need for fine-grained access to knowledge embedded within them. Query-relevant knowledge is often concentrated in a limited number of sentences rather than distributed evenly across an entire document. To address this gap, this study develops a Knowledge-Entity-Grounded Scholarly Retrieval Framework comprising Knowledge-Entity-Bearing Evidence Identification and Structure-Guided Relevance Ranking. The framework is evaluated on a primary corpus of 5356 full-text articles from JASIST, IPM, LISR, and ASIST proceedings published between 2010 and 2023. The corpus was manually annotated for knowledge entities and rhetorical structure. SciBERT achieves the best performance for evidence identification (F1 = 94.17%), and the knowledge-entity-aware ALBERT-Ranking model improves NDCG@1 and NDCG@10 by 12.54 and 6.38 percentage points over BM25. External validation on 957 Journal of Informetrics articles published between 2010 and 2020 confirms that the framework transfers effectively to unseen literature. The results indicate that grounding relevance ranking in knowledge-entity-bearing evidence and rhetorical structure can improve full-text scholarly retrieval.
records.scientific_rationale: 初筛漏筛补录：官网原摘要及Methods/Discussion片段确认用SciBERT识别科学全文中承载知识实体的句子证据，再由知识实体/修辞结构指导ALBERT排序；5356篇信息科学全文人工标注实体及结构，另957篇JoI作外部语料检查。具体研究任务是科学概念/知识实体的证据定位与提取检索，直接贡献于科学信息组织，不仅拿科研数据演示通用分类性能。F1 94.17%是证据识别而非实体抽取全部环节正确率；NDCG增益12.54/6.38为百分点，外部语料不等于跨所有科学领域验证；未见完整拆分/开放数据许可，不猜泄漏保证、模型训练阶段或PDF。

records.title: The diffusion of artificial intelligence methods in scientific research: growth pattern, disciplinary variation, and task alignment
records.verified_abstract: How AI methods are integrated into scientific research remains poorly understood despite the rapid growth of AI adoption in science. This study provides large-scale empirical documentation of this integration, analyzing 27,636,491 Web of Science publications from 2000 to 2022. Using a task-oriented AI method classification system from Papers with Code, a three-round LLM-based identification pipeline, bibliometric analysis, co-occurrence network analysis, and an entropy-weighted TOPSIS evaluation framework, we identify 361,480 AI application papers spanning 867 distinct methods. Three principal patterns emerge. First, the share of publications employing AI methods almost tripled between 2018 and 2022, with AI present in at least 120 WoS subfields by the end of the period. Second, adoption rates vary by more than an order of magnitude across disciplines (from approximately 9% in Engineering sciences to below 1.5% in the Humanities sciences), a pattern consistent with differences in disciplinary knowledge forms. Third, among application papers referencing multiple AI methods, the study reveals a task-level specialization across a four-stage research lifecycle: interpretable classical methods are associated with early-stage knowledge acquisition and hypothesis construction, while deep learning methods are most prominent at experimental validation, and specialist optimization methods concentrate at result generation and transformation. These findings characterize AI integration as a process of functional stratification, and suggest the pre-2022 methodological ecosystem formed a critical foundation for the emergence of generative AI in science.
records.scientific_rationale: 初筛漏筛补录：官网原摘要及Methodology/Discussion片段明确以三轮LLM识别流程从27636491篇WoS记录抽取AI应用及方法—任务关联，再用网络/计量分析研究361480应用论文、867方法的跨学科扩散及任务分工。AI不仅被研究，还实际完成科学文献信息识别，故符合社会科学/科学信息抽取任务。TOPSIS和共词网络本身不是AI；没有公开具体LLM/配置/误差全表，不猜模型或将识别数当人工全真值，也不把2000—2022观察模式作未来生成式AI因果预测；Claude校对非科学依据。

records.title: Paper with code diffusion on GitHub: Disruption or consolidation?
records.verified_abstract: Papers with code have become increasingly prevalent in disciplines such as computer science, yet the relationship between code diffusion and scientific disruption or consolidation remains insufficiently understood. This study examines 29,900 computer science papers published between 2009 and 2024 that contain GitHub links, employing repository indicators such as Stars, Watching, Forks, Issues, and Pull Requests to capture code diffusion in terms of collection, attention, application intent, discussion, and maintenance. The number of contributors is used to represent the size of the development team. We constructed a citation network to calculate the CD index and assessed the relationships among all variables using logistic regression and interpretable machine learning. The results show that code collection, attention, application intent, and discussion are primarily associated with scientific consolidation. In addition, the negative association between application intent and disruption becomes weaker when code maintenance is taken into account. Contributor counts exhibit only a limited effect on consolidation, operating mainly through team size. Overall, the study highlights the value of incorporating repository-based metrics into research evaluation frameworks, offering a more nuanced understanding of how open-source code relates to the trajectory of scientific progress.
records.scientific_rationale: 初筛漏筛补录：官网原摘要及Results/Discussion片段明确在29900篇附GitHub代码的论文上，除logistic回归外实际使用可解释机器学习，分析Stars/Forks/Issues等扩散指标与CD颠覆/巩固指标关系。AI实质服务科学知识传播这一社会科学研究，不是GitHub工具使用本身。现有片段未给具体模型，故不猜RF/XGBoost/SHAP或训练配置；仓库计数为使用/关注代理，关联/探索性中介不证明代码传播导致巩固或维护的因果机制。

records.title: Compensation or concordance between warmth and competence: Examining social class stereotypes in English and Chinese languages using natural language
records.verified_abstract: The pervasive notion that “the poor are warm but incompetent, and the rich are competent but cold” represents a prevalent social class stereotype. However, different theoretical views and empirical findings exist on this notion, which varies between inter- and intra-class perspectives and across cultures. Against this backdrop, this study employs an innovative research method (Fill-Mask Association Test, FMAT) to examine social class stereotypes in English and Chinese languages from inter- and intra-class perspectives. A total of 12 English and eight Chinese pretrained bidirectional encoder representations from transformers (BERT) models were used to test the research questions. Results found no evidence of ambivalent stereotypes between social classes in either English or Chinese contexts. The rich were perceived as more competent and warmer than the poor, and the Chinese language reflected a more polarized view of warmth and competence across socioeconomic status groups than the English language. Additionally, a within-class stereotype emerged in which the rich were viewed as more competent than warm. These findings shed light on social class stereotypes in real-world textual contexts.
records.scientific_rationale: 初筛漏筛补录：实际以12英语和8中文预训练BERT执行Fill-Mask Association Test研究阶层温暖/能力刻板印象，AI语义表征/探针直接服务社会认知比较。

records.title: Social influence and network structure: How conspiracy theories spread on social media
records.verified_abstract: Political conspiracy theories (CTs) pose serious risks to democratic institutions, social trust, and policymaking. While prior research has examined the psychological, cultural, or network-structural correlates of conspiracy beliefs, the social mechanisms underlying their active transmission within online networks remain insufficiently understood. This study offers empirical application of Rogers’s diffusion of innovations theory to conspiracy theory transmission, providing a dynamic account of how individuals adopt, continue, or discontinue sharing such content. Drawing on nearly 15 million tweets, retweets, replies, and quotations produced or encountered by 98 politically active Polish X (formerly Twitter) accounts over 15 months, we investigate how network exposure shape CT diffusion. Using Bayesian unordered categorical regression and network data, we examined the conditions under which these accounts acted as CT spreaders, non-spreaders, converted spreaders, and converted non-spreaders. The results indicate that the proportion of CT-spreading nodes in an account’s immediate network, rather than their absolute number, is the strongest predictor of CT transmission. Even a small fraction (1–5 %) of conspiracy theorists in one’s network significantly increases the likelihood of spreading such content. Contrary to classic diffusion theories, single-contact ties proved more influential than reinforcement from repeated-contact ties in spreading CT content. This result challenges the conventional wisdom in network diffusion theory, suggesting that even complex contagions like conspiracy sharing may spread via minimal reinforcement under certain conditions.
records.scientific_rationale: 初筛漏筛补录：正式正文2.2使用词嵌入扩展动态阴谋词表，结合人工标注构建CTI测量15百万推文，支撑网络暴露与传播机制研究；下游Bayes回归本身不标AI。

records.title: Professional patterns: Occupation-Specific health behavior profiles
records.verified_abstract: Health behaviors represent a primary determinant of population health and a critical mechanism through which social inequalities become embodied as health disparities. This study examines whether occupation specificity improves the understanding of key health behaviors (smoking, drinking, sleep duration, exercise, and Body Mass Index) beyond traditional sociodemographic measures and identifies distinct health behavioral patterns across specific occupational categories. Using data from the National Health Interview Survey (2004-2018; n = 215,241), we analyzed the five health behaviors among working adults aged 25-64. Results demonstrated that increasingly granular occupational classifications (94 categories) significantly improved model fit across the health behaviors compared to only sociodemographic measures. Latent profile analysis identified four distinct occupational profiles with shared behavioral patterns: Conventional Lifestyle, Creative Intellectual, Higher Calling Service, and Physical Production. Our findings suggest that workplace-based interventions tailored to specific occupations and occupational profiles may more effectively improve health behaviors.
records.scientific_rationale: 初筛漏筛补录：从215241人数据的五类健康行为，实际LPA在94职业上归纳4画像以揭示职业环境共有模式；原文明确由观察数据推断而非预设职业大类，按无监督概率聚类服务社会健康机制研究。

records.title: Kinship structure in contemporary China: Analysis based on covariation in perceived trustworthiness across kinship roles
records.verified_abstract: This study investigates the cultural representation of kinship structure in contemporary China, as an analytical lens for understanding family organization and evaluating how social transformations interact with enduring normative traditions. Using data from the Traditional Culture and Cognitive Pattern Survey (TCCPS), we analyze respondents' trust assessments across 15 family roles to construct a family-role network. We then apply network partitioning algorithms to identify latent kinship clusters and fit exponential random graph models (ERGMs) to investigate the extent to which different principles of relatedness are embedded in this structure. The findings reveal a three-cluster configuration, composed of (1) spouses and children, (2) parents and grandparents, and (3) siblings, cousins, and in-laws. Systematic differences in the reported trust scores across these clusters are consistent with Xiaotong Fei's classic idea of the differential mode of association. Subsequent analyses further demonstrate that this configuration is significantly structured by orientations toward direct kinship and nuclear-family affiliation, instead of conventional patrilineal order or traditional mourning-based classificatory norms. Substantial heterogeneity is observed across demographic and socioeconomic subsamples, indicating that kinship representations remain socially differentiated. Overall, the study provides empirical evidence that kinship boundary work constitutes a central organizing feature of contemporary Chinese family culture, which prioritizes nuclear and direct-kin intimacy over lineage-based principles.
records.scientific_rationale: 初筛漏筛补录：对15亲属角色的信任网络实际用partitioning算法学习三个潜在亲属簇，再以ERGM检验文化边界；核心数据驱动分类而非预设父系/丧服类别。

records.title: Analyzing embodied learning in classroom settings: A human-in-the-loop AI approach for multimodal learning analytics
records.verified_abstract: Background: Embodied learning enhances cognition and metacognition through physical activity, but analyzing students’ behaviors in dynamic classrooms from multimodal data is complex. Human-guided, AI-driven Multimodal Learning Analytics offers promise, yet demands labor-intensive coding. Using coding schemas to fine-tune deep learning for accurate interpretation of learner behaviors remains both challenging and computationally intensive. Aims: Develop a robust human-in-the-loop AI framework to analyze students’ self-regulated learning (SRL) and socially shared regulation of learning (SSRL) in embodied learning environments. The framework integrates multimodal data streams, deep learning algorithms, and a late-fusion Large Language Model (LLM) for deriving SRL and SSRL behaviors. Sample and Methods: A two-month study in a 4th-grade science classroom, focused on two class sessions and four fully consented students. A novel codebook mapped multimodal features to high-level SRL-SSRL behaviors. Our multimodal pipeline combined deep learning algorithms of students’ interactions with an LLM for late fusion to segment and classify behaviors. Learning scientists validated the results using an interactive timeline. Results: The LLM identified 470 segments across 40 min of video from two enactments of the photosynthesis scenario. Enacting (66.4%) and Interacting (15.5%) were most frequent. Human evaluation confirmed accuracy but noted challenges with overlapping behaviors. A case study of two students revealed distinct regulatory strategies across behaviors and durations. Conclusion: Integrating AI with human expertise enhances analysis of SRL and SSRL in embodied learning. Future work will refine behavioral definitions, improve data alignment, expand validation, and deploy the pipeline online to generate enactment summaries that support teachers and students.
records.scientific_rationale: 初筛漏筛补录：多模态深度模型及晚融合LLM实际分段/识别具身科学课堂自我和共同调节行为，四名完全知情学生及两次课堂、470段由科学研究者核验；小样本限制不夸推广。

records.title: The differential impacts of primary mathematics teachers’ multimodal behaviors on student engagement: A deep learning-driven relational matrix network analysis
records.verified_abstract: Background: Mathematics is increasingly important in the AI era, yet student engagement in mathematics classrooms remains low, constraining learning outcomes. Although teacher behavior plays a critical role in shaping engagement, prior research has largely examined isolated behavior types, offering limited insight into the differential and synergistic effects of teachers’ multimodal behaviors within classroom discourse, particularly in the Chinese cultural context. In addition, traditional approaches are often limited by subjectivity and small data scales. Aims: This study proposes an ICAPD_Q framework for student engagement and examines the differential effects of primary mathematics teachers’ multimodal behaviors and their verbal–postural synergistic patterns on student engagement in China. Sample: Data were drawn from 90 classroom video samples collected from primary mathematics classrooms in China. Methods: Deep learning technologies were employed to extract large-scale process data on teachers’ multimodal behaviors and student engagement. A relational matrix network analysis was then conducted to systematically examine the differential impacts of teacher behaviors. Semi-structured teacher interviews were further used to complement and interpret the quantitative findings. Results: While questioning verbal behaviors and adaptive postural behaviors occurred most frequently, directive verbal behaviors and proximal postural behaviors were most effective in enhancing engagement and promoting high-level engagement. Moreover, questioning-proximity and directive-proximity emerged as particularly effective dialogic discourse strategies, representing the most powerful verbal–postural synergistic patterns in the Chinese cultural context. Conclusions: Different types of teacher verbal behaviors, postural behaviors, and their synergistic patterns exerted significantly different effects on student engagement within Chinese mathematics classrooms.
records.scientific_rationale: 初筛漏筛补录：实际深度学习提取90节小学数学课堂教师行为和学生投入度，再用关系矩阵及访谈研究言语-姿态协同机制。

records.title: Utilizing AI and machine learning in vocal training programs: A contemporary approach
records.verified_abstract: Background The integration of machine learning methods into vocal training has emerged as a transformative approach in music education. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly utilized to enhance vocal instruction, offering personalized and adaptive learning experiences. However, the effectiveness of AI-based methods compared to traditional approaches requires further exploration. Aims This study aims to evaluate the impact of AI-driven vocal training programs on the development of key vocal skills, accessibility, adaptability, and personalized learning. The research seeks to determine whether AI-based instruction leads to measurable improvements in vocal performance. Sample The study analyzed a diverse group of vocal students (N = 120) with varying levels of experience. Participants were divided into two groups: one receiving AI-assisted training and the other following traditional vocal instruction methods. Methods A comparative analysis was conducted using quantitative assessments of vocal skill development. Key parameters, including articulation, diction, breath control, and intonation accuracy, were evaluated. AI-based training programs were also assessed for their adaptability and effectiveness using standardized scoring metrics. Results Findings indicate a statistically significant improvement in vocal training outcomes with AI-based methods (p < 0.001). Notable advantages were observed in accessibility (t = 11.18), adaptability (t = 10.51), and personalized learning (t = 9.45). AI training programs received high effectiveness scores (8.7–9.5/10) and adaptability ratings (7.9–9.7/10). However, limitations included reduced live performance interaction (9/10) and challenges in handling emotional nuances (8/10). Conclusions AI-driven vocal training offers significant benefits, enhancing accessibility, skill development, and learning efficiency. Despite some limitations, AI presents a promising tool for modernizing vocal education and accelerating student progress.
records.scientific_rationale: 初筛漏筛补录：120名声乐学生接受AI辅助或常规教学比较，实际AI训练反馈条件检验发音/呼吸/音准等学习效果；不按未给出的具体架构打标签。

records.title: An experimental study on the impact of Generative AI on university students' emotions and performance in creative problem-solving tasks
records.verified_abstract: Background With Generative AI's growing educational applications, its impact on students' emotions and performance in creative problem-solving remains underexplored, particularly regarding metacognition. Methods This quasi-experimental study assigned participants to three groups: Generative AI, internet search engines, and no technology. The comprehensive effects of these tools on emotions and performance in creative problem-solving tasks were compared. Results Shame was negatively correlated with solution novelty. Generative AI reduced anxiety and shame while enhancing correctness and novelty. Metacognitive regulation significantly affected novelty and interacted with AI use. Conclusions The study highlights metacognition's importance in effective Generative AI application for creative problem-solving.
records.scientific_rationale: 初筛漏筛补录：108名大学生的准实验比较生成式AI、搜索引擎与无技术条件，实际干预检验焦虑/羞耻及创造性问题解决、元认知交互；不将结果泛化为AI必然促进长期能力。

records.title: From scaffolding to transfer: The impact of AI-powered support on children’s narrative skills
records.verified_abstract: Background Children's oral narrative skills are foundational to their school readiness. While artificial intelligence (AI) offers new opportunities to enhance early narrative abilities, research on AI-powered narrative support for young children remains limited, especially in Majority World countries. Aims Guided by the Interactive, Constructive, Active, and Passive (ICAP) framework, this training study examined the impact of three AI-powered narrative support conditions on Chinese school-aged children's narrative performance. Sample 180 children (Mage = 78.91 months, SD = 7.05; 97 boys) from North China. Methods Children were randomly assigned to one of three conditions: (1) Passive-Active Retelling, (2) Autonomous Storytelling with AI Feedback, and (3) Iterative Storytelling with AI Feedback. Narrative performance (story structure, story complexity, and internal state terms) was assessed at baseline, scaffolding, and transfer phases. Children's perceived enjoyment and interest were also examined. Results After controlling for baseline performance, age, and interaction duration, children in the Iterative Storytelling condition outperformed those in other conditions on all narrative measures during the scaffolding phase. However, in the transfer phase without continued AI support, no significant condition differences emerged with the same controls. Children in the Iterative condition also reported higher enjoyment and interest. Conclusions Iterative and Autonomous AI support each enhance children's narrative skills during active engagement, with Iterative AI support proving more effective than the other conditions during the scaffolding phase. However, lasting transfer appears to require sufficient practice and interaction time.
records.scientific_rationale: 初筛漏筛补录：180名儿童随机接受三种AI叙事支持条件，检验脚手架阶段与撤去AI后的迁移；迭代反馈改善当前叙事但迁移无显著组差，真实教育认知实验。

records.title: Thinking beyond boundaries: Epistemic curiosity predicting creative problem finding through semantic networks
records.verified_abstract: Objective This study examined how diversive curiosity (DC) and specific curiosity (SC) shape creative problem finding, including fluency, flexibility, originality, semantic network structure, and semantic exploration during question generation. Methods A total of 170 undergraduates completed a 15-min creative problem-finding task by generating scientific questions about space exploration and reported their levels of DC and SC using the Epistemic Curiosity Scale. Responses were scored for fluency, flexibility, and originality. Sentence-BERT embeddings were used to construct semantic networks across four subgroups (high/low DC × high/low SC). Clustering coefficient, average shortest path length, modularity, and small-worldness were analyzed. Dynamic and instantaneous forward flow captured semantic exploration across the sequence of generated questions. Results Participants high in SC showed greater fluency, flexibility, and originality than those low in SC. Semantic network structure reflected the joint influence of DC and SC, with the high-DC/high-SC subgroup showing more clustered, globally integrated, and less compartmentalized networks than the other groups, indicated by higher clustering, shorter path lengths, lower modularity, and stronger small-world characteristics. DC did not significantly predict fluency, flexibility, or originality. However, participants high in DC showed greater dynamic forward flow, indicating broader sequential semantic exploration. Notably, the high-DC/low-SC subgroup showed high initial semantic divergence but little subsequent increase across the sequence. Conclusion SC supports creative problem finding through focused and coherent inquiry, whereas DC promotes broader semantic exploration. The benefits of DC appear strongest when paired with SC, suggesting that effective problem formulation depends on the interplay between gap-driven inquiry and novelty-seeking exploration.
records.scientific_rationale: 初筛漏筛补录：170名大学生的问题生成任务实际使用Sentence-BERT表征构建语义网络与前向语义流，研究不同认识性好奇心的认知机制；图统计是下游，AI角色为语义测量。

records.title: Prompting strategies with generative AI during learning from multiple sources
records.verified_abstract: Background As generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) becomes increasingly incorporated in education, research is needed to understand how students use GenAI while learning from multiple sources. GenAI expands these environments by introducing dynamic, prompt-responsive output alongside more stable materials, yet little is known about the prompting strategies students use in such settings or how those strategies relate to the quality of GenAI-assisted written products. Aims We aimed to identify the prompting strategies students used when interacting with a GenAI tool during an authentic academic multiple source integration task and to examine how those strategies were associated with the quality of students’ GenAI-assisted essays. Sample Participants were 293 undergraduate students in the northeastern United States. Methods Students completed a scenario-based integrative essay task using multiple textbook chapters and ChatGPT-3.5. We analyzed students’ conversation logs qualitatively to develop a coding scheme. We then quantified the frequency of each strategy and used multiple regression analyses to examine whether strategy use predicted four dimensions of integration task performance. Results Writing improvement was the strongest positive predictor across essay-quality dimensions. More specifically, task-based framing, learner-based generation, linguistic refinement, and referencing were linked to higher scores for some dimensions, whereas monitoring was negatively associated with several dimensions. Conclusions The findings suggest that the educational value of GenAI in learning from multiple sources depends not simply on whether students use it, but on how they use it. Prompting strategies appear to be one observable way students strategically engage with GenAI within these environments.
records.scientific_rationale: 初筛漏筛补录：293名学生实际使用ChatGPT-3.5完成多来源整合任务，研究真实人机对话策略与论文质量；非仅既有使用态度问卷，也不把回归本身说成AI。

records.title: Individual differences in the executive functions of perfectionism profiles
records.verified_abstract: Background Previous research has indicated that perfectionism traits demonstrate close associations with EFs, and their association patterns differ among individuals. However, there is a lack of research examining these from the perspective of heterogeneity and examined different aspects of EFs. Aims Based on the heterogeneity of perfectionism, we examined the individual differences of rating-based Executive Functions (EFs) in typical daily life and task-based EFs in optimal situation after performance-feedback. Sample(s) and methods In Study 1, 1230 college students completed self-reported rating scales of perfectionism and rating-based EFs. In Study 2, we manipulated multiple success and failure feedback in the laboratory and then recorded performance of task-based EFs of 196 participants. Results Latent profile analysis identified four distinct perfectionism profiles, named non-perfectionism, concerned-perfectionism, strived-perfectionism, and mixed-perfectionism. And they exhibit individual differences in rating-based EFs. Additionally, results indicated significant individual differences in task-based inhibitory control (IC) and cognitive flexibility (CF), whereas no significant individual differences existed in working memory (WM). Repeated failure feedback enhanced IC of concerned-perfectionists and strived-perfectionists, both repeated success feedback and failure feedback enhanced the CF of four perfectionism profiles. Conclusions These results reveal individual differences in different aspects of EFs across perfectionism profiles, as well as the potential of performance feedback in facilitating EFs.

records.title: Navigating uncertainty: the role of college students' cognitive styles and uncertainty intolerance in learning rate from a Bayesian inference perspective
records.verified_abstract: Background Self-regulated learning (SRL) involves monitoring and controlling cognitive processes, especially in uncertain environments. The Metacognitive and Affective model of Self-Regulated Learning (MASRL) highlights individual differences in SRL, yet the roles of cognitive style and intolerance of uncertainty remain underexplored. Aims This study examined (a) how cognitive styles correspond to learning performance, (b) whether learning rate mediates this relationship, and (c) whether intolerance of uncertainty moderates these effects. Methods Seventy-eight college students completed a probabilistic reward-based learning task after assessing cognitive style and intolerance of uncertainty. The Hierarchical Gaussian Filter (HGF) model estimated trial-by-trial learning rates as an index of monitoring and control. We conducted linear mixed effects analyses to examine the influence of different cognitive style tendencies on learning rate and used a multilevel structural equation model to assess the mediating role of learning rate and the moderating effect of intolerance of uncertainty. Results Learning rate mediated the relationship between cognitive style and performance in college students. The association between rational cognitive style and learning rate depended on intolerance of uncertainty: at low levels of intolerance, higher rationality corresponded to lower learning rate, whereas at higher levels, higher rationality corresponded to higher learning rate, with the relationship strengthening as intolerance increased. Conclusions Findings highlight the nuanced role of intolerance of uncertainty in SRL. While rational thinking supports adaptive learning, its benefits depend on uncertainty tolerance. This study underscores the need to integrate cognitive traits and uncertainty tolerance into SRL models and educational practices.

records.title: Creating and testing adaptive guidance for thermodynamics classroom instruction
records.verified_abstract: Background Adaptive instruction tailors learning to individual students by responding to their evolving ideas. Aims This study uses principles of Knowledge Integration (KI) and cognitive activation to inform the design of adaptive instruction that integrates system-driven and teacher-led activities and examines how students’ conceptual understanding and disciplinary ideas progress during implementation. Participants Two middle school science teachers and 272 students. Method In regular classrooms, students engaged with an adaptive thermodynamics unit. Based on real-time formative assessment scores (T1), students received condition-specific activities featuring three adaptive elements (example response, guiding question, and interactive model), revised their explanations (T2), participated in teacher-led instruction, and revised again (T3). Explanations were automatically scored for the level of knowledge integration and disciplinary ideas at three time points. A pre-post item is used to assess overall learning gains. Learning process data is quantified for additional insight. Results Linear mixed-effects models showed that students with emerging understanding at T1 benefited most from the adaptive activities. Students expressing connected ideas at T1 decreased their knowledge integration level across the revisions of the formative assessment but improved most from pre-to posttest. Analysis of student-generated improvement suggestions revealed that many students identified target domain ideas during the adaptive activity. Conclusions The adaptive design successfully integrated automated and teacher-led instruction and supported the development of condition-specific target ideas. However, students need help to retain, rather than replace, relevant ideas. Future studies should evaluate the design against a non-adaptive control group to determine the added value of adaptivity.

records.title: Global patterns and controls of soil priming effects under carbon and nitrogen additions
records.verified_abstract: The priming effect (PE) refers to changes in soil organic matter (SOM) decomposition following inputs of organic matter or nutrients, yet its magnitude and controls vary widely across substrates, soils, ecosystems, and experimental conditions. Here, we synthesized 1807 observations to compare PE under C-only, N-only, and combined C and N additions, identify the dominant environmental and substrate controls, and predict global PE potential. C-only addition induced a positive PE (+33%), whereas N-only addition showed a weak negative PE (−4.7%). Combined C and N addition induced a PE of +28%, closely approximating the sum of the individual effects and indicating an approximately additive response. Simple and complex substrates showed similar overall PE, whereas organic acids induced the highest PE (+126%) among substrate types, potentially reflecting rapid microbial utilization and destabilization of mineral-associated organic matter. Soil pH was the strongest predictor overall and under C-only and combined C and N additions, whereas substrate C:N ratio ranked second overall. Under N-only addition, soil C:N ratio became the strongest predictor, indicating that dominant controls varied with input type. PE showed a unimodal relationship with soil pH, with the strongest responses under neutral conditions, and was markedly stronger at substrate C:N > 15. These results revealed complementary regulation by broad edaphic conditions and substrate-level stoichiometry. Global spatial prediction revealed widespread positive PE potential, with a mean value of 50%. PE potential was relatively high in polar climates, tundra, deserts, and other cold or arid regions, but lower in wetlands and acidic forests. The mapped PE potential represented the intrinsic sensitivity of SOM decomposition to organic matter or nutrient inputs under incubation conditions, rather than actual field priming. Overall, this synthesis integrated input-specific responses, substrate chemistry, and environmental and stoichiometric controls at the global scale, providing a quantitative framework for assessing SOM vulnerability under global change.

records.title: Energy management of hybrid energy storage system with renewable energy sources for electric vehicles based on green anaconda optimization and multi-resolution sinusoidal neural network
records.verified_abstract: Efficient energy management (EM) in hybrid energy storage systems (HESS) using renewable energy sources (RESs) is critical for optimizing electric vehicles (EVs). However, integrating advanced storage technologies with RESs is costly and can suffer from energy losses during storage and conversion, impacting overall system performance. This paper suggests a novel hybrid approach, combining Green Anaconda Optimization (GAO) and Multiresolution Sinusoidal Neural Network (MSNN), termed GAO-MSNN, to optimize EM for HESS in EVs. GAO ensures efficient energy distribution between HESS components, balancing supply and demand, while MSNN predicts future energy demand and EV charging/discharging profiles based on driving patterns and renewable inputs. The suggested GAO-MSNN is implemented in MATLAB and benchmarked against existing techniques, such as ANN-PSO, COA-CANN, GOA-THDCNN, NBO-QNN, and SCSO-RERNN. Results show that GAO-MSNN achieves a 99 % efficiency and operational cost of 1508 cents, outperforming other methods in terms of both cost-effectiveness and energy optimization, making it an effective solution for sustainable EV EM.

records.title: Synergistic integration of text-to-image generation and deep learning for photovoltaic system inspection
records.verified_abstract: The autonomous photovoltaic (PV) system inspection experiences challenges like data acquisition constraints as well as large and diverse data requirement. Addressing these challenges, this study firstly proposes first-of-its-kind of text-to-image generation method to generate electroluminescence (EL) images of PV modules. Therein, several text-to-image models were trained on text-image pairs data of PV modules collected from accelerated ageing experiments. The stable diffusion v2-based model generates realistic data with multi-defects and diverse representations, and can work on shorter prompt instructions. The study also deals with prompt engineering and understanding the model capabilities to explore the performance in terms of conditioning, biasness, and unrealistic generations. The developed text-to-image model and dataset are openly contributed.

records.title: Degradation prediction of the low-Pt loading proton exchange membrane fuel cell based on spatio-temporal Transformer network
records.verified_abstract: Owing to the high energy density and low pollutant emissions, proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) have emerged as promising solutions for sustainable energy applications. Low-Pt loading proton exchange membrane fuel cells (low-Pt PEMFCs) hold great promise in the field of sustainable energy for reducing the use of precious metals and enhancing cost-efficiency. However, the long-term operational stability of low-Pt PEMFCs remains a major barrier to large-scale commercialization. Accurate prediction of the degradation process is essential for achieving system health management and ensuring operational reliability. Under dynamic operating conditions, the increased nonlinearity and uncertainty in the degradation process of low-Pt PEMFCs make accurate prediction more difficult. To address these issues, a novel Transformer model named Adaptive Cross-Dimensional Transformer (ACD-Transformer) is proposed. The model integrates a Dual Deformation Attention Block (DDAB) and an Adaptive Filtering Block (AFB), effectively extracting spatio-temporal dependencies in time-series data through deformable attention mechanisms and learnable filtering thresholds. To evaluate the effectiveness and generalizability of the proposed model, two degradation tests were designed for low-Pt PEMFCs: Steady-State Conditions (SSC) and Multi-Temperature Region Conditions (MTRC), the latter simulating real-world onboard temperature distributions. The results show that the ACD-Transformer achieves superior performance on low-Pt PEMFCs compared to the baseline models. Compared to the LSTM model, MAE is reduced by 63.64 % and 47.62 % across two datasets. This work contributes to the development of prognostic methodologies, facilitating effective health monitoring and durability enhancement of low-Pt PEMFCs.

records.title: A physically interpretable machine-learning method in efficiently and explicitly exploring predictive thermodynamic models for mixture working fluids
records.verified_abstract: Mixture working fluids are key energy carriers in emerging energy and power systems. The speed of sound and its derived properties underpin thermodynamic analysis and flow-related-component design. However, traditional semi-empirical modeling methods struggle to characterize speed of sound that contains thermodynamic differential relationships, while merely data-driven machine-learning approaches also fall short for mixture properties with diverse physical constraints, causing narrow applicability in current sound-speed mixing models. This work attempts to develop a data-to-function machine-learning method with physical guidance, where mixture-related thermodynamic constraints are embedded into the symbolic regression framework in several aspects, forming a comprehensive model-exploration workflow and visually algebraic statistical mechanism. Taking the ideal mixing rule as a baseline and regularized thermodynamic parameters as algebraic elements, the nonpolar and polar characteristics were described stepwise by the symbolic regression algorithm based on limited experimental data, and a universally predictive mixing model is established for commonly used or highly potential mixture working fluids. The model only relies on basic physical parameters and exhibits a relative root mean square deviation of only 0.3 % in predicting 2552 experimental data points of 17 pairs of mixtures across a wide quasi-gaseous region. Notably, the prediction deviations are reduced by 1∼2 orders of magnitude compared to existing universal mixing models in high-density gaseous regions, indicating significant expansion of the available range. The mathematical robustness, physical significance, and error controllability of the model are quantitatively analyzed, supporting the extrapolation to mixtures or thermodynamic regions beyond the training range and verifying some inaccurate data. Taking the speed of sound as the example, the proposed method reveals the usability of interpretable machine learning in explicit modeling of thermodynamic properties for mixtures, forming a new research perspective that can be applied to other similar properties. The results can provide data and modeling techniques for conveniently characterizing thermodynamic properties for new mixture working fluids, thus supporting reliable thermodynamic analysis in pre-studies of novel thermodynamic cycles.

records.title: Towards carbon neutrality: The effects of artificial intelligence on carbon neutrality technology innovation
records.verified_abstract: As a pivotal technological advancement, artificial intelligence (AI) is witnessing increasing integration into carbon neutrality initiatives. However, there is a lack of research on the potential impact of AI on carbon neutrality technology innovation (CNTI). This paper, for the first time, combines the Large Language Model and patent abstracts to accurately identify CNTI. This study systematically explores how AI impacts enterprises while examining its fundamental mechanisms. The principal conclusions derived from this study are summarized below: firstly, AI significantly promotes the CNTI of enterprises, especially in zero-carbon technologies. Secondly, AI can effectively promote CNTI of enterprises by enhancing knowledge absorption capacity, green innovation quality, and collaborative innovation level. Thirdly, the promoting effect of AI is more effective for technology-intensive industry enterprises, heavy pollution industry enterprises, high market competition enterprises, and low financing-constrained enterprises. Fourthly, an intelligent application has the most significant impact on CNTI. At last, we put forward policy recommendations to leverage AI to achieve the “dual carbon” goal.

records.title: A stochastic cloud-driven clustering sizing method for a hybrid photovoltaic/battery energy system integrated with electric bus charge station: A case study for China
records.verified_abstract: This paper presented a fuzzy multi-objective, cloud-clustering stochastic approach for the optimal sizing of a hybrid photovoltaic, battery storage, and electric bus charging station system that supplies a commercial load in Yangjiang region, China. The proposed multi-objective formulation jointly minimizes project life-span cost and energy supply inadequacy probability and maximizes a socio-technical indicator. In this regard, a multi-objective Improved Newton-Raphson-Based Optimizer was proposed which was driven by Logistic Map chaotic sequence to overcome its premature convergence drawbacks. Three uncertainties involving irradiance, temperature, and load have been considered and modeled using an enhanced Cloud Model which is K-means scenario clustering balanced between representativeness and computational efforts. Three cases were evaluated: Case I (deterministic PV/BESS), Case II (deterministic PV/BESS/EBCS), and Case III representing stochastic PV/BESS/EBCS with the novel CLCSA. This work shows that the incorporation of EBCS improves the techno-economic performance and equity, for example, reducing the cost by 4.78 % and ESIP by 5.22 % and increasing HDI by 2.21 %, while considering the uncertainty can expose more realistic trade-offs, for example, cost increases moderately by 7.36 %, reliability reduces by 11.05 %, and HDI by 3.07 %. CLCSA achieved similar reliability when compared with MCS and scenario-reduced MCS with higher accuracy at remarkably lower runtime. MOINRBO significantly outperformed MONRBO, MOPSO, and MOAOA on Pareto quality metrics such as hypervolume and spacing, confirming its effectiveness. These results confirmed that PV/BESS systems, if integrated with EBCS and sized under the novel CLCSA, offer a practical and scalable pathway to robust planning while considering real-world variability.

records.title: Machine learning-based optimization of an integrated system with an organic Rankine cycle, Kalina cycle, multi-effect desalination, and LNG vaporization
records.verified_abstract: Industrial sectors generate large amounts of gases and waste heat that remain underutilized, limiting opportunities for the recovery of clean energy and resource efficiency. Addressing this challenge is vital for enhancing sustainability, reducing emissions, and enhancing economic performance in energy-intensive industries. This research introduces a new machine learning-based optimization of an integrated multigeneration system that combines an organic Rankine cycle (ORC), Kalina cycle (KC), multi-effect desalination (MED), and liquid natural gas vaporization (LNGV) unit, driven by recovered Coke Oven Gas (COG). The system features advanced thermal integration among subsystems, enabling simultaneous production of electricity, heating, cooling, and freshwater with minimal energy loss. Thermodynamic analyses show high energy and exergy efficiencies of 83.22 % and 38.06 %, correspondingly, and a specific CO2 emission of 0.15 kg/kWh. Also, economic assessment indicates strong feasibility with a net present value of 69.98 M$, a total unit product cost (TUCP) of 8.75 $/GJ, and a short payback period of 0.27 years. The machine learning-driven Ant Lion Optimizer further enhances performance, increasing exergy efficiency to 40.30 %, improving sustainability index to 1.68, and minimizing TUCP to 8.26 $/GJ. On the whole, the proposed framework provides a technically and economically viable pathway for low-carbon, waste-to-energy utilization, offering scalable potential for clean power generation and freshwater co-production in industrial applications.

records.title: Enhanced eco-driving and energy management for heterogeneous hybrid electric vehicles through integrated transfer learning and deep reinforcement learning
records.verified_abstract: Eco-driving and energy management strategy (EMS) significantly influence the real-world performance of hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs). Traditional approaches often optimize eco-driving and energy management strategies separately using layered optimization, which frequently results in suboptimal outcomes. Moreover, transferring eco-driving and energy management strategies between heterogeneous HEVs remains challenging. To address these issues, this paper proposes a collaborative optimization strategy for eco-driving and EMS leveraging transfer learning (TL) and deep reinforcement learning (DRL). The proposed framework not only enhances optimization performance but also improves the generalizability of reinforcement learning methods across different HEV types. Firstly, models of heterogeneous hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) and traffic signalized lights were constructed. Secondly, an eco-driving and energy management agent for fuel cell hybrid electric vehicles (FCHEVs) was constructed through the utilization of the soft actor-critic (SAC) algorithm. Knowledge transfer via TL was then employed to establish the TL-SAC eco-driving and EMS agent for power-split hybrid electric vehicles (PSHEVs). Compared to conventional SAC-based method, the proposed TL-SAC strategy achieved equivalent fuel reductions of 16.10 %, 10.57 %, and 4.76 % under multi-intersection scenarios. Compared with the PMP algorithm, the proposed TL-SAC strategy reduces energy consumption of PSHEV by 11.88 %, 3.73 % and 4.16 % in three generalization testing scenarios respectively, while achieving close travel time and better real-time performance. This study provides a novel and transferable approach to co-optimize eco-driving and EMS, paving the way for broader deployment of diverse HEVs.

records.title: A novel dual-knowledge embedded graph convolutional network method combining knowledge quantification for gas turbine gas path analysis
records.verified_abstract: Data-driven algorithms provide a powerful method for rapid gas path analysis (GPA) of gas turbines. The conventional GPA models based on only sensor data could be improved in the generalization capability. Incorporation of knowledge offers a potential solution to enhance the diagnosis performance of data-driven GPA models. This paper proposes a novel Quantified-Knowledge Guided Graph Convolutional Network (QK-GCN) model to enhance the physical interpretability and generalization. The QK-GCN model embeds dual forms of knowledge: firstly, the graph topology is constructed from the physical relations among 9 gas path sensors, identified through reachability analysis of the thermodynamic equations; secondly, the corresponding edge weights in the graph are assigned by quantifying the relation similarities between sensors via knowledge representation learning technique. The proposed QK-GCN model is developed and verified using the annual field data from a GE 9F-class gas turbine. The proposed model achieves a lower overall error value and a narrower error distribution in all comparative studies. Embedding relation similarity as the GCN edge weight improves the root mean square error by 15.3 % for compressor efficiency degradation (DEC) and 33.5 % for flow rate degradation (DGC). Furthermore, the proposed QK-GCN model maintains strong generalization capability even with a 30 % training data size. The results indicate that the proposed QK-GCN model provides a reliable, generalizable, and interpretable solution for gas turbine GPA. The dual-knowledge method is promising for application to the performance prediction and fault diagnosis of other energy and power systems.

records.title: Dynamic graph convolutional network considering wind speed delay and two-stage transfer learning applied to few-shot wind power prediction
records.verified_abstract: To address the performance degradation of prediction models caused by limited data in newly built wind farms, this study proposes a time-varying physics-constrained "multi-source domain to pseudo to source domain - target domain" two-stage transfer learning framework by revealing the dynamic spatiotemporal coupling mechanism between adjacent wind farms induced by wind direction and speed propagation delays. First, the multi-kernel maximum mean discrepancy (MK-MMD) algorithm is introduced to capture both local features and global distribution similarities between source and target domains, enabling accurate selection of highly relevant source wind farms. Then, by combining geographical locations, wind direction, and wind speed, a bidirectional wind delay criterion is formulated to quantify the time-varying delays between wind farms. Based on this, constructed a wind direction and speed constrained dynamic graph convolutional network (WDSDGCN). WDSDGCN projects historical source domain data onto the target domain coordinates to generate pseudo-source domain samples that are structurally consistent with the target. Finally, a temporal convolutional network (TCN) is pre-trained on the pseudo-source domain and fine-tuned with limited target data. Experimental results on four datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently achieves R2 scores above 91.07 %, showing excellent accuracy and robustness in few-shot wind power prediction.
records.scientific_rationale: 风速传播约束动态图卷积与时序网络两阶段迁移，提高新建风场少样本功率预测。

records.title: Real-time efficient short-term peak load and day-ahead electricity load forecasting system using machine learning approach
records.verified_abstract: Accurate short-term electricity demand forecasting is essential for grid reliability, operational efficiency, and energy resource planning. Traditional models often struggle with the highly non-linear and dynamic nature of load patterns, especially for high-resolution forecasts. To address this challenge, we propose a novel hybrid deep learning framework for forecasting 30-min interval peak electricity demand. The model utilises real-time demand data collected from January 1 to December 31, 2023. The input data undergo zero-mean normalisation and dimensionality reduction using Principal Component Analysis Network (PCANet) to enhance feature relevance. Temporal dependencies are captured via a Deep Walk Gated Recurrent Unit (DWGRU) model, which integrates spatial, temporal, and semantic information through a dynamic attention mechanism. A Hybrid Sampling and Self-Attention Deep Neural Network (HSSA-DNN), optimised using an Improved Moth Flame Optimisation (IMFO) algorithm, further refines the forecasting process. Experimental results demonstrate superior predictive performance, with a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 0.85 %, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 14.3 MW, and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 19.8 MW. The proposed model achieves a day-ahead forecasting accuracy of 99.15 %, significantly outperforming benchmark models such as LSTM, GRU, and standard DNNs by margins of 4.2 %–7.8 % in MAPE. These findings underscore the effectiveness of incorporating advanced feature extraction, temporal modelling, and optimisation techniques for high-precision load forecasting. The model's robust performance supports its potential application in real-time energy management systems and operational planning.
records.scientific_rationale: 循环门控网络及自注意力深度模型从实际电网数据预测半小时峰值和日前负荷。

records.title: A novel configuration for sustainable methanol and power generation from industrial flue gas and renewable energies: AI-enhanced modeling and 4E multi-criteria optimization
records.verified_abstract: This study presents a novel integrated energy system for the sustainable co-production of methanol and power from industrial flue gas and renewable energies, addressing critical research gaps in carbon capture and utilization (CCU) and energy efficiency. The system features a unique polygeneration configuration that integrates cascaded energy recovery (Rankine cycle and ORC) with a diversified renewable energy portfolio (Solar PTC, Wind Turbine, PEMFC) to ensure a resilient and self-sufficient power supply for on-site CCU. A pioneering hybrid AI-thermodynamic and 4E modeling framework was developed, combining first-principle thermodynamic models with six distinct AI algorithms for CO2 capture and methanol synthesis. Evaluation of AI models demonstrated superior predictive capabilities of XGBoost and Ensemble models for methanol production. A comprehensive multi-criteria optimization framework was employed to simultaneously optimize Net Power Output, Methanol Production Rate, Exergy Destruction, Economic Cost, and Environmental Impact. Comparative analysis of MOPSO, NSGA-II, NSGA-III, and MOEA/D algorithms revealed distinct strengths, with MOEA/D excelling in minimizing environmental impact, economic cost, and exergy destruction, while MOPSO maximized net power and methanol production. Economically, the proposed system achieves highly competitive methanol production costs ($0.154/kg) and exceptionally low electricity generation costs ($0.045/kWh), outperforming most existing technologies. Furthermore, the system demonstrates a remarkable overall energy efficiency of 68.10 %, positioning it as a leading solution for sustainable energy conversion and management. This research provides a robust and economically viable pathway towards reducing industrial carbon footprints and advancing renewable energy integration.

records.title: Machine learning-based prediction and optimization of solid oxide electrolysis cells for green hydrogen production using RF, FFNN, and PSO approaches
records.verified_abstract: This study presents an innovative approach to optimizing hydrogen production in solid oxide electrolyzer cells (SOECs) by integrating advanced machine learning (ML) techniques with particle swarm optimization (PSO). A curated dataset of 257 data points, representing key SOEC operational parameters, was utilized to develop and optimize predictive models. Two ML algorithms, random forest (RF) and feed-forward neural network (FFNN), were applied to predict hydrogen production rates. Recursive feature elimination with cross-validation (RFECV) confirmed the relevance of all 15 input variables, including numerical features such as current density, voltage, temperature, pressure, surface area, humidity, volumetric flowrate, electrolyte thickness, volume fractions of (H2, CO2, and H2O), and Ohmic resistance, as well as categorical variables such as cathode electrode type, electrolyte type, and inlet gas composition. The RF model outperformed the FFNN, achieving a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.9561 compared to 0.9081 for the FFNN model. While the RF model's R2 was slightly below the best-reported value in the literature for XGBoost (R2 = 0.9677), it significantly outperformed support vector regression (R2 = 0.8062). To further maximize hydrogen production, PSO was integrated with the RF model to optimize the key input variables. This approach achieved a maximum predicted hydrogen production rate of 1.287 L/(h·cm2), representing a notable improvements over previous benchmarks in the literature under optimal conditions: a temperature of 739.65 °C, current density of 2.70 A/cm2, surface area of 6.40 cm2, an operating cell voltage of 1.30 V, electrolyte thickness of 42.62 μm, humidity of 25.39 %, and volumetric flowrate of 104.13 mL/min. SHapley additive exPlanations (SHAP) provided interpretability by identifying the magnitude and direction of impact for key variables such as current density, flow rate, surface area, and voltage on hydrogen production. The integration of SHAP analysis not only confirmed the importance of features identified by RFECV but also offered deeper insights into the models' decision-making processes. Furthermore, this study underscores the novelty of adopting PSO over traditional genetic algorithms (GA), achieving improved hydrogen production under feasible and realistic operating conditions. These results show that the proposed method can be useful for scaling up SOEC systems and helping to make better decisions in operating green hydrogen technologies. Overall, this approach supports the global move toward clean energy by providing a data-driven pathway to improve hydrogen production in high-temperature electrolysis systems.

records.title: Heat loss identification method for heating building exterior walls based on BO-TCN-LSTM-SA
records.verified_abstract: To address the limitations of current energy monitoring methods for heating buildings—such as strict testing conditions, long cycles, and low efficiency, which hinder accurate characterization of the dynamic thermal behavior of exterior walls—this study proposes a grey-box deep learning model, BO-TCN-LSTM-SA, optimized via Bayesian techniques. The model integrates wall heat transfer mechanisms and correlation analysis, with input variables including indoor and outdoor environmental parameters, wall surface temperatures, meteorological factors, and historical data. A case study on a residential building in Harbin tested four different input configurations. The results showed that the Case 2 input scheme achieved the best balance between identification accuracy and practical applicability, with an average error of 2.21 W/m2 and a relative error of 7.0 %. Compared with the traditional LSTM model, the proposed model reduced RMSE and MAE by 25.0 % and 20.2 %, respectively, and improved R2 by 6.4 %. This method enables efficient and accurate identification of the surface heat flux on heating building envelopes and provides a reliable basis for energy retrofit diagnostics and decisions in cold climate regions.

records.title: Design of low carbon CO2-alternative-water injection processes using a machine-learning-assisted multi-objective optimization protocol
records.verified_abstract: Large-scale CCUS projects can generate considerable CO2 emissions during operational processes. However, very little attention has been paid to the CO2 emissions associated with the injection process itself for field scale CO2 enhanced oil recovery (EOR) projects. A notable contribution of this study is the incorporation of CO2 intensity into multi-objective optimization framework employing a thermodynamic variable exergy. This CO2 emission related metric is considered alongside cumulative oil production, CO2 storage capacity and net present value (NPV) to obtain a comprehensive strategy. A hybrid machine learning model that integrates deep neural networks (DNN) with support vector machine (SVM) is trained as the surrogate to the high-fidelity numerical simulator. Coupling with the NSGA-II optimizer, Pareto optimum set can be structured with non-dominating solutions considering the aforementioned objectives. The proposed optimization workflow is implemented to a benchmark CO2 water alternative gas (WAG) project and investigate the compromise relationships among objectives. A weighted scoring criteria is employed to screen the Pareto optimum set and identify the most practical scenarios. Results show that compared with the original development strategy, the best scoring solution achieves a 37 % increase in cumulative oil production and enhances CO2 storage by 38.4 million metric tonnes. Moreover, average CO2 emissions per kilogram of CO2 injected or per cubic meter of water injected are reduced from 0.053 kg to 0.029 kg achieving a 45 % reduction, with the NPV increased by 47.36 %. The proposed optimization strategy offers a practical solution toward low-carbon and efficient field development.

records.title: AI-driven predictive model for acid sludge formation intensity during oil well stimulation: Integrating laboratory data and SMOTE techniques
records.verified_abstract: Acidizing is a widely employed stimulation technique in petroleum engineering that aims to mitigate near-wellbore formation damage. Nevertheless, inappropriate acid treatment can trigger induced acid sludge and emulsions, further impairing the reservoir. To address this challenge, compatibility tests using several additives are commonly conducted. However, these tests are costly, time-consuming, and associated with safety concerns. This study introduces a data-driven predictive framework that integrates artificial intelligence (AI) with laboratory measurements to optimize test design and reduce experimental requirements. A dataset consisting of 115 observations from thirteen crude oil samples, featured by; oil viscosity, density, SARA fractions (saturates, aromatics, resins, and asphaltenes), hydrochloric acid concentration, concentrations of various additives, and ferric ion concentration, was used to train and evaluate four machine learning classifiers: random forest, support vector machine, multi-layer perceptron, and extreme gradient boosting. The class imbalance in the original dataset was addressed by applying the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) to improve representativeness. Among the tested algorithms, the artificial neural network demonstrated the best predictive performance, achieving 96.4 % accuracy on the training set and 81.4 % on the testing set, with corresponding kappa values of 0.9509 and 0.7462. In addition, sensitivity analysis revealed that the iron-reducer additive (importance weight of 0.23) had the strongest influence on preventing sludge formation, followed by the anti-sludge additive and hydrochloric acid concentration. The originality of this work lies in establishing an AI-assisted complement tool for conventional compatibility testing, offering a reliable, safer, more efficient, and cost-effective decision-making tool for acidizing operations in an oil field.

records.title: Optimal scheduling of low-carbon ethylene production system based on deep reinforcement learning: Considering flexible operation under furnace coking and renewable energy fluctuations
records.verified_abstract: The integration of renewable energy and carbon capture technologies plays a vital role in energy saving and emission reduction of the ethylene industry. However, the joint deployment of various low-carbon technologies introduces significant challenges for the coordinated operation of the overall system. To address this, this study proposes a deep reinforcement learning-based scheduling approach for the low-carbon ethylene production system. High-fidelity models of the cracking furnace and post-combustion carbon capture process are first developed using physics-informed neural network, providing a physically consistent simulation environment for the learning process. Building on this, a coordinated scheduling framework is formulated that considers flexible operation under furnace coking and renewable energy fluctuations. The optimization problem is modeled as a Markov decision process and solved using the proximal policy optimization algorithm. Case study based on a 300 kt/a ethylene plant demonstrates that the proposed method can effectively coordinate the operation of multiple processes, maximizing economic profits while ensuring energy supply and demand balance. Furthermore, an in-depth discussion is conducted to understand the impacts of coking, flexible operation and solution methods on scheduling performance, offering broader insights into the operation strategies of the integrated low-carbon ethylene production system.

records.title: Machine learning-driven optimization of an integrated renewable energy system for power, water, and cooling with CO2 capture
records.verified_abstract: Rising worldwide demands for sustainable freshwater, energy, and cooling are increasingly constrained by the exhaustion of fossil energies, surging greenhouse gas emissions, and intensifying water scarcity. Low-carbon systems can simultaneously provide clean energy and environmental benefits. This study presents a biomass-based hybrid design that produces electricity, cooling, desalinated water, and removes atmospheric CO2 in one structure. The model links biomass gasification, a SOFC (solid oxide fuel cell), a CO2 power unit, a cooling stage, a desalination-unit, and a carbon-capture process for sustainable performance. Its novelty lies in the tightly coupled design that addresses energy, environmental, and resource concerns concurrently, while leveraging machine learning–based surrogate models—Random Forest, Bayesian Gaussian Process Regression, Fine Gaussian Support Vector Machine, and Elastic Net Regression—linked with a hybrid Ant Lion Optimizer (ALO) algorithm for optimization. Thermodynamics have shown that the efficiency for energy is 76.3 % and exergy is 34.3 %. Results also show a capacity to produce net electricity of 113.2 kW, cooling of 214.72 kW, potable water at 23.79 × 106 kg/y, and CO2 at 1.47 × 106 kg/y, showing very good overall performance by the system. Exergoeconomics has confirmed that resources are being utilized efficiently economically and that there is room for improvement primarily in reducing exergy destruction in the major components. The hybrid ALO algorithm improves convergence stability and broadens solution diversity, surpassing conventional optimization methods. This study advances biomass-based energy conversion by establishing a scalable, cost-effective framework for integrated multigeneration, efficient resource use, and tangible gains in energy performance and environmental sustainability.

records.title: GeoMTNet: Multi-Task deep learning for investigating the impact of injection temperature on CO2 storage in saline aquifers
records.verified_abstract: Given the critical importance of geological carbon storage in mitigating climate change, this study examines the influence of injection temperature on solubility and mineral trapping in saline aquifers using thermo-hydro-chemical (THC) simulations with the TOUGH code. To address the high computational cost of traditional simulations, we developed a lightweight deep learning model, GeoMTNet. Its shared encoder and dual-branch design enables unified extraction of global and local features and allows simultaneous prediction of CO2 storage amounts and spatial distribution fields—capabilities beyond those of conventional image-based networks. Using grid and formation properties as inputs, GeoMTNet rapidly predicts solubility and mineral trapping with high accuracy (R2 > 0.99 for amount; R2 > 0.97 and SSIM >0.85 for distribution) and achieves about 30,000 × speedup over traditional simulations. Both simulations and deep learning predictions show that injection temperature strongly affects a near-wellbore zone. Lower temperatures enhance early (<10 years) solubility trapping but inhibit late (>50 years) mineral trapping, whereas higher temperatures inhibit early solubility trapping but markedly promote late mineral trapping. The deep learning model effectively captures and explains the influence of injection temperature on CO2 storage dynamics. At 100 years, both dissolution storage and mineralization storage increase with higher injection temperatures, with mineralization storage exhibiting greater sensitivity. Therefore, higher injection temperatures are recommended in field operations to enhance safe storage amount, defined as the sum of dissolved and mineralized CO2 storage amounts.

records.title: Machine learning and simulated annealing/Moth-flame based prediction-optimization for improving ultrasonication-assisted co-anaerobic digestion
records.verified_abstract: This study investigates a novel, hybrid approach to enhance biomethane production through ultrasonic-assisted anaerobic co-digestion of buffalo dung and food waste. Ultrasonic pretreatment effectively disrupted the complex organic matrix and stimulated hydrolysis, accelerating microbial degradation and increasing volatile fatty acid synthesis. In addition, a model-prediction-optimization framework was developed employing machine learning (ML) approaches of XGBoost and Decision Tree coupled with optimization methods of response surface methodology (RSM), Simulated Annealing (SA), and Moth-Flame Optimization (MFO). As a result, XGBoost showed superior performance with an R2 of 1 and an MSE of 0 during training, while delivering an R2 of 0.832 and an MSE of 6.139 in the model testing phase. Alternatively, RSM could optimize biomethane yield to 69.36 % at 51.52 °C and 60.97 min, while SA was marginally superior with 69.39 % biomethane yield at 51.08 °C and 61.38 min. Furthermore, MFO could achieve 68.81 % at 57.69 °C and 60.8 min, showing marginally lower efficiency but strong consistency across similar control parameters. This validated hybrid approach offers a scalable solution for advancing methane recovery in waste-to-energy systems, bridging experimental work with computational modelling. For next-generation bioenergy systems, this integrated approach offers great progress in integrating process intensification via ultrasonic waves, predictive analytics using ML, and multi-objective metaheuristic optimization.

records.title: Adaptive energy management of electric vehicles via attention-enhanced LSTM networks for load power demand prediction
records.verified_abstract: Existing prediction-based energy management optimization methods struggle to capture characteristics of complex operating conditions like vehicle abrupt acceleration or traffic congestion, and cannot adjust prediction horizons to adapt to varying driving conditions. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel energy management method for hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) based on attention-enhanced long short-term memory (LSTM) and adaptive model predictive control (AMPC). First, an attention-enhanced LSTM is proposed to provide the load power demand prediction, where the self-attention mechanism (SAM) is integrated to improve the prediction accuracy under complex conditions by capturing key time-step features in temporal data. Then, a heuristic algorithm called the sparrow search algorithm (SSA) is introduced to dynamically adjust hyperparameters to improve the generalization capability of the attention-enhanced LSTM. Building on the load power demand prediction, a model predictive control (MPC) strategy with adaptive prediction horizons is further developed by integrating operating condition awareness through vehicle-to-everything (V2X) technology. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed power demand prediction model reduces the root mean square error (RMSE) by 25.9% in comparison with the traditional LSTM. Compared to the energy management method using MPC with the fixed prediction horizon, the proposed power demand prediction model and energy management method with adaptive prediction horizon achieve a 1.4% reduction in operating costs per 100 km.

records.title: Safe and efficient dispatch of integrated electricity-hydrogen systems via robust constrained reinforcement learning with adversarial training
records.verified_abstract: Sustainable, low-carbon solutions to modern energy supplies have been achieved via the application of reinforcement learning (RL) methods to the scheduling of integrated electricity-hydrogen systems (IEHSs) that combine renewable energy sources (RESs) with hydrogen energy systems. However, conventional RL methods remain of limited usefulness in this regard owing to their neglect of the randomness and uncertainty inherent in RES outputs, and, in particular, for their disregard for discrepancies between training and deployment environments. The present work addresses this issue by proposing a robust constrained RL framework that facilitates safe, robust, and efficient policy learning under environmental uncertainties by applying a novel uncertainty set based on an asymmetric coefficient to capture discrepancies between learning and deployment environments. Furthermore, a constraint-aware network is developed to detect constraint violations, and these estimates could be leveraged to bootstrap RL. Finally, a robust proximal policy optimization algorithm is applied for adversarial training, where an agent policy is generated to optimize rewards while an opponent policy simulates worst-case scenarios by maximizing constraint violations. The results of numerical computations demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves zero constraint violations in actual deployment environments, along with an 82.6 % greater reward stability and a convergence rate that is 3.7 times greater than that of existing dispatch algorithms.
