records.title: Cooperative optimization of energy and thermal management in PHEV using a time-correlated Laplacian noise-based reinforcement learning framework
records.verified_abstract: Plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs) are a key force driving the low-carbon energy transition in the 21st century, and their performance is closely tied to the energy management strategy (EMS). However, focusing solely on EMS may cause thermal safety issues in PHEVs. To address this problem, this paper proposes an intelligent control method based on time-correlated Laplacian noise, termed TLP-TD3, for the cooperative optimization of thermal management in PHEV electric drive systems and vehicle energy management. The method innovatively introduces TLP exploration noise, which, by virtue of its time correlation and the peaked, heavy-tailed characteristics of the Laplacian distribution, exhibits superior exploration and regulation capabilities. By innovatively integrating TLP noise with the TD3 reinforcement learning (RL) agent, the exploration of optimal policies is enhanced, achieving cooperative optimization between thermal management and energy management. Experimental results under multiple driving cycles show that TLP-TD3 achieves a converged average reward of −3.11, at least 51.41% higher than other methods. Under two unseen cycles (HWFET and China_City + JN1015), while maintaining state-of-charge (SOC) within 0.6–0.3 and battery/motor temperatures within 40 °C and 85 °C, TLP-TD3 attains low equivalent fuel consumptions (EFCs) of 5.85 L/100 km and 3.43 L/100 km. Compared with baseline ECMS-RULE, it trades modest EFC increases of about 3.21% (China_City + JN1015) and 26.32% (HWFET) for better SOC maintenance and thermal safety, demonstrating good comprehensive performance under constraints. This work offers an efficient and stable RL solution for cooperative thermal-energy management of intelligent PHEVs.
records.scientific_rationale: TD3配时相关拉普拉斯探索噪声学习插混汽车热—能量协同控制，在未见工况兼顾电池电机温度和燃料消耗。

records.title: Multi-objective parameter optimization of a methanol-mediated carbon-closed power system assisted by a neural network prediction model
records.verified_abstract: A novel methanol-mediated carbon-closed power system integrating green methanol synthesis, carbon capture and utilization, and high-efficiency power generation is proposed to address the challenges of renewable energy intermittency and carbon emission reduction. The system couples alkaline electrolysis, methanol synthesis, methanol reforming, gas turbine combined cycle, and carbon capture into a highly integrated energy conversion framework. To efficiently optimize this complex system under strict operating constraints, a novel staged optimization framework combining a neural-network surrogate model with the NSGA-II algorithm is developed. High-efficiency energy utilization is achieved by employing extraction steam for reforming and carbon capture, facilitating a carbon-closed cycle by recycling captured CO2 for methanol synthesis. During the methanol synthesis system optimization phase, the NSGA-II algorithm identified optimal parameters that reduced the unit exergy cost and unit exergy carbon intensity of methanol by 3.5% and 2.01%, respectively, compared to the base case. For the methanol utilization system, a neural network surrogate model was introduced to achieve effective prediction of turbine inlet temperature and flue gas temperature constraints. This approach, validated against simulated values, eliminated over 90% of invalid operating cases and significantly accelerated the search process. Optimization results reveal that the unit exergy cost and unit exergy carbon intensity of power decreased by 1.4% and 6.2%, respectively. Ultimately, the system efficiency increased to 32.9%, reaching peak operational performance within the defined flue gas temperature constraints. The results demonstrate the feasibility of integrating neural-network-assisted optimization with carbon-closed energy systems and provide a scalable framework for future low-carbon energy system design.
records.scientific_rationale: 神经网络代理预测甲醇碳闭环系统涡轮及烟气温度约束，并与NSGA-II联合降低火用成本和碳强度。

records.title: Artificial intelligence-based optimization of HVAC systems: Advances in thermal comfort, energy efficiency, energy consumption, challenges, and research gaps
records.verified_abstract: As buildings consume roughly a third of all the energy used in the world, improving their energy efficiency and environment-friendliness is essential. Artificial intelligence (AI) methods, especially machine learning and deep learning, have been gradually adopted over the last decade to handle the complexity of built-environment systems. This review summarizes the recent research on AI-driven integrated and holistic frameworks for building management. Functions such as occupancy detection and behavior modeling, energy consumption forecasting and optimization, indoor air quality and thermal comfort assessment, and fault detection and diagnosis must be examined to streamline the management of buildings and address interrelated heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning issues. While studies have evaluated the performance, modeling approaches, and methodological structures of AI-based techniques, identifying viable AI models remains challenging due to the rapid proliferation of algorithms across spatial scales, including system components, urban-level studies, temporal resolutions, and assessment metrics. Because of this methodological diversity, drawing direct comparisons and selecting optimal techniques for specific applications is difficult. Although AI techniques can improve the energy efficiency of buildings, most studies have focused on controlled laboratory settings or simulations, with few post-occupancy evaluations and real-world deployments. Standardized evaluation frameworks and practical guidelines are required to implement AI solutions in operational buildings. Based on the current study, from 2000 to 2026, the application of AI techniques and thermal comfort models has enabled energy saving on average 21.91 and 44.76% and comfort improvement on average between 21.77 and 85.95%. Finally, this paper discusses the challenges faced in the use of AI for energy productivity and comfort improvement and opens main future directions in relation with AI-based HVAC control systems for human comfort and energy-efficiency management.
records.scientific_rationale: 系统综述既有AI暖通负荷、故障、占用及舒适度模型，比较量化性能与部署局限，属于实质研究综合。

records.title: Unveiling multi-scenario land use-carbon nexus: Crested Porcupine Optimizer-enhanced deep learning model with attention mechanisms for predicting carbon emissions
records.verified_abstract: Accurate projection of land-use-related carbon emissions is essential for regional low-carbon planning, particularly in rapidly urbanizing regions where land conversion, energy consumption, and socio-economic development are closely intertwined. This study develops a multi-scenario modelling framework integrating energy-consumption forecasting, deep-learning-based carbon-emission prediction, and land-use simulation. City-specific grey forecasting models are used to project energy consumption associated with building land, whereas emissions from other land-use types are estimated using emission coefficients. A Crested Porcupine Optimizer (CPO)-enhanced CNN-GRU-Attention model integrates land-use, energy-consumption, socio-economic, environmental, and spatial-accessibility variables to represent nonlinear relationships and feature interactions in regional carbon-emission prediction. Opti-LEAS is used to estimate land-expansion probabilities, and a cellular-automata-based CARS module with multiple stochastic seeds simulates land-use changes under natural development, urban development, and ecological protection scenarios. The framework is applied to the Fenwei Plain, China. Most city-level energy-consumption sequences satisfy the suitability requirements of grey forecasting, and city-specific model variants are selected according to validation errors. Under the primary training-testing partition, the proposed model achieves a testing R2 of 0.9574 and outperforms the benchmark models. Across ten repeated random partitions using 70% of the samples for training and 30% for testing, the mean testing R2 was 0.9798 ± 0.0267 and the mean WAPE was 7.31% ± 2.80%, although performance declined under individual partitions. Under the specified literature-informed transition rules, the ecological protection scenario produces the lowest regional net carbon-emission level among the three scenarios by 2030. The framework provides quantitative support for low-carbon land-use planning and regional carbon-mitigation policymaking.
records.scientific_rationale: CNN-GRU-Attention结合土地利用模拟预测汾渭平原多情景碳排放，学习土地、能源及环境因子的非线性关系。

records.title: An autoencoder-integrated extended Long Short-Term Memory model for long-sequence energy consumption prediction across climate zones
records.verified_abstract: Building carbon emissions account for 37% of the global total, with early design decisions locking in approximately 80% of lifecycle energy load. Accurate long-sequence energy prediction across climate zones is therefore critical. However, standard recurrent networks encounter gradient collapse in long sequences, and cross-climate methods lack effective mechanisms for extracting climate-invariant features. This study proposes an autoencoder-integrated extended Long Short-Term Memory (xLSTM_AE), which utilizes xLSTM to mitigate gradient issues and integrates Sinusoidal Position Encoding (SPE) to provide a deterministic temporal reference. An Autoencoder (AE) performs task-integrated nonlinear compression, where the bottleneck is jointly optimized with the prediction objective through end-to-end training. This represents the first systematic application of xLSTM_AE for cross-climate-zone long-sequence building energy prediction, with ablation experiments delineating each component's contribution. Evaluations across five climate zones indicate that xLSTM_AE achieves consistent performance (R2 = 0.97, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) = 3.95, Coefficient of Variation of Root Mean Square Error (CVRMSE) = 14.67%, Normalized Mean Bias Error (NMBE) = −2.88%), outperforming Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), Back Propagation Neural Network (BPNN), and Transformer. Ablation analysis shows the AE bottleneck recovers xLSTM's capability in complex climate zones (R2 from 0.63 to 0.73 to 0.94–0.97), while CVRMSE by load quantile reveals lower calibration error than Principal Component Analysis (PCA) + xLSTM in the high-load regime in three of five cities. Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) shows SPE mitigates positional drift in recursive memory, with structurally divergent representations. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) reveals adaptive heating and cooling mode switching across climate zones, offering retrofit prioritization guidance.
records.scientific_rationale: 自编码器联合xLSTM端到端学习跨气候建筑长序列能耗，消融与SHAP解释冷热响应及高负荷校准。

records.title: An interpretable GRU–Transformer hybrid model for multi-target time-series prediction and thermal management of proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer systems
records.verified_abstract: Renewable-coupled proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) requires short-horizon prediction of coupled electrical and thermal states for proactive temperature regulation. This study develops an interpretable gated recurrent unit (GRU)–Transformer model to predict inlet temperature, outlet temperature, stack voltage, and stack temperature. A zero-dimensional multiphysics model, calibrated against a custom-built 3 kW PEMWE system, generates a 60 h dynamic dataset spanning prescribed ranges of current, heating power, and water flow for training and internal testing. Bidirectional GRU layers extract local transient features, whereas a Transformer encoder captures temporal dependencies within the input window. Target-specific feature weighting and temporal attention provide indicators of feature importance and temporal relevance, respectively. The model achieves a normalized multi-target mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.016 on the model-derived test set and 0.080 against measured dynamic responses. For normalized stack-temperature prediction, the model achieves an MAE of 0.0384 and an R2 of 0.9833, outperforming the evaluated GRU, long short-term memory (LSTM), and Transformer baselines. A separately trained voltage-prediction configuration achieves an MAE of 0.0119 V and an R2 of 0.9837 on a public PEMWE dataset spanning 961 h. The learned attributions recover the dominant thermal and electrochemical dependencies represented in the training data. In the simulated MPC scenario, incorporating attribution-weighted control penalties reduces the peak stack temperature by more than 4 °C relative to the default experimental control settings under a scaled wind-power profile.
records.scientific_rationale: GRU-Transformer学习实测校准电解槽多物理动态，预测温度电压并在实测与公开数据验证，实际支撑MPC热控制。

records.title: Spatiotemporal deep learning for wind turbine blade root load prediction via physics-guided GCN-GRU modelling
records.verified_abstract: Accurate blade-root load estimation is important for structural monitoring of operating wind turbines, but direct load measurements are not routinely available. This study proposes a physics-guided spatiotemporal GCN-GRU framework for one-step-ahead blade-root load prediction using commonly available SCADA variables. Historical wind speed-power curves are used to construct a static graph representing quasi-static operational similarity among turbines, while graph convolution and gated recurrent units capture cross-turbine relational information and temporal dependencies, respectively. With the 1 Hz sampling rate used in this study, the prediction horizon is 1 s. The framework is evaluated using SCADA and measured blade-root load data from five 4 MW turbines in an industrial wind farm. Three turbines are used for model development, whereas two turbines are completely held out for within-farm, same-type cross-turbine evaluation. The proposed model achieves R2 values of 0.98-0.99 on the chronological test segments of the model-development turbines. For the held-out turbines, the average R2 values reach 0.815 for flapwise load prediction and 0.95 for edgewise load prediction. Ablation results further show that graph-based relational aggregation improves prediction performance over a GRU using only turbine-identity information, while the power-curve-based graph provides an interpretable, reproducible, and competitive relational prior. The results support the proposed framework as a near-real-time virtual-sensing approach for blade-root load monitoring.
records.scientific_rationale: GCN-GRU利用风机SCADA与物理功率曲线图预测叶根载荷，在工业风场持出机组验证虚拟结构感知。

records.title: Ultrahigh-heat-flux inclined jet-impingement layered-manifold liquid cooling synergized by machine learning for high energy efficiency
records.verified_abstract: Thermal management presents growing challenges for advanced electronics as the devices become more compact and powerful, which also leads to substantial energy consumption. To this end, we propose an inclined jet-impingement layered-manifold microchannel (IJMC) that delivers ultrahigh heat flux removal with high energy efficiency through a parametric multi-objective optimization framework. Analysis of variance reveals that all four key geometric parameters exert statistically significant impacts on the thermo-hydraulic performance. Specifically, the microchannel width is the most influential factor on thermal performance (57.05%), followed by the jet inlet and outlet widths, while the jet inlet and outlet widths dominate hydraulic performance (43.50% and 36.11%, respectively). Physical mechanism analysis demonstrates that introducing an inclined jet creates a pre-diffusion zone, effectively reducing the friction factor by 12.76%. Through machine learning-assisted multi-objective optimization, three distinct solutions tailored for balanced-priority, thermal-priority, and hydraulic-priority scenarios are derived, achieving COP increments of 1500, 589, and 1898 over the baseline, respectively. The thermal-priority solution is capable of dissipating a maximum heat flux of 1629 W/cm2. Importantly, at a heat flux of 1000 W/cm2 and a 60 °C maximum temperature rise, the thermal-priority solution can exhibit a thermal resistance as low as 0.075 K cm2/W and achieve a COP of up to 19349, enabled by an extremely low pumping power of only 0.47 mW.
records.scientific_rationale: 机器学习辅助多目标优化倾斜冲击液冷微通道，分析几何因子和摩擦换热机制并量化高热流散热及泵功收益。

records.title: Toward deployment-ready Deep Learning for energy-efficient power plants: A critical survey of forecasting, control, and operational gaps
records.verified_abstract: Improving energy efficiency in power plants has become increasingly important due to increasing demand, fluctuating renewable generation, environmental pressures, and grid complexity. However, most Deep Learning studies still focus on accuracy and forecasting metrics and do not clearly demonstrate their relationship with measurable improvements in power plant operational indicators. This study, using a PRISMA-Guided Review Protocol, reviewed studies published between 2019 and May 2026 and selected 41 studies from 512 records for final analysis after Screening, Quality Assessment, and Standardized Data Extraction. The main innovation of the paper is to provide a Problem-Oriented, Deployment-Focused, and Power-Plant-Centered Taxonomy in four axes: Renewable Output Forecasting, Network Energy Coordination, Asset Condition Monitoring, and Cross-Domain Hybrid Efficiency. The results showed that Forecast Savings with 27% and Control Savings with 21% are the dominant research objectives. In comparison, Validation Debt with 25% and Context Lock-In with 23% are the most important barriers to transferring models to the real environment. Also, evidence related to the direct reduction of Fuel Consumption, Heat Rate, Energy Loss, and the increase in Equipment Availability is still limited. Therefore, progress in Model Accuracy has been faster than proving Operational Energy-Efficiency Impact. Future research should focus on Multi-Site Validation, Before–After KPI Assessment, Uncertainty Quantification, Explainable AI, MLOps, Techno-Economic Assessment, and Cybersecurity to develop Deployment-Ready and reliable models.
records.scientific_rationale: PRISMA流程从512记录选41研究，实质比较2019至2026发电厂深度学习预测、监测及控制与部署指标局限。

records.title: A novel multi-agent deep reinforcement learning framework based on scene clustering for dynamic scheduling of integrated energy systems
records.verified_abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy and the unpredictable nature of load demand pose challenges to traditional single-agent reinforcement learning. Therefore, a decentralized learning decentralized execution framework based on deep reinforcement learning is proposed, focusing on an electricity-hydrogen-heat system with electric energy as the central component. Firstly, due to the lack of exploration scenes within a single system, a novel multi-environment multi-agent interaction learning framework is proposed based on the K-means clustering algorithm. By training specialized agents for distinct scenes or environments, this framework partially mitigates the impact of uncertainties on agent decisions. Therefore, a prediction module combining a convolutional neural network and a gated recurrent unit is introduced to forecast environmental features for scheduling periods. This enables the clustering algorithm to match similar environments and corresponding agents based on these features. Subsequently, addressing the issue of goal preference in the multi-objective deep reinforcement learning, an economy-deep deterministic policy gradient model is proposed, which enhances the economic weight of decisions by integrating an economy-guided network into the deep deterministic policy gradient. Finally, the stability and superiority of the proposed method are validated, through comparisons with advanced deep reinforcement learning methods and traditional optimization approaches.
records.scientific_rationale: K-means匹配工况专用智能体、CNN-GRU预测场景及DDPG学习电热氢调度，与实际优化基线比较新能源不确定性处理。

records.title: Predictive modeling of a 100 MJ cascaded packed-bed thermal energy storage system with macro-encapsulated PCMs using XGBoost machine learning: Experimental data integration and performance analysis
records.verified_abstract: Addressing the imbalance in energy supply and demand, particularly for intermittent renewable sources, necessitates efficient thermal energy storage systems. Conventional modeling approaches struggle with the complex, nonlinear interactions within packed-bed thermal energy storage systems utilizing phase change materials. This study tackles this problem by developing advanced XGBoost machine learning models to predict the thermal dynamics of a 100 MJ cascaded packed-bed thermal energy storage system, uniquely trained and validated using comprehensive, real-world experimental data. The models' performance was rigorously assessed using six statistical metrics. The developed models demonstrated high predictive accuracy for the thermal energy storage system's performance. For both charging and discharging processes, predictions for Heat Transfer Fluid Outlet Temperature, Charging Energy, and Discharging Power showed excellent agreement with experimental data. Specifically, Coefficients of Determination were consistently high, between 0.99459 and 0.99979. Furthermore, all predictions consistently achieved an Index of Agreement of 0.99 and very low Margin of Deviation. These results affirm the XGBoost model's accuracy, precision, and reliability in predicting critical operational parameters. This work offers a significant step by validating machine learning performance with comprehensive, industrial-scale experimental data, providing a robust, computationally efficient proxy tool that can support the preliminary design optimization and control strategy development for future high-capacity thermal energy storage solutions.
records.scientific_rationale: 完整原AB明确工业100MJ级相变蓄热实验数据训练/验证多目标XGBoost动态温度/充能/放功代理，AI直接研究储热热过程。

records.title: Thermodynamic analysis and deep learning-based prediction for curved-channel printed circuit heat exchangers with rectangular cross-section
records.verified_abstract: Printed Circuit Heat Exchangers (PCHEs) offer compact structure and high-efficiency heat transfer for advanced energy systems, with liquid working medium enabling low-pressure operation and high reliability. To elucidate the internal flow and heat transfer mechanisms in PCHEs and develop a reliable predictive model for thermodynamic performance, this study systematically evaluates and optimizes serrated and zigzag channels with varying geometric parameters (bending angle and curvature radius) through a comprehensive approach combining experiments, numerical simulation, and deep learning methods. The flow and heat transfer experiment of liquid lead-bismuth eutectic in a rectangular single channel provides a reliable reference for the validation of the numerical model. The thermodynamic performance of Serrated and Zigzag channels (SRPEs and ZZPEs) with bending angle (η) of 15°, 30°, 45° and curvature radius (R) of 0 mm, 5 mm, 10 mm is comprehensively evaluated using numerical methods. When the bending angle is fixed, extending the return length of the SRPEs to form a ZZPEs configuration effectively decreases the internal frictional losses. At a bending angle of 30°, introducing curvature enhances the PEC performance of both SRPEs and ZZPEs compared with the straight configuration; however, further increasing the curvature radius weakens the geometric disturbance, leading to a diminished enhancement at 10.0 mm relative to 5.0 mm. A similar tendency is observed for the SRPEs at 45°, whereas the ZZPEs exhibits the opposite response, with its average ΔPEC rising by approximately 1.2% as the curvature radius increases from 5.0 mm to 10.0 mm. With a nonzero curvature radius, the SRPEs exhibits superior PEC performance by maintaining a favorable balance between effective flow perturbation and reduced frictional loss. At a bending angle of 30°, the ΔPEC of SRPEs ranges from 17.9% to 21.7%, exceeding that of ZZPEs (15.3%–17.0%). At 45°, SRPEs achieves 30.6%–38.7%, compared with 24.8%–26.0% for ZZPEs. These findings highlight the advantage of integrating moderate curvature with serrated periodic disturbances in the structural design of CCPEs. With the support of data augmentation techniques, multiple neural networks are trained using multilayer perceptron (MLP) and convolutional neural network (CNN) methods. The results show that the CNN enhanced with cubic spline interpolation achieves the best predictive performance. Across TPUA, f *, Nu * and PEC, the model attains an average MSE of 0.14, RMSE of 0.29, MAE of 0.18, and R2 of 0.94. Curvature radius, inlet velocity and bending angle are the three most sensitive input parameters. Based on this dataset, a predictive model for SRPEs and ZZPEs thermodynamic parameters is developed, accounting for variations in bending angle and curvature radius.
records.scientific_rationale: 核能换热器液态铅铋实验与仿真训练MLP和CNN，预测弯曲通道传热流阻及热力指标并解释结构影响。

records.title: Intelligent structural optimization of composite mini-channel heat exchangers using reinforcement learning algorithms
records.verified_abstract: Structural optimization of compact heat exchangers involves high-dimensional design spaces where thermal, hydraulic, and structural constraints are tightly coupled. This paper develops a reinforcement learning (RL) framework that couples three tabular algorithms (Sarsa, Q-learning, Dyna-Q) and one deep RL algorithm (Proximal Policy Optimization, PPO) with a physics-informed environment based on segmented LMTD methodology and ASME structural verification, simultaneously optimizing the cross-sectional channel geometries and spatial layouts of a composite mini-channel heat exchanger. The model-based Dyna-Q algorithm reduces the training episodes required for convergence by 75% relative to Sarsa and maintains the lowest post-convergence reward fluctuation. PPO achieves a peak ECO of 329.17 at γ = 0.5, exceeding the genetic algorithm (GA) baseline by 14.4%, but suffers a 32.5% degradation through catastrophic forgetting at γ = 0.9, confirming the robustness advantage of tabular methods in low-dimensional discrete optimization. The RL-optimized design attains a volumetric power density of 223 MW/m3, which is a 32.7% improvement over the GA baseline. This work provides a methodology for intelligent design of mini-channel heat exchangers with application potential in aerospace thermal management systems.
records.scientific_rationale: SARSA、Q-learning、Dyna-Q和PPO嵌入热结构物理约束优化微通道截面及布局，定量比较换热器体积功率与稳定性。

records.title: Deep neural network observer for energy system monitoring with nuclear application
records.verified_abstract: To improve the safety, stability, flexibility and efficiency for the operation of complex energy mix comprising renewables, fossil fuels, nuclear power, storage, and load, it is urgently necessary to develop advanced monitoring methods for anomaly detection. A key challenge in system monitoring is the observation of unmeasurable internal states that indicates system's healthy condition, which is complicated by high nonlinearity and uncertainty. Given the powerful approximationability of neural networks (NNs), it is promising to integrate data-driven NNs with model-based state-observers for enhanced state-observation. To this end, a deep neural network observer (DNNO) is proposed by embedding a deep neural network (DNN) into a Luenberger observer within deterministic framework. The DNNO, essentially a recurrent neural network (RNN), provides globally bounded state-observation and features parameter-free, online learning, and globally bounded convergence. Driven exclusively by the output observation error, the online learning laws guarantee globally asymptotic convergence of the state-observation error to a bounded set, independent of any prior knowledge of system's physical parameters. The effectiveness of the DNNO is validated through its application to a modular high temperature gas-cooled reactor (mHTGR), a representative small modular reactor (SMR). Simulation results in multiple scenarios verify the theoretical findings, confirm the satisfactory performance of the DNNO, and highlight the advantages of its deep structure.
records.scientific_rationale: 深度循环网络嵌入Luenberger观测器在线学习不可测能量状态，以模块化高温气冷堆多场景验证状态估计。

records.title: AI-enabled real-time hybrid model testing of floating wind turbines: An asynchronous aerodynamic load prediction framework validated on a 16 MW TLP turbine
records.verified_abstract: High-fidelity wave-basin testing of floating wind turbines requires real-time reproduction of motion-dependent aerodynamic loads, but existing real-time hybrid model testing (RTHM) systems remain constrained by online aerodynamic-solver blocking and limited multi-axis load actuation. This study proposes an AI-enabled RTHM framework in which an OpenFAST-informed aerodynamic surrogate is embedded as an active numerical substructure and integrated with asynchronous command execution and multi-channel physical loading. A CNN-BiLSTM-Attention surrogate is trained using fully coupled OpenFAST data to predict one-step-ahead rotor thrust Fx and aerodynamic moments Mx, My, and Mz from turbulent wind input, turbine operating states, and real-time six-degree-of-freedom platform-motion feedback. A prediction–cache–release strategy decouples command release from AI inference, load scaling, and command generation, with the measured cache-release latency below 1 ms. The predicted loads are scaled and physically reproduced by a six-rotor aerodynamic loading device in a 1:85 wave-basin test of a 16 MW tension-leg platform floating wind turbine. The AI-predicted loads agree closely with OpenFAST references, with the minimum Q-Q coefficient of determination reaching 0.997. The corresponding measured thrust and moment channels achieve minimum Q-Q coefficients of 0.988 and 0.927, respectively. At the system-response level, the main statistical errors of platform surge, heave, pitch, and upwind center tendon tension remain below 9.6%. The proposed framework establishes a motion-feedback-in-the-loop AI numerical-substructure approach for real-time hybrid testing of the investigated 16 MW TLP floating wind turbine.
records.scientific_rationale: CNN-BiLSTM-Attention学习OpenFAST气动载荷作为实时物理试验主动数值子结构，在16MW张力腿风机缩比水池验证。

records.title: Multi-objective parameter performance optimization of a novel ultrasonic oscillation falling film generator based on machine learning
records.verified_abstract: Ammonia-water absorption refrigeration and heat pump systems are restricted by low thermodynamic coefficient of performance, meanwhile the generator component suffers from unsatisfactory heat and mass transfer efficiency. To solve this bottleneck, this work innovatively introduces ultrasonic oscillation technology into a newly developed falling film generator. A one-dimensional theoretical model is established to characterize ammonia-water falling film desorption under ultrasonic excitation, covering five key operating variables: ultrasonic power, inlet solution concentration and flow rate, hot water inlet temperature, and generation pressure. Multi-parameter coupling impacts on average mass transfer rate and degassing range (Δω) are systematically analyzed. A histogram-based gradient boosting regressor is constructed as an efficient surrogate of the physics-based model for high-dimensional screening and optimization. Accumulated local effects analysis quantifies each parameter's marginal contribution to Δω variation, and a differential evolution algorithm performs multi-variable performance optimization. The results demonstrate that inlet flow rate dominates Δω variation with a 61.66% contribution. The predicted maximum Δω has a relative error of only 3.2% against numerical simulation, and the optimized Δω is 33.3% higher than the conventional generator without ultrasonic reinforcement. Although this study verifies the remarkable performance improvement brought by ultrasonic intensification, it should be noted that these quantitative values are theoretical predictions derived from the first-order acoustic streaming intensification model, without considering the boiling nucleation effect induced by cavitation. Since cavitation phase change can produce additional enhancement effects, the actual intensification performance will be higher. Further experimental verification is required before all these results can be applied to practical engineering scenarios.
records.scientific_rationale: 直方图梯度提升代理超声降膜发生器物理模型，解释流量与传质关系并以差分演化优化，研究明确标注理论预测局限。

records.title: Physics-consistent reinforcement learning for temperature control in delayed thermal energy systems
records.verified_abstract: Delayed flow heat transfer control is challenging because outlet temperature is governed by fluid transport delay, solid heat storage, and hidden wall–fluid thermal states. Under limited measurements, the control task becomes partially observable, making reinforcement learning based only on instantaneous observations prone to delayed actions, excessive overshoot, and closed-loop oscillations. To address this problem, this study proposes a physics-consistent state-augmented reinforcement learning framework for overshoot-suppressed temperature control in delayed thermal energy systems. First, the delayed input–output relationship of the flow-heating process is analyzed to clarify why instantaneous observations are insufficient for policy learning. A fast reduced-order physical model is then developed to predict steady-state thermal–hydraulic features, including outlet temperature, pressure, velocity, and characteristic settling time. To reduce model bias caused by dimensional reduction and uncertain heat-transfer conditions, an ensemble Kalman filter is introduced to update the equivalent heat-source correction parameter online. The corrected physical predictions are incorporated into the policy state, and a PPO-based policy is trained for continuous control using this augmented state representation. At the 80 °C benchmark, the proposed method achieved a maximum temperature overshoot of 0.291±0.201°C across five independently trained seeds, representing an 86.4% reduction relative to Standard PPO. Across the 70, 75, and 80 °C targets, the mean maximum overshoot remained between 0.148 and 0.291 °C, demonstrating repeatable overshoot-suppressed regulation at the tested setpoints. These results show that online-corrected physical state augmentation improves reinforcement-learning state representation and provides a control reference for delayed thermal energy systems.
records.scientific_rationale: 物理降阶预测与在线滤波扩增PPO状态，解决热输运时滞与隐藏热状态，并用多种温度目标和随机种子验证超调抑制。

records.title: Comprehensive solvent evaluation for post-combustion carbon capture in cement decarbonization: 4E analysis, machine learning, life cycle assessment and sensitivity analysis
records.verified_abstract: Global warming and climate change have intensified the need for effective carbon mitigation strategies to achieve net-zero emissions. The cement industry is among the largest industrial sources of CO2 emissions, making post-combustion carbon capture (PCC) a key technology for decarbonization. However, the performance of PCC systems strongly depends on solvent selection.This study provides a comprehensive multi-criteria evaluation of commercial amine-based solvents, including monoethanolamine (MEA), diethanolamine (DEA), diglycolamine (DGA), methyldiethanolamine (MDEA), piperazine (PZ), triethanolamine (TEA), and other blends. Steady-state simulations were combined with an integrated 4E framework (energy, exergy, exergoeconomic, and exergoenvironmental analyses), together with life cycle assessment and sensitivity analysis, to evaluate thermodynamic, economic, and environmental performance. In addition, machine learning models, including K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Decision Tree, Random Forest, Artificial Neural Network, Support Vector Classifier (SVC), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), were optimized using GridSearchCV for predictive solvent classification.The results show that no single solvent is optimal across all evaluation criteria. DGA performs best in terms of energy consumption, exergy destruction, exergoeconomic performance, economic cost, life cycle assessment, and sensitivity analysis. MDEA achieves the highest exergy efficiency (60.5%), while Disopropanolamine exhibits the lowest environmental impact. From a data-driven perspective, the Random Forest model achieved the highest predictive performance, with an Area Under Curve (AUC) of 0.94, and identified TEA as the optimal solvent. Overall, the proposed integrated thermodynamic and machine learning framework provides a robust decision-support tool for sustainable solvent selection and supports the broader decarbonization of the cement industry.
records.scientific_rationale: 随机森林等六类模型以GridSearchCV优化碳捕集溶剂分类，结合4E、生命周期及敏感性分析比较胺溶剂；完整原摘要转录的RF AUC0.94和TEA结论与官网Highlights独立匹配。

records.title: Intelligent setpoint decision-making for PWR automatic startup based on multi-agent deep reinforcement learning
records.verified_abstract: The automatic startup of a pressurized water reactor exhibits strong coupling, wide-range transients, and stringent safety constraints. Existing setpoint decision-making methods typically treat each control loop independently and rely on fixed offline trajectories, leaving inter-loop couplings unaddressed and lacking adaptability to real-time disturbances. Consequently, even with well-tuned bottom-layer controllers, the startup performance remains constrained by oscillations and potential safety violations. To overcome these limitations without modifying existing safety-certified controllers, this study proposes a non-intrusive deep reinforcement learning strategy for intelligent setpoint decision-making. A two-stage “offline training – online decision-making” architecture integrates an intelligent module above the existing automatic startup system. Three independent deep deterministic policy gradient agents are developed for pressure, temperature, and water level control, each with a low-dimensional state space and incremental actions. An indirect multi-agent coordination mechanism based on shared environmental feedback enables emergent inter-agent collaboration. Simulation verification on a high-fidelity Hua-long pressurized water reactor simulation platform demonstrates robust single-agent generalization, active disturbance rejection, and effective multi-agent coordination under load transients. Compared with conventional fixed setpoints, the multi-agent intelligent setpoints reduce the integral of time-weighted squared error by 95.0%, 27.3%, and 78.5% for pressure, temperature, and water level, respectively. These results confirm that the proposed strategy achieves adaptive, disturbance-rejecting, and coordinated automatic startup.
records.scientific_rationale: 三个DDPG智能体以共享反馈协调压水堆启动压力、温度及水位设定，在华龙高保真模拟器验证扰动抑制与安全。

records.title: Predicting energy efficiency and carbon footprint in livestock farms using artificial neural networks: A case study in Turkey
records.verified_abstract: On dairy farms, the increasing number of operational processes over time, along with rising energy costs and environmental issues, has made managing energy and its carbon footprint (CF) a necessity for farm sustainability. Thus, energy efficiency and energy-related CF were calculated for 93 dairy cattle farms in Türkiye, with capacities ranging from 1 to 225 heads, using conventional production methods and semi-open free-stall systems. Within the scope of the study, average energy consumption and output amounts, as well as energy efficiencies were determined using six parameters (feed, electricity, labor, machinery, young dairy cattle, fuel) and three output parameters (manure, milk, meat) obtained from field studies conducted on 93 farms. Additionally, average CF calculations based on energy sources have been carried out using the directly consumed energy inputs (electricity, fuel) and the inputs that drive energy consumption in production processes (feed and manure) for all farms. Finally, the energy efficiency and CF amounts for these farms were predicted using an artificial neural network (ANN). The average energy consumption of all farms was determined to be 78737.94 MJ/LSU. The average energy output from the farms was 13082.23 MJ/LSU. Accordingly, only 17% of the energy consumed in farms can be met. The average CF per liter of milk was 0.558 kg CO2-eq. On farms, the highest energy-related CO2-eq was fuel, while the lowest was manure. Using ANN, energy efficiency and energy-related CF have been successfully predicted, with R2 scores over 90% and low error rates. This will inform farms by providing a practical decision-support tool.
records.scientific_rationale: ANN学习93座土耳其奶牛场实地能量投入产出及碳足迹，预测能源效率和奶产相关环境影响，实际农业环境研究明确。

records.title: Hot helium temperature optimization in modular high-temperature gas-cooled reactors using supervisory LSTM-MPC
records.verified_abstract: Flexible operation of modular high-temperature gas-cooled reactors (MHTGRs) requires effective regulation of the delayed and oscillatory hot helium temperature during load changes. This study develops a supervisory long short-term memory-based model predictive control (LSTM-MPC) strategy that reshapes the thermal power setpoint online while retaining the existing coordinated control system. A unified closed-loop LSTM surrogate was trained using data collected within 50%–75% rated full power (RFP) and applied without retraining to bidirectional transients extending to 100% RFP. The model predicts the hot helium temperature increment and is embedded in a differentiable receding-horizon optimizer to generate bounded setpoint compensation. Hard constraints, control penalties, and baseline fallback limit the supervisory authority and preserve plant-side stabilization and actuator coordination. The strategy was implemented through Open Platform Communications Unified Architecture (OPC UA) on an MHTGR engineering simulator and evaluated under two load-reduction scenarios and one power-increase scenario, with baseline coordinated control and dynamic matrix control used as benchmarks. LSTM-MPC improved all evaluated temperature-response indices and representative extrema, with integral of squared error reductions of 40.9%–64.3% relative to the baseline. These results demonstrate that data-driven predictive setpoint reshaping can improve MHTGR load-changing performance through a bounded and non-intrusive supervisory implementation.
records.scientific_rationale: LSTM代理在线重塑高温气冷堆热功率设定，以OPC-UA工程模拟器验证跨额定功率热氦温控及非侵入安全约束。

records.title: Strategic day-ahead bidding for hydropower producers under heterogeneous competitor behavior: A clustering-based boundedly rational behavioral modeling and bilevel optimization framework
records.verified_abstract: In day-ahead electricity markets, hydropower producers face the challenge of optimizing bids while anticipating the reactions of heterogeneous, boundedly rational competitors. This study proposes an integrated framework combining data-driven competitor typology identification, behavioral modeling, and bilevel optimization. First, a multi-view spectral clustering approach fuses statistical features and dynamic time warping-based temporal patterns to identify representative competitor types from historical data. Second, an improved Barberis–Shleifer–Vishny (BSV) model is developed, incorporating a psychological confidence index, a diurnal seasonal anchor, and a shock overreaction mechanism to predict each competitor's boundedly rational bidding adjustments in a self-feeding multi-step manner. Third, these behavioral predictions are embedded into the lower-level market clearing of a bilevel model, where the upper level maximizes the hydropower producer's profit under hydraulic constraints. Validated with real data from the Hubei electricity market, the improved BSV model achieves R2 above 0.94 and MAPE below 5% over a 24-h horizon. The resulting bidding strategy yields profit improvements of 7.5%–18.1% over traditional BSV, game-theoretic, and greedy benchmarks, with independent validation discrepancies below 1%. The framework demonstrates that explicitly modeling heterogeneous bounded rationality significantly enhances hydropower bidding performance.
records.scientific_rationale: 谱聚类学习真实电力市场竞争者类型并与行为模型、水力约束竞价优化耦合，分析异质有限理性对水电市场行为的作用。

records.title: A scalable BIM-machine learning-evolutionary framework for multi-objective building performance optimization
records.verified_abstract: In sustainable design, optimizing building performance to simultaneously achieve energy efficiency, low environmental impact, and indoor comfort remains a significant challenge, mainly due to the complexity of the calculations involved in simulating and optimizing numerous design parameters. Although traditional methods mainly rely on physical simulations or simplified models, they often have limitations in terms of computational efficiency, the ability to optimize high-dimensional objectives, and the predictive accuracy in resolving the complex nonlinear relationships between building parameters and performance indicators. This study proposes a comprehensive framework that systematically integrates three key technologies: Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) for hyperparameter adjustment, Machine Learning (ML) for performance prediction, and Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm (NSGA)-III for multi-objective optimization. First, orthogonal experiments are conducted using the Building Information Model (BIM) with DesignBuilder (DB), and a comprehensive sample dataset is generated. Secondly, the particle swarm optimization algorithm is used to optimize the hyperparameters of four machine learning models (including Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), and Support Vector Machine (SVM)), thereby establishing an accurate prediction model. Finally, the optimal model obtained is used to construct the fitness function of NSGA-III and to obtain the Pareto optimal solution. A study was conducted using an office building in Wuhan. The results show that: (1) Compared with PSO-GBDT, PSO-ANN, and PSO-SVM, the PSO-RF model has prediction R2 values of 0.999, 0.998, and 0.957 respectively for energy consumption, carbon emissions, and thermal comfort. (2) The optimization results are remarkable, with life-cycle energy consumption and carbon emissions reduced by 23.49% and 5.58%, and thermal comfort (PMV) approaching a neutral state. (3) Parameter importance analysis indicates that the cooling setpoint temperature and building airtightness are the primary factors affecting the design. Our study provides a robust and intelligent framework that enables designers and policymakers to make informed decisions toward the development of high-performance sustainable buildings.

records.title: Real-time adaptive energy management with acceleration-consistency-regularized trend-enhanced transformer-based speed prediction for hybrid electric amphibious vehicles
records.verified_abstract: Hybrid electric amphibious vehicles (HEAVs) are characterized by highly dynamic speed profiles and speed-dependent transient load variations, posing challenges to fuel economy, SOC regulation, and powertrain stability. To address these issues, this paper proposes a real-time adaptive energy management framework integrating an acceleration-consistency-regularized Trend-Enhanced Transformer (TE-Transformer) with a prediction-guided load-splitting adaptive equivalent consumption minimization strategy (PLS-AECMS). Firstly, a stop-constrained method is developed to segment a 10314s real-world waterborne dataset into low-speed maneuver, mid-speed fluctuation, and high-speed cruise profiles. To capture the evolution characteristics of waterborne speed, the TE-Transformer jointly learns point-wise temporal dependencies and segment-level trends, achieving average MAE, RMSE, and R2 values of 0.1107, 0.1993, and 0.9951 on an EAORA07 controller. Based on the predicted speed sequence, PLS-AECMS assigns baseline load to the engine and transient demand to the battery. Across nine scenarios, it maintains final SOC within 59.19%-59.90%, reduces total SOC-corrected fuel consumption by 1.27% and 2.93% compared to prediction-based MPC (P-MPC) and AECMS, and decreases the average maximum engine power change rate by 88.26% and 90.18%, respectively. Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) tests further verify the real-time performance and deployment potential of PLS-AECMS, with an average solving time of 15.3 ms and a maximum solving time below 20 ms. Overall, this study provides an effective solution for real-time energy management of HEAVs, and offers valuable insights for hybrid marine propulsion systems.
records.scientific_rationale: Transformer融合速度趋势和加速度一致性学习真实水上行驶数据，驱动混合动力两栖车辆预测能量分配并作硬件在环验证。

records.title: Balancing energy-comfort-carbon trade-offs for traditional Sanheyuan building retrofit: A decision support framework integrating two-stage SHAP analysis and pareto clustering
records.verified_abstract: Traditional Sanheyuan buildings in the Hot Summer and Cold Winter (HSCW) zone face a critical trilemma under heritage conservation constraints: balancing operational energy use intensity (EUI), thermal comfort hours (TCH), and embodied carbon (CE). This study develops a decision support framework integrating two-stage SHAP analysis and Pareto clustering to address this challenge. A validated EnergyPlus model generated 2000 design scenarios. Among seven machine learning models, XGBoost achieved the highest predictive accuracy and was selected as the surrogate model. Global SHAP analysis reveals that active measures dominate EUI (outdoor air flow rate contributes 71.0%), while passive measures dominate CE (wall insulation material and its thickness collectively contribute 62.5%), with TCH exhibiting synergistic active-passive control. The NSGA-III algorithm generated 129 Pareto optimal solutions. Entropy-weighted TOPSIS selected a comprehensive optimal solution from the Pareto front. Local SHAP analysis on this solution identifies cooling setpoint and outdoor air flow rate as key TCH drivers, and material selection as the primary CE reducer. Finally, K-means clustering condensed the 129 Pareto solutions into four retrofit archetypes: energy-prioritized, comfort-oriented, low-carbon balanced, and robust-balanced. Key contributions include the two-stage SHAP interpretation bridging global sensitivity and local attribution, an integrated NSGA-III–TOPSIS–K-means decision pipeline producing actionable archetypes, and quantification of the carbon penalty and energy-comfort trade-off under conservation constraints.
records.scientific_rationale: XGBoost代理三合院能耗、热舒适及隐含碳，SHAP解释并以NSGA-III与K-means形成保护约束下改造方案。

records.title: Thermodynamically consistent feature representation for machine learning-based HHV prediction of municipal solid waste
records.verified_abstract: Higher heating value (HHV) is a key property for evaluating municipal solid waste (MSW) feedstocks in waste-to-energy systems. However, the as-received HHV of MSW reflects the combined effects of combustible composition and physical dilution associated with moisture and ash. This coupling requires a direct machine-learning model to simultaneously fit combustible-composition effects and moisture/ash dilution effects within a single regression mapping, which increases the complexity of the learning task and may reduce the stability and physical interpretability of the fitted relationship. To address this issue, this study developed a thermodynamically consistent feature-representation framework that separates dry ash-free combustible-fraction HHV prediction from physical dilution reconstruction. Three strategies were evaluated under the same modeling and validation protocol: a direct model using as-received elemental composition, moisture, and ash to predict as-received HHV; a partially converted model using dry ash-free elemental composition together with moisture and ash to predict as-received HHV; and a fully converted model using dry ash-free elemental composition to predict dry ash-free HHV, which was then converted back to the as-received basis by multiplying it by the combustible mass fraction calculated from moisture and ash contents. The results show that converting elemental features to a dry ash-free basis alone is insufficient when as-received HHV remains the direct learning target. Among the three evaluated frameworks, the fully basis-converted framework achieved the lowest overall prediction errors for as-received HHV and provided a more stable residual structure for directly learned dry ash-free HHV. Its R2, RMSE, and MAE were 0.9845, 1.202 MJ/kg, and 0.713 MJ/kg for HHVar, respectively, whereas the corresponding values for directly predicted HHVdaf were 0.8970, 2.182 MJ/kg, and 1.375 MJ/kg. It also showed more stable sample-wise error behavior across different moisture and ash dilution levels. However, the improved as-received metrics partly reflect the error-scaling effect introduced by deterministic reconstruction. This framework also provides a clearer physical allocation of model components, in which dry ash-free elemental features are used to represent the combustible fraction, while moisture and ash are introduced through mass-based reconstruction. These findings suggest that thermodynamically consistent basis conversion is an effective representation strategy for improving prediction accuracy, residual stability, and interpretability in the present small and highly heterogeneous MSW dataset.

records.title: Eco-engineered multi-product sustainable energy system by utilization waste-heat recovery from flue-gas and CO2 capture: Integrated 6E analysis and convolutional neural network assisted multi-objective moth-flame optimization
records.verified_abstract: This study proposes an eco-engineered multi-product system that utilizes post-combustion flue-gas streams from cement kilns as a primary thermal resource to improve energy recovery and reduce environmental impacts. To maximize the utilization of high- and medium-grade thermal energy, a small fraction of the exhaust gas is directed to Rankine-based modules, while the majority is supplied to a Kalina cycle unit. The system integrates a two-stage organic Rankine cycle with a steam Rankine cycle to simultaneously generate electricity and hot water from different temperature levels. To ensure complete cascade utilization of the remaining low-temperature thermal energy, the exhaust stream leaving the Kalina unit is further recovered in a desalination subsystem. An integrated CO2 capture unit is also incorporated to recover carbon dioxide from cement-kiln flue gas and support emission reduction objectives. The proposed configuration is evaluated using energy, exergy, and emergy analyses, complemented by sensitivity and parametric investigations. Results indicate an exergy efficiency of 34.02%, an exergy-based product cost of 6.76 $/GJ, and a sustainability index of 1.516. Emergo-economic assessment reveals the lowest factors for the Kalina and desalination units because of their significant exergy-destruction contributions. Neural-network-assisted moth-flame optimization identifies an optimal design with 45.228% exergy efficiency, 0.036 $/kWh levelized cost, a sustainability index of 1.824, and a net present value of 27.088 M$.

records.title: Integrated neural-network modeling and improved discrete-time RL-EADRC control for flexible operation of ultra-supercritical units
records.verified_abstract: With the increasing penetration of renewable energy and its inherent intermittency, ultra-supercritical (USC) units are required to operate flexibly across different load levels to accommodate fluctuating grid demands. However, accurately modeling the USC unit under such load-varying conditions remains challenging due to large inertia, strong nonlinearity, and multivariable coupling. Meanwhile, in practical implementations, the performance of error-based active disturbance rejection control (EADRC) is influenced by discrete-time realization and parameter tuning. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a flexible operation scheme integrating neural-network modeling and discrete-time reinforcement learning (RL)-EADRC control. Firstly, an improved Titans model featuring a long-term memory module (LMM) and trend-aware attention mechanism is designed to characterize the dynamic behavior of USC units. Secondly, a control strategy based on discrete-time EADRC with a current-form observer is developed to reduce observation lag and improve control performance. Furthermore, an RL agent is introduced to adaptively tune key EADRC parameters online under varying operating conditions. Experimental results based on field operating data from a 1000 MW USC unit show that the improved Titans model achieves a modeling accuracy of 99.3%. Based on this high-accuracy model, tracking and disturbance rejection tests are conducted to evaluate the proposed RL-EADRC. The results show that it achieves stable and accurate peak-shaving performance over the 57%-87% rated load range and maintains robustness at two representative operating points. These results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method for flexible operation of USC units.

records.title: Enhancing Energy Management in Microgrids with Renewable Sources and Electric Vehicles using Hybrid Red Panda Optimization and Multi-fidelity Bayesian Neural Networks
records.verified_abstract: The increasing integration of Renewable Energy Sources (RESs) and Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicles (PHEVs) into microgrids (MGs) presents significant energy management (EM) challenges due to renewable generation intermittency, fluctuating load demand, and uncertain vehicle charging requirements. Efficient MG operation requires intelligent prediction and optimization to maintain energy balance while minimizing Total Operating Costs (TOC). To address these challenges, this study proposes a hybrid Red Panda Optimization and Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Neural Network (RPO-MFBNN) framework for intelligent EM in RES- and PHEV-integrated MGs. The Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Neural Network (MFBNN) utilizes multi-fidelity information to accurately predict future renewable generation, load demand, and PHEV charging requirements, while the Red Panda Optimization (RPO) algorithm optimally allocates energy among renewable sources, battery energy storage systems, PHEVs, local loads, and the utility grid to minimize TOC and maintain reliable operation. The framework is implemented in MATLAB and evaluated under two MG operating scenarios with different storage and PHEV conditions. Comparative analysis with ANN-PSO, COA-CANN, LSO-DADRCNN, ANN-FLC, and BESO demonstrates the superiority of the proposed approach. The RPO-MFBNN framework achieves TOC values of 333.28 €ct and 321.63 €ct, compared with 385.45 €ct and 385.44 €ct for controlled operation and 671.42 €ct and 660.71 €ct for uncontrolled operation, demonstrating accurate prediction, optimized energy allocation, reduced operating costs, improved energy utilization, and efficient EM for renewable- and PHEV-integrated MGs under varying operating conditions.

records.title: Comparison and optimization of advanced machine learning methods for performance prediction of the hydrogen-enriched Wankel engine under multiple engineering constraints
records.verified_abstract: This study proposes a data-driven multi-objective optimization framework for a hydrogen-blended gasoline Wankel rotary engine. All experiments and GT-Power simulations were conducted at 4200 r/min and a manifold absolute pressure of 35 kPa. A fused dataset of 54 experimental samples and 250 simulated samples was established at three hydrogen volume fractions across the investigated ranges of excess-air coefficient and spark timing. A KDE-weighted kernel stacking model combining random forest, support vector regression, and Gaussian process regression with a ridge meta-learner was used to predict effective thermal efficiency, indicated mean effective pressure, source-specific NOx responses, peak in-cylinder pressure, and peak temperature. The model delivered the best overall predictive performance among the evaluated approaches. Feature-attribution analysis showed that the excess-air coefficient dominated peak temperature, while spark timing mainly affected effective thermal efficiency through combustion phasing; hydrogen volume fraction and excess-air coefficient jointly influenced simulated NOx. The frozen surrogate was then coupled with constrained hypervolume-improvement-based multi-objective Bayesian optimization to identify Pareto trade-offs. The selected compromise solution balanced efficiency, simulated NOx, and thermal load while satisfying the adopted screening criteria. GT-Power recalculation of five representative solutions supported the internal consistency of the surrogate predictions and screening results, but did not constitute independent validation. The proposed framework provides an efficient calibration strategy for the investigated condition, although its applicability to other speed-load conditions requires further investigation.

records.title: Data-driven sensitivity analysis and dominant factor identification for coal and gas outburst: An explainable machine learning approach fusing multi-source monitoring data
records.verified_abstract: The precise prevention and control of coal and gas outburst is crucial for achieving safe and efficient mine production. Addressing the limitations of existing big data analysis methods, which often focus on constructing high-precision black-box early warning models while lacking interpretability for decision-making, and have not yet systematically leveraged multi-source data for dynamic sensitivity analysis, this study proposes and develops a research methodology that integrates multi-source monitoring data, multi-level feature engineering, and explainable machine learning. Firstly, a feature engineering framework incorporating static geological data, dynamic gas and acoustic emission time-series data, and mining disturbance data is constructed, achieving a multi-dimensional characterization of the outburst triggering process. Secondly, by integrating the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) explainable framework with the XGBoost model, a three-dimensional sensitivity quantification analysis method is established, encompassing global importance, local triggering mechanisms, and feature interaction effects. This enables a multi-level quantitative analysis of the nonlinear coupled contributions of multiple factors. Through a typical mine case study, the abrupt variation patterns of key sensitivity indicators immediately prior to an outburst are dynamically captured, and highly sensitive data features are mapped to the physical process of stress concentration-fracture evolution-gas emission, thereby constructing a linkage from data correlations to disaster-causing mechanisms. The research outcomes provide a solution with both theoretical value and engineering applicability, facilitating a transition in outburst risk warning from static single-indicator thresholds to dynamic multi-indicator collaborative early warning.

records.title: Energy Markets, AI-Driven Demand, Electric Vehicles, and Smart Grids under Geopolitical Risk: Implications for the Energy Transition
records.verified_abstract:
This study examines the evolving interactions among energy and carbon systems, green finance, and technology-driven assets in the context of geopolitical risk and energy transition. The analysis incorporates key energy-related variables, including crude oil (WTI), carbon prices (ETS), green finance, smart-grid infrastructure, artificial intelligence, semiconductors, electric vehicles (EVs), copper, and geopolitical risk, capturing recent structural shifts associated with the post-2022 AI expansion and the 2026 Middle East geopolitical escalation. Using daily data from 18 September 2018 to 19 March 2026, the study applies TVP-VAR, generalized variance decomposition of forecast errors, quantile connectedness, and network analysis. Spillovers are identified through order-invariant generalized variance shares that measure the direction and magnitude of shock transmission across markets.

The findings reveal that the global energy system has become increasingly interconnected, particularly during periods of geopolitical tension and energy market disruptions, including those in 2026. Oil markets remain the central node in the estimated spillover network, linking conventional energy dynamics to carbon pricing, green finance, and technology-driven demand. The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence and digital infrastructure is a major market-based indicator associated with expected energy demand, reinforcing the link between technology markets and electricity consumption. At the same time, the growing adoption of electric vehicles is associated with changes in energy-demand patterns by reducing dependence on fossil fuels while increasing electricity consumption and pressure on grid systems. Smart grids play a key role in this transition by facilitating the integration of renewable energy, improving grid flexibility, and supporting the rising electricity demand associated with digitalization and electrification. Energy price fluctuations closely tie carbon markets to fossil fuel dynamics, highlighting their continued dependence.

These findings suggest integrated energy policies that jointly address energy security, AI-driven demand, EV expansion, smart-grid development, and carbon market stability to ensure a resilient and sustainable energy transition.

records.title: AI-enabled optimization of integrated photovoltaic-latent heat thermal energy storage systems for sustainable building energy management
records.verified_abstract: Global energy transition and building decarbonization have increased interest in photovoltaic and latent heat thermal energy storage (PV-LHTES) systems for zero energy buildings. This review focuses on building integrated PV-LHTES systems, including building envelopes containing PCMs and latent heat storage units coupled with photovoltaic generation, HVAC systems, and domestic hot water supply. Sensible and thermochemical storage are discussed only briefly to distinguish their functions from those of LHTES in building energy management. Recent studies on the use of AI to optimize integrated PV-LHTES systems are reviewed within a common technical framework. Physical integration of PV and LHTES enables solar energy conversion, thermal buffering, and load shifting, while AI supports system prediction, optimization, and operational control. Data based prediction and adaptive control can improve system design and operation under changing building conditions. Current building applications of PCMs include macroencapsulated panels, microencapsulated PCMs incorporated into cement or gypsum, and phase change Trombe walls. Dynamically movable PCM layers have also been investigated to make better use of natural heat and cold sources, thereby reducing summer heat gain and winter heat loss. Important limitations remain, including cycling stability, leakage, declining thermal response, high energy use during production, environmental impacts, and long payback periods. Further development of AI based PV-LHTES optimization requires better handling of heterogeneous data, improved transfer of models across building types, and greater interpretability and reliability of AI methods. Progress in materials, control methods, data management, and building energy policy will further support the application of PV-LHTES systems in low carbon buildings.

records.title: Multimodal unsupervised early warning of thermal runaway in traction batteries incorporating target-cell-aware relative-voltage pseudo-heatmap
records.verified_abstract: To address the scarcity of labeled fault samples prior to thermal runaway, the complexity of real-world operating conditions, and the difficulty in identifying weak cell-level anomalies, this study proposes a multimodal feature construction method incorporating target-cell-aware relative-voltage pseudo-heatmaps (RVPHs) and develops an unsupervised anomaly detection model with multimodal feature fusion for early thermal-runaway warning. The method integrates statistical features, time–frequency spectrograms, and target-cell-aware RVPHs to provide multidimensional representations of each target cell. The model uses modality-specific branches to encode and fuse heterogeneous inputs and locates potential faulty cells based on cell-level reconstruction errors. Validation using real-world vehicle operating data shows that, for vehicles that experienced thermal runaway, the model can identify anomalous cells several hours to several days in advance. Fixed-threshold tests on normal vehicles across different SOC ranges and cumulative mileage levels trigger no alarms. In cross-model validation, the model can still capture persistent deviations of anomalous cells from the remaining cells in the battery pack. The full multimodal model achieves the best overall performance, with Top-1 and Top-3 localization rates of 91.03% and 94.24%, respectively, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method for early thermal-runaway warning.

records.title: Economical, reliable, and deployable operation of integrated energy systems for communities: a hierarchical multi-timescale constrained reinforcement learning approach
records.verified_abstract: Integrated energy systems (IES) for communities are key building blocks of urban energy management, yet reliable operation is challenged by multi-energy coupling, multiple operational constraints, and significantly different device response speeds. Existing deep reinforcement learning methods typically operate on a single timescale and rely on penalty functions for constraint handling, where manually tuned coefficients are scenario-sensitive and often yield unstable constraint satisfaction, undermining the reliability required for real-world deployment. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a hierarchical multi-timescale dispatch method that combines constrained reinforcement learning with mathematical programming, in which a cross-timescale constraint propagation mechanism feeds residual constraint information from the inner layer back to the outer-layer policy, transforming one-way hierarchical scheduling into closed loop coordination across timescales. The method is validated on a community-scale system in Beijing, China, under typical winter and summer scenarios against six benchmark strategies. Results show that the proposed method reduces total operating cost by 3.01% and 1.10% relative to mixed-integer linear programming under the multi-timescale framework, and by 5.06% and 6.86% relative to single-timescale deep reinforcement learning, while reducing constraint violations by over 98% compared with penalty-function-based reinforcement learning and maintaining a daily cumulative online computation time below 0.1 s. Further evaluations confirm the reliability and robustness of the proposed method under different parameter settings and operating uncertainties. These findings provide a theoretical basis and practical foundation for the economical, reliable, and deployable multi-timescale dispatch optimisation of IES.

records.title: Towards sustainable aviation: aircraft fuel flow estimation using an improved iTransformer for pollutant emission calculations
records.verified_abstract: Accurate estimation of aircraft fuel consumption and emissions is essential for sustainable aviation but is constrained by the lack of publicly available fuel flow data and the limited accuracy of existing methods. This study proposes an improved iTransformer-based approach for aircraft fuel flow estimation using ADS-B data. First, key variables influencing fuel flow are identified through Spearman correlation analysis. An LSTM network and a multi-head differential attention mechanism are then incorporated into the iTransformer architecture to improve temporal feature extraction, estimation accuracy, and model generalization. QAR and ADS-B data are preprocessed and analyzed, with the model trained using QAR data and subsequently applied to ADS-B data for fuel flow estimation. The fuel flow estimation yields an average accuracy of 93.7% based on 4968 flights covering 11 aircraft types. Further estimation of fuel consumption and pollutant emissions was performed on a dataset of 23,756 flights with the same 11 aircraft types, and the overall average accuracy of all estimation results is higher than 90%. The resulting emission estimates are consistent with observed operational characteristics. Furthermore, the proposed method is applied to a large-scale dataset of 855,000 flight movements across mainland China in October 2024, enabling nationwide quantification of aviation fuel consumption and emissions. The results demonstrate the robustness and scalability of the proposed approach and highlight its potential to support aviation energy management, emissions monitoring, and sustainable aviation development.

records.title: Integrated PEM electrolyzer–fuel cell polygeneration system powered by photovoltaic–thermal solar energy: Exergoeconomic analysis and artificial intelligence optimization
records.verified_abstract: Growing requirements for low-carbon energy, freshwater, and thermal services have made the development of efficient, integrated systems based on renewable resources increasingly necessary. Accordingly, this study proposes a novel poly-generation configuration powered by a concentrated photovoltaic thermal unit for the simultaneous production of electricity, freshwater, heating, and cooling. The proposed system combines a proton exchange membrane electrolyzer for hydrogen generation, a proton exchange membrane fuel cell for electricity production, a humidification–dehumidification desalination unit, an organic Rankine cycle for recovering waste heat, and liquefied natural gas–trans-critical CO2 compression refrigeration subsystems to provide cooling. A detailed assessment encompassing energy, exergy, and economic (3E) performance is performed, after which a tri-objective optimization is applied to improve both operational efficiency and overall cost metrics. The optimization outputs reveal that the system attains an overall exergy efficiency of 3.08%, a poly-generation unit cost of 44.65/GJ, and a total cost rate of 13.48/GJ. When compared with the baseline configuration, these optimized operating conditions yield substantial gains in thermodynamic performance and economic viability, thereby validating the practicality and promise of the concentrated photovoltaic thermal-based poly-generation arrangement for low-carbon multi-energy utilization.

records.title: Data-driven energy consumption prediction for electric vehicles considering differentiated driving behavior: A hybrid machine learning model
records.verified_abstract: To address the significant impacts of heterogeneous driving behaviors on electric vehicle energy consumption, as well as the limited performance of conventional data-driven models that ignore differentiated driving features and long-term temporal dependencies, this paper constructs a data-driven hybrid machine learning prediction framework that fully considers differentiated driving behaviors throughout speed sequence generation and energy consumption forecasting. Based on 10,170 real-world kinematic segments, hierarchical K-means clustering is adopted to separate driving conditions and classify styles, while a LightGBM-based model is established for online driving style recognition. Style-specific Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) speed prediction method is further employed to generate speed sequences, and a dual-layer LSTM-Transformer (DLLT) architecture is designed to capture both local dynamics and long-term dependencies of energy consumption. Results show that the recognition model achieves 96.07% accuracy, and the DLLT model yields a weighted-average R2 of 0.9412, significantly outperforming baseline methods. The proposed data-driven hybrid machine learning framework accurately captures heterogeneous energy consumption patterns under different driving behaviors, achieving superior accuracy and generalization under low-frequency sampling compared with undifferentiated generic models.

records.title: A machine learning-based framework for electric carsharing service and energy optimization via V2G interactions
records.verified_abstract: One-way station-based electric carsharing (ECS) improves shared mobility convenience and sustainability, but encounters supply-demand imbalance issue affects ECS promotions. Regional supply-demand attributes and real-time distributions are vague to identify. Supply-demand imbalance status further affects ECS utilization, charging efficiency and service revenue. Therefore, we propose a machine learning-based framework for ECS service and energy optimization, focusing on spatiotemporal supply-demand identification, prediction, and rebalancing. Initially, a multi-category data collection and analysis pattern is formulated, involving land-using forms, ECS trajectory, user orders and station energy operations information. Then, Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) and Categorical Boosting (CatBoost) are integrated to predict user time-varying demands and station-based supply capacity within the divided ECS hot and cold regions. Group-aware splitting mechanism (GASM) and time-grouped validation mechanism (TGVM) are further introduced to enhance prediction accuracy. Finally, a user-oriented allocation model is developed for ECS supply-demand rebalancing and energy optimization. Based on dynamic price incentive mode (DPIM), an improved immune genetic algorithm (IIGA) is applied to maximize service allocation and energy operation profits. Flow-Conservative Integer Mapping Mechanism (FCIMM) and adaptive crossover and mutation factors are utilized in IIGA to enhance model convergence and robustness. Case study proves that DBSCAN and CatBoost models show higher supply-demand identification and prediction accuracy than benchmark methods. Sensitivity analysis results demonstrate that DPIM improves ECS service balance in multi-scale scenarios and enhances energy efficiency and profitability by vehicle-to-grid (V2G) interactions. To conclude, our research contributes to more efficient ECS service and energy optimization in urban transportation systems.
