records.title: LiDAR-informed transformer framework for spatiotemporal estimation of rotor-effective wind speed beyond Taylor’s frozen turbulence hypothesis
records.verified_abstract: The accurate estimation of rotor effective wind speed (REWS) is crucial in terms of improving feedforward control and enabling the effective optimization of wind turbine performance. Currently, upstream measurements provided by light detection and ranging (LiDAR) technology have been employed for REWS estimation; however, Taylor’s frozen turbulence hypothesis is commonly assumed. Furthermore, effects present in real atmospheric boundary layer flow, e.g., turbulence evolution, are neglected; thus, estimation accuracy is limited. This paper proposes a data-driven approach that utilizes a transformer model to estimate REWS directly from LiDAR measurements. Through its attention mechanism, the transformer model understands the spatiotemporal information of the wind, effectively bypassing Taylor’s hypothesis. LiDAR measurements are obtained from high-fidelity large eddy simulations of the atmospheric boundary layer across different wind speeds and preview distances to train and evaluate the proposed framework. The obtained results demonstrate that the transformer estimation exhibits good agreement with the target REWS values, significantly outperforming the REWS estimated with Taylor’s hypothesis. The proposed model improved both the time lag and wind speed overestimation present in the LiDAR measurements. At the closest measurement gate, the root mean squared error of the estimation was reduced by 68%, 56%, and 37% for mean wind speeds of 12, 14, and 16 m/s. The findings of this study highlight the application prospects of the proposed framework in real-world wind turbine control.

records.title: Establishment and verification of a predictive model for the startup strategy of turbine mode of the pumped storage unit based on machine learning
records.verified_abstract: With the global energy transition accelerating and large-scale integration of intermittent renewable energy sources—primarily wind and photovoltaics—grid frequency regulation and peak-shaving demands have intensified significantly. Pumped storage units, owing to their fast response and multi-functional regulation capabilities, serve as key supporting equipment for modern power systems. However, the strong coupling of runner speed, guide vane opening, flow rate, and pressure during the startup transient makes accurate prediction and intelligent control extremely challenging. This study investigates the pump-turbine of a high-head pumped storage power station. 15 transient CFD simulations are conducted across three typical startup strategies: Linear, 2Slopes, and BEP. A full-dimensional time-series dataset is constructed, covering hydraulic performance, hydraulic losses, runner force characteristics, and pressure pulsations. Three deep learning models—LSTM, TCN, and Informer—are trained with startup control parameters as inputs for multi-target prediction. Model performance is systematically evaluated using R2, MAE, and RMSE. Key findings are as follows. For temporally regular signals such as flow rate, output power, and guide vane pressure pulsations, all three models achieve high accuracy (R2 > 0.90). Under complex nonlinear BEP conditions with coupled multi-physics dynamics, Informer—leveraging ProbSparse self-attention and generative decoding—achieves the lowest overall error and best comprehensive performance. TCN excels in local feature fitting but struggles with long-range temporal dependencies. LSTM performs well under steady conditions but degrades significantly under strong nonlinear and abrupt-change scenarios. This work presents an efficient, data-driven prediction framework for rapid optimization of pumped storage startup strategies, effectively avoiding the high computational cost of repeated multi-scheme CFD simulations.

records.title: Machine learning prediction of hydrochar and bio-oil properties during biomass hydrothermal conversion with aqueous phase recirculation
records.verified_abstract: Hydrothermal conversion coupled with aqueous phase (AP) recirculation has emerged as a promising strategy for enhancing biomass valorization by improving product yields and energy recovery (ER). For the first time, AP recirculation was explicitly incorporated as a specific input variable into ML models (Model 1 and Model 2) for predicting hydrochar and bio-oil properties during hydrothermal carbonization (HTC) and hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL), respectively. Four ML algorithms were systematically compared and optimized, with Gradient Boosting Regression (GBR) showing a slight performance advantage. Model 1 (GBR) delivered the best performance for hydrochar properties, with testing R2 of 0.98 for hydrochar yield (HY) and 0.95 for energy recovery of hydrochar (ER_HC). Model 2 (GBR) achieved the most robust performance, with testing R2 of 0.83 for bio-oil yield (BY) and 0.85 for energy recovery of bio-oil (ER_BO). Feature importance analysis revealed that AP recirculation ranked among the top one or two most influential variables for both HTC and HTL. Increasing AP recirculation initially led to significant improvements in hydrochar and bio-oil yields as well as ER, whereas further increases resulted in diminishing benefits due to the gradual saturation of organic compounds in the AP. Furthermore, donut chart analysis demonstrated that biomass elemental composition contributed more significantly to product properties than hydrothermal conditions. Finally, the integrated software enables rapid prediction of hydrothermal products, facilitating biomass screening, AP recirculation-assisted hydrothermal conversion process route selection, and optimization.

records.title: Selective expert-guided reinforcement learning for vehicle cabin thermal management
records.verified_abstract: Model-free reinforcement learning for vehicle cabin thermal management requires extensive environment interaction, as early exploration can generate ineffective or energy-intensive actuator commands. Expert demonstrations can reduce this burden, but their utility and reliability depend on how expert information is used during learning. We propose Selective Expert-Guided Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (SEG-TD3), which selectively allocates expert-derived information across value learning, exploration, and actor regularization. Genuine expert transitions and one-step counterfactual probes jointly support critic learning, whereas only genuine expert actions provide residual guidance for exploration. For actor learning, a detached positive-advantage Soft Q-filter admits only critic-supported candidate actions for actor regularization. Expert influence decays with accumulated experience and is removed at deployment. SEG-TD3 and five learned baselines were trained for 100 episodes with five matched random seeds on a physics-based vehicle thermal management system and evaluated using deterministic controllers, mechanism ablations, and 12 operating conditions. Under the same interaction budget, SEG-TD3 reached high training returns earlier than standard TD3 and reduced mean cabin-temperature MAE at episode 100 by 13.1% with similar TMS energy use. Across the 12-condition suite, SEG-TD3 reduced mean MAE and TMS energy use by 18.8% and 9.7%, respectively, relative to TD3; both reductions were statistically significant after Holm correction. SEG-TD3 also required 87.7% less measured reinforcement-learning update time than SPReD-E in the same software and hardware environment. These results show that role-selective allocation of expert information can improve interaction efficiency and closed-loop performance without retaining expert guidance at deployment.

records.title: Semantic-mask-enhanced deep reinforcement learning for energy storage scheduling in virtual building-cluster microgrids with vehicle-to-building flexibility
records.verified_abstract: To address the optimal operation of building-cluster microgrids integrating multiple distributed energy resources and vehicle-to-building (V2B) flexibility, this study constructs a 30-day virtual environment using adapted multi-source building load data and public electric vehicle (EV) charging records. Vehicle arrival, charging, discharge eligibility, and departure are modeled under time-of-use prices. A state-dependent semantic action masking mechanism is developed for deep reinforcement learning (DRL) based stationary energy storage system (ESS) scheduling. The mechanism integrates ESS physical constraints and operational information to dynamically construct a state-dependent candidate action set. Deep Q-Network (DQN), Dueling Double Deep Q-Network (D3QN), and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) select the final ESS action. Under the V2B-enabled condition, EVs supply 141.5 MWh to buildings, and the average net electricity cost per unit charging energy decreases by 24.2%. Across six paired comparisons, semantic action masking reduces operating cost and total grid purchase by averages of 1.27% and 3.77%, respectively. The action modification rate decreases by an average of 56.18 percentage points, and the variability of total episode returns during late-stage training decreases by an average of 51.05%. Among the evaluated configurations, PPO with semantic action masking and V2B achieves the lowest operating cost, reducing operating cost, total grid purchase, and peak-period grid purchase by 18.5%, 13.2%, and 44.7%, respectively, compared with the baseline configuration without ESS or V2B. These findings provide a methodological reference for the intelligent operation and coordinated utilization of flexible energy resources in building-cluster microgrids.

records.title: A dual-driven framework for low-carbon dispatch in the steel enterprise: Integrating deep learning forecasting and distributionally robust optimization under carbon price uncertainty
records.verified_abstract: The steel industry remains one of the largest industrial carbon emitters worldwide and is exposed to increasingly stringent carbon market regulations. The operation of Renewable Integrated Energy Systems (RIES) in steel enterprises is complicated by multi-dimensional uncertainties, including intermittent renewable generation, strongly coupled multi-energy loads, and volatile carbon prices. To address these challenges, this study develops a dual-driven framework that combines high-precision forecasting with a two-stage distributionally robust optimization model (TSDROM) for day-ahead and real-time low-carbon dispatch of a steel enterprise RIES. First, a chaos game optimization-enhanced hybrid forecasting architecture, integrating Transformer, bidirectional long short-term memory, and XGBoost, is constructed to predict renewable generation, multi-energy loads, and carbon trading prices with hourly resolution. The prediction errors are then used to build a Wasserstein distance-based ambiguity set, enabling data-driven uncertainty characterization without assuming a specific probability distribution. On this basis, a TSDROM with a linear affine recourse policy coordinates electricity, thermal, gas, hydrogen, and cooling subsystems under worst-case uncertainty realizations. A case study shows that carbon capture reduces daily physical emissions by 76.0% relative to pre-capture direct emissions and yields a 90.13 t/day Emissions Trading System (ETS) allowance surplus under the adopted capacity configuration. Under the largest resampling configuration considered, explicitly modeling carbon price uncertainty reduces the total system cost by CNY 1.105 million relative to the corresponding case without carbon-price uncertainty. The proposed framework provides an operationally tractable “prediction–optimization” paradigm for robust and cost-effective low-carbon dispatch in steel and other energy-intensive industries.

records.title: Unveiling nonlinear thresholds and synergistic effects in continuous supercritical water gasification of biomass via interpretable machine learning
records.verified_abstract: Driven by the global imperative for green hydrogen transition, supercritical water gasification (SCWG) of biomass waste has gained attention for its high conversion efficiency. Developing an interpretable and generalizable model to predict hydrogen yield is essential for accelerating industrial deployment of biomass-based SCWG, yet related studies remain scarce. Herein, experimental data from a continuous SCWG reactor are used to identify key parameters, including biomass elemental and proximate analyses, as well as operating temperature, pressure, residence time, and biomass concentration. These parameters are then used to develop XGBoost, CatBoost, and RF models for hydrogen yield prediction. The results indicate that the XGBoost model demonstrated superior predictive accuracy, with an R2 of 0.975, an RMSE of 0.944, and an MAE of 0.626. Furthermore, based on interpretable machine learning analysis, this study elucidated the synergistic regulatory mechanism of multivariate nonlinear interactions on the hydrogen production performance of continuous-flow SCWG. Three key coupling effects in the process were quantitatively analyzed, including the thermodynamic competition between steam reforming and decarboxylation reactions, the time-temperature compensation effect of temperature-residence time, and mass-transfer limitations imposed by ash and high-concentration feed. The results provide a direct mechanistic basis for delineating the reactor's optimal operating window and guiding process amplification.

records.title: Neural Network Enhanced Digital Twin Based Carbon Oriented Planning of Distributed Generation and Hydrogen Microgrids in Prosumer-Centric Energy hub
records.verified_abstract: Carbon-aware distribution planning requires investment decisions that account for how storage, hydrogen-based microgrids, and network carbon flows interact over time. Existing planning and scheduling models usually treat these elements separately, leaving weak representation of storage-induced emission shifting and hydrogen-microgrid carbon responsibility. This paper develops an integrated planning framework for a power distribution network coupled with hydrogen-based microgrids under emission targets and chronological carbon-flow effects. The framework formulates distributed generation, electrical storage, and hydrogen storage decisions within a two-stage stochastic structure, transfers carbon burden across charging and discharging periods. The resulting nonlinear formulation is converted into a mixed-integer nonconvex quadratically constrained programming structure and solved through a penalty-based proximal-distance scheme. Tests on a modified network show that coordinated hydrogen flexibility reduces total annual cost by about 20.5% compared with an electrical-storage-dominant compliance case while preserving the same emission target. Hydrogen-specific carbon-flow guidance reduces system emissions by about 18.5% relative to the unrestricted operating trial and lowers the carbon intensity of hydrogen-related electricity use from 0.317 to 0.114 Ton/MWh. Annual hydrogen-storage complementarity also decreases operating cost by nearly 5.9% and increases renewable utilization by about 1.7 percentage points. The results indicate that chronological carbon tracing can materially alter storage valuation and coordinated low-carbon planning.

records.title: AI-driven generative design method for tunnel smoke control system using diffusion model and NSGA-II
records.verified_abstract: Smoke control systems are critical for tunnel fire safety. With the increasing adoption of new-energy vehicles, tunnel fires are becoming more complex due to changing fire characteristics. However, traditional smoke control design relies on case-by-case analysis and repetitive numerical simulations, resulting in high computational costs and limited adaptability to diverse fire scenarios. These limitations may result in an inefficient smoke control system design process. To overcome these challenges, this study proposes an AI-driven generative design framework that integrates diffusion model and NSGA-II to optimize smoke control system schemes. A diffusion model is established that can efficiently and accurately predict smoke control performance for diverse scenarios. The trained diffusion model is then embedded into the NSGA-II framework to perform global design space exploration, where thermal and toxic risk assessment indexes are incorporated as optimization function, enabling the automatic generation of optimal solutions for diverse fire scenarios. In the case of tunnel fire scenarios, the method achieves R2 = 0.95 for smoke fields for training dataset and maintains relative errors below 20% for tunnel geometries and fire scenarios outside the training distribution. For the three primary smoke control modes, including longitudinal ventilation, centralized smoke exhaust, and combined modes, the optimized scheme can be automatically generated within minutes under different smoke control requirements, reducing ventilation or smoke exhaust volume requirements by 52%, 15%, and 23%, respectively, and decreasing temperature- and CO-exceedance regions by 10%, 6%, and 12% versus traditional methods. This study proposes a decision-making tool, which supports the development of next-generation smoke control systems.

records.title: Data-efficient battery pack aging diagnosis in real-world electric vehicles via uncertainty-aware semi-supervised learning using random short charging data
records.verified_abstract: Accurate battery aging diagnosis is fundamental to the safe and cost-effective operation of electric vehicles. However, existing data-driven methods generally require large quantities of labeled data collected under relatively complete charging conditions, which are difficult and costly to obtain in practical applications where charging events are random, fragmented, and mostly incomplete. To address these issues, this paper proposes a data-efficient uncertainty-aware semi-supervised learning framework that exploits predictive uncertainty to guide pseudo-label utilization for battery-pack aging diagnosis using random short charging data collected from real-world electric vehicles. Predictive uncertainty is used to evaluate pseudo-label reliability, enabling adaptive utilization of abundant unlabeled data while suppressing error propagation from unreliable pseudo-labels. To improve both robustness and physical relevance, aging-related features are automatically extracted from random short charging data in main-peak window of incremental capacity curve, effectively capturing degradation information while alleviating the impact of cell inconsistency and eliminating the need for manually designed features. Validation is conducted on field data collected from 20 electric vehicles spanning more than 154 weeks. With only 10% of vehicles labeled, the mean RMSE and MAE are 0.5 and 0.2 Ah in the best case and 1.1 and 0.7 Ah in the worst case, respectively. Compared with four benchmarks, the proposed framework reduces best- and worst-case RMSE by 46.5%-62.9% and 15.2%-32.5%, respectively, and MAE by 51.1%-77.5% and 23.7%-48.6%, enabling reliable capacity estimation with limited reference labels from random short-charging data.

records.title: Optimization of cavitation performance of centrifugal pump impeller using flow field point cloud and deep learning
records.verified_abstract: This study presents an accurate and reliable methodology for the multi-objective optimization of cavitation performance of a centrifugal pump. An automated approach for determining critical cavitation pressure is developed, overcoming limitations inherent in conventional sampling strategies. An end-to-end surrogate modeling framework based on PointNet++ is constructed, integrating geometric parameters and flow characteristics by extracting key physical features from flow field data via point cloud technology. Geometry-grouped five-fold cross-validation across five training seeds shows that the proposed fine-tuning model outperforms the five comparison models, achieving an R^{2} of 0.98 ± 0.0004 while maintaining high predictive accuracy in the low-pressure region. CFD validation further confirms that the prediction error for the critical cavitation pressure at the optimized point is merely 0.77%. Furthermore, by combining the surrogate model with the NSGA-II algorithm and entropy weight method, a representative compromise design is selected from the Pareto front in the three-dimensional objective space encompassing head, efficiency, and critical cavitation pressure. Results show that the optimized pump exhibits enhanced hydraulic performance across the entire operating range, increasing the head by 35.78 m and the efficiency from 0.568 to 0.610 at the design flow rate, while reducing the critical net positive suction head by 0.20 m. Under identical NPSH_{a} conditions, the optimized impeller exhibits smaller low-pressure and vapor regions than the baseline impeller, which is consistent with a modest improvement trend in cavitation performance.

records.title: A physics-guided topology-aware graph neural network surrogate framework for intelligent design and optimization of underground compressed air energy storage systems
records.verified_abstract: Underground compressed air energy storage (CAES) systems involve complex system configurations and thermodynamic processes, while existing thermodynamic analysis methods are computationally expensive and lack global optimization of system topology and operating parameters, limiting further improvements in system efficiency and energy density. This study proposes a physics-guided topology-aware surrogate framework for rapid performance prediction and multi-objective optimization of underground CAES systems. A high-fidelity thermodynamic model coupling the surface energy conversion system and underground storage cavern is established to generate the training dataset. The CAES system is then represented as a graph, and a GraphSAGE surrogate is integrated with NSGA-II to simultaneously optimize system topology and operating parameters. The surrogate achieves ${R}^{2}>0.997$ for all 14 predicted performance indicators, with MAPEs of 0.30% and 1.24% for round-trip efficiency and energy density, respectively. For unseen system topologies, the corresponding MAPEs remain below 2.5%. Under batch inference, the proposed surrogate reduces the computational time from 358.7 ms per case for the high-fidelity solver to only 0.078 ms per case, corresponding to an approximately 4600-fold computational speedup. Multi-objective optimization reveals a clear trade-off between round-trip efficiency and energy density. The recommended design adopts four-stage compression and seven-stage expansion, achieving a model-predicted round-trip efficiency of 80.48% and an energy density of 8.25 kWh m^{−3}. These results demonstrate the predictive accuracy, topology generalization, and computational efficiency of the proposed framework for preliminary design and optimization of underground CAES systems.

records.title: Greywater as a valuable source of clean energy in buildings: Evaluation of a new horizontal shower heat exchanger based on machine learning methods integrated with SHAP analysis
records.verified_abstract: Predicting the efficiency of heat recovery from wastewater is crucial for designing more efficient domestic hot water systems equipped with drain water heat recovery exchangers. This study presents the developed predictive models for predicting the preheated water temperature (Tph) and efficiency (E) of the new horizontal shower heat exchanger (HSHE). Six popular machine learning algorithms were used to determine the most suitable prediction models: eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGB), Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting (GB), CatBoost (CB), Support Vector Regression (SVR), and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN). The dataset for these models was obtained from laboratory tests of the constructed HSHE prototype. Experimental research was conducted for a wide range of input variables and for three heat recovery system configurations: Configuration I – balanced flow conditions, Configuration II, and Configuration III – unbalanced flow conditions. The models were evaluated using regression metrics, and the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method was used to better understand the predictions generated by the selected machine learning models. The results show that the tree models perform best in predicting Tph and E for all system configurations. Depending on the system configuration, the mixed water flow rate Q or mixed water temperature Tsh determined the efficiency of the tested heat exchanger. In most cases, the effect of hot water temperature on E and Tph was marginal. The research results also showed that advanced machine learning methods are a valuable tool in the design and optimization of drain water heat recovery exchangers.

records.title: Nature-to-microstructure network: A cross-domain knowledge transfer framework for steel microstructure classification
records.verified_abstract: Reliable microstructure identification underpins the control of microstructural evolution and the tailored design of mechanical performance in steels. However, conventional approaches are limited by subjectivity and inefficiency, while deep learning models often struggle with data scarcity and multiscale complexity. This study proposes Nature-to-Microstructure Network (N2M-Net) a cross-domain transfer learning (TL) framework leveraging morphological similarities between natural textures and steel microstructures. It is designed to enable accurate microstructure classification under extreme data scarcity and to enhance model generalization through morphology-guided knowledge transfer. Pretrained on 750 natural images, N2M-Net incorporates residual connections, spatial attention, and dilated Inception modules for robust multiscale feature extraction. With only 20 microscopic images, it surpassed 95.00 % accuracy within 20 epochs and reached 95.67 % final accuracy, significantly outperforming direct training. This work demonstrates a novel morphology-driven cross-domain transfer paradigm for intelligent microstructure analysis under limited data.

records.title: Tuning screw-to-edge dislocation slip discrepancy via graph neural network–accelerated exploration of local ordered states in refractory high-entropy alloys
records.verified_abstract: Refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) exhibit unique dislocation behaviors that underpin their exceptional mechanical properties. However, the vast compositional space and complex local atomic environments make it difficult to tailor dislocation slip mechanisms. In this study, we demonstrate that dislocation slip resistance in RHEAs with local ordering can be effectively tuned by jointly adjusting the diffuse-antiphase-boundary energy (DAPBE) and lattice distortion difference (LDD). Using a high-throughput framework enabled by a physics-informed graph neural network, we systematically explored the MoNbTaW compositional space through atomistic simulations with machine-learning potentials. Our findings reveal that increasing DAPBE strengthens resistance to screw dislocation slip, while increasing LDD diminishes this effect but enhances the resistance to edge dislocation slip. Notably, compositions exhibiting both high DAPBE and LDD yield a balanced dislocation response. This study offers a design strategy to improve the strength–ductility synergy in BCC RHEAs by tuning intrinsic material parameters via local ordering.

records.title: On the efficient texture representation in neural network methods for plastic deformation modelling
records.verified_abstract: Representation of crystallographic texture and its evolution is critical for efficient mesoscale modelling of plastic deformation. Although Euler angles are widely adopted to represent texture, the high dimensionality and unclear correlation with stress responses compromise their effectiveness in neural network-based deformation modelling, especially when applied to diverse textures. This paper introduces the generalized convex yield network (GCYN), a feedforward neural network with partial input convexity constraints to predict the yield onset. The proposed architecture decomposes the yield function into a convex stress-dependent branch that guarantees global convexity of the yield surface, and a non-convex branch integrates tailored material descriptors, such as generalized spherical harmonics (GSH) coefficients and typical yield onsets, to explicitly capture anisotropic yield behavior across distinct textures and materials. This bifurcated design enables the GCYN to learn texture/material-specific corrections to the yield surface. The generalizability of GCYN across textures was demonstrated by training on yield datasets for different textured TA1 titanium generated via crystal plasticity (CP) simulations. The well-tuned criteria accurately predicts the yield onsets when applying to the untrained textures, achieving an average prediction error of 0.903% in the 6D stress space. In addition, GCYN accurately predicted the yield onsets of some experimental titanium textures with different characteristics. To demonstrate the potential applicability of GCYN to different materials at a conceptual level, the model was trained on datasets generated from the Lode-dependent anisotropic-asymmetric (LAA) Hill48 criterion. The trained model accurately emulates a parameterized family of analytical yield loci, achieving an average prediction error below 0.2% in plane. Moreover, The yield loci predicted by the GCYN strictly satisfy global convexity while preserving the essential characteristics of the original yield surface. This work provides a fully convex and material/texture-sensitive yield criterion.

records.title: Materials Informatics approach to design new high-entropy shape memory alloys
records.verified_abstract: The current study uses a materials informatics approach to design new high-entropy shape memory alloys (HESMAs). The two-stage Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) was used to enhance the dataset. Several machine learning models are trained and tested to predict martensite start temperature (Ts). The trained ML models are used to select new potential compositions of HESMAs. A modified Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model shows a testing R^{2} score of 0.89 and predicted the new alloys transformation temperature comparable to the experimental data. The effect of material descriptors on the prediction of Ts is interpreted using SHAP and LIME.

records.title: Physical feature guided design of refractory high entropy alloys for strength-plasticity synergy across wide strain rates
records.verified_abstract: Strength and plasticity are critical properties but always unavoidable trade-offs of materials for various service environment. The vast composition-property space of refractory high entropy alloy (RHEAs) enables resolving this trade-off, but makes their composition design highly challenging. Herein, we formulate a physical feature-guided design strategy for RHEAs toward balanced strength-plasticity across strain rates. Three RHEAs with a superior combination of strength and plasticity over wide strain rate ranges were discovered and synthetized. The composition-property diagrams are constructed and an optimal composition range is identified based on model prediction for several typical refractory elements. By decoding the key physical features governing property trade-offs via interpretable machine learning (ML), this study establishes a data-efficient paradigm for multi-objective materials design, demonstrated here for refractory high-entropy alloys but extensible to other complex systems.

records.title: Quantitative composition‑annealing temperature map of stacking‑fault energy in CoCrNi medium‑entropy alloys unveiled by first‑principles neural‑network potentials
records.verified_abstract: Precise control of stacking-fault energy (SFE) underpins CoCrNi medium entropy alloys deformation design, yet its quantitative dependence on composition and temperature remains unclear. We apply a first-principles neural-network potential (NNP) with Monte Carlo sampling to deliver a high-resolution SFE map as a function of composition and annealing temperature. The map, governed by Cr-Co/Ni order pairs and element-specific SFE signatures, reveals that concentration-thermal history interplay regulates chemical order and SFEs. Changes in alloy composition and annealing temperature collectively influence the annealed configuration, thereby affecting the SFE. The SFE spans a tunable range from -67.5 to +194.5 mJ m⁻², transitioning from negative in disordered to ∼195 mJ m⁻² in ordered. This tunability dictates deformation pathways: ordered low-temperature states suppress twinning, disordered high-temperature ones promote martensitic transformation. Overall, chemical order is the key variable linking atomic chemistry with defect energetics, enabling predictive alloy design.

records.title: Identification and mechanistic understanding of key elements governing the thermal expansion coefficient in Ni-based superalloys: a combined machine learning and first principles study
records.verified_abstract: The coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) critically governs the thermal stability and dimensional reliability of Ni-based superalloys. However, the influence of alloying elements on CTE and their temperature-dependent mechanisms remain unclear. This study constructed a machine learning model with a high coefficient of determination (R² = 0.92), successfully identifying Mo, W, and Cr as key elements regulating CTE. Based on the Grüneisen theory, first-principles calculations further elucidate that at low temperatures, Mo and W-doped systems effectively suppress the CTE through the synergistic effects of introducing low-frequency phonons and high bulk modulus (BT). Above 800 K, the Ni-Mo system exhibits lower Grüneisen parameter (γ) and heat capacity (CV) values than the Ni-W system, resulting in a more pronounced thermal expansion suppression effect. In contrast, Cr induces only minor perturbations in electronic states and phonon spectra, resulting in a relatively weak influence.

records.title: Agentic AI for autonomous discovery of radiation-tolerant CoCrFeMnNi high entropy alloys
records.verified_abstract: Designing radiation-tolerant high entropy alloys (HEAs) traditionally requires thousands of expensive atomistic simulations with domain knowledge informed iterations. Here, we present an agentic AI framework that autonomously explores alloy compositional space by coupling a large language model (LLM) with on-the-fly molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. The agent operates in a closed-loop manner wherein it proposes new alloy compositions, launches LAMMPS primary knock-on atom simulations on each candidate, extracts defect production, and updates its search strategy based on the evolving defect landscape. Using six distinct starting chemistries, i.e. Co-rich, Cr-rich, Fe-rich, Mn-rich, Ni-rich, and equiatomic, our AI agent adjusts exploration breadth, performing large global sweeps when early simulations indicate high defect production and narrowing to local searches when favorable low defect regions are discovered. The framework demonstrates the ability of an agentic AI framework to autonomously navigate high dimensional compositional space and reason about defect trends without predefined heuristics.

records.title: Identifying the structural origin of soft spots in prism-dominated Mg65Cu25Y10 metallic glasses via SOAP-driven machine learning
records.verified_abstract: Mg-based metallic glasses (MGs) are typically brittle and exhibit prism-dominated local order, unlike the more ductile Cu-Zr MGs built on icosahedral backbones. Elucidating the structural origin of plastic susceptibility in such glasses remains challenging because conventional low-dimensional descriptors cannot capture the coupled effects of local topology and chemical environment. Here we develop a Smooth Overlap of Atomic Positions (SOAP)-driven machine-learning framework to predict plasticity-prone "soft spots" in modeled Mg65Cu25Y10 MG directly from the undeformed atomic structure. Using optimized high-dimensional SOAP descriptors, a sigmoid-calibrated logistic-regression classifier achieves strong predictive performance (ROC-AUC = 0.913), clearly outperforming representative low-dimensional descriptors based on local chemistry and fivefold-symmetry-related order. These results indicate that plastic susceptibility in the modeled Mg-Cu-Y glass is governed by coupled topological-chemical features, which are more effectively encoded in the high-dimensional SOAP representation. This SOAP-driven framework provides a robust structural fingerprint for locating shear-transformation-susceptible regions in amorphous alloys.

records.title: Interface-aware interpretable attention U-Net for phase-field surrogate modeling
records.verified_abstract: In this study, an attention U-Net (AU-Net) based surrogate model for phase-field (PF) simulations of grain growth is developed to predict subsequent microstructure frame given a preceding frame. The learned interface awareness in the AU-Net significantly mitigates the localized error accumulation at interfaces during long-time recursive prediction, which is substantially higher in conventional U-Net (CU-Net) models. The AU-Net produces state-of-the-art results by outperforming a strong benchmark CU-Net across various evaluation matrices such as intersection over union (IoU>0.990), structural similarity index measure (SSIM>0.998) and mean absolute error (MAE<0.004) throughout 100-step recursive rollout. The interpretability analysis using gradient weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) reveals that the AU-Net predominantly focuses on interfaces while the CU-Net exhibits a bias towards grain interiors. Consequently, AU-Net produces higher fidelity predictions over CU-Net in the spatially dense regions of interfaces, especially during the event of disappearance of smaller grains.

records.title: Uncovering a structural phase transition underlying surface-accelerated dynamics via machine learning in glassy films
records.verified_abstract: Enhanced dynamics near the glassy surface alters glass transition points and matters new material designs that exploit surface effects. Despite studies over the past decades, resolving the mechanism of the depth-dependent dynamic acceleration remains a big challenge. Herein, we find that the decoupling of the surface dynamics associates with a bimodal distribution of atomic mobility in a prototype CuZr metallic system. By combining molecular dynamics with a supervised machine learning framework, we derive a local structural order parameter, “softness”, accurately predicting particle mobility in the CuZr glassy films. We identify a depth-dependent structural crossover in the derived order parameter, marked by a gradual shift from a “soft” phase to a “hard” phase region. We demonstrate that the soft phase accounts for the decoupled dynamics near surface, while the diminishing of it corresponds to the weakening of the transferred dynamics from surface to the interior.

records.title: Bridging the maturity-expectation gap: Generative AI in strategic decision-making for public R&D interim review
records.verified_abstract: Public R&D interim reviews face persistent challenges related to scalability, evaluator bias, and inconsistency in multi-stakeholder judgment. Generative AI (Gen AI) has the potential to mitigate these limitations by enhancing efficiency and standardization, yet its deployment also introduces risks such as algorithmic bias and loss of transparency. This calls for a systematic framework to support strategic decision-making and guide responsible adoption. This study introduces the Maturity–Expectation Gap (MEG) framework, which captures the misalignment between stakeholder perceptions of AI maturity and the actual technological state. Existing models such as the Technology Acceptance Model fail to reflect the temporal and institutional dynamics of emerging technologies. To address this, the study combines expert survey data on perceived maturity with machine learning-based literature analysis to compute expectation scores across twenty-four evaluation criteria. Results show that MEG significantly varies across stakeholder groups, and that higher MEG values are associated with lower confidence in Gen AI adoption, highlighting the framework's utility in explaining strategic adoption decisions (RQ1). Furthermore, MEG enables diagnostic classification of evaluation domains, identifying areas of alignment (e.g., Financial Health) and misalignment (e.g., Decision-Making), thereby supporting phased and risk-aware deployment strategies (RQ2). MEG framework offers a structured lens for managing expectation–capability alignment, extending technology adoption theory while supporting strategic decision-making for the responsible integration of Gen AI in public-sector evaluation systems.

records.title: Exploring the directions of artificial intelligence in good health and well-being (SDG3) using big data and LDA topic modeling
records.verified_abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds significant potential for advancing Sustainable Development Goal 3 (SDG3)—Good Health and Well-being—yet the field remains fragmented across numerous topics and disciplines. In this study, we apply Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) to a final corpus of 60,010 Scopus abstracts after filtering, extracting k = 160 latent topics (selected via metric-based tuning; see Appendix A) and organizing them into a process-oriented, Health Technology Assessment–inspired framework that links Drivers, AI Infrastructure and Methods, Implementation, and Results. Key findings include dominant research streams in disease diagnostics (e.g., breast cancer, cardiovascular disease), personalized treatment, and automation, alongside the emergence of large language models (LLMs) like ChatGPT. Geographical mapping highlights Asia, North America, and Europe as research hubs, while underexplored areas such as AI in social media and student education are identified. We also introduce a quadrant-based trend analysis to distinguish “niche excellence” from “leading research areas” and chart short-versus medium-term dynamics. This methodological contribution not only offers a comprehensive “scientific map” of AI–SDG3 research but also provides a scalable blueprint for mapping AI's role across other SDGs and guiding future theory-driven and policy-relevant investigations.

records.title: Identifying firm-specific technology opportunities: Heterogeneous graph neural network-based link prediction
records.verified_abstract: A firm’s technological innovation is influenced by both its internal capabilities and external technological trends. However, previous firm-specific technology opportunity discovery (TOD) studies have predominantly focused on structural associations between technologies within a firm’s internal and external contexts, with limited exploration of deeper semantic relationships. This paper proposes a novel firm-specific TOD approach that considers both structural and semantic associations. Our methodology consists of four modules: (1) collecting patent data; (2) constructing a technological innovation heterogeneous graph; (3) identifying the target firm’s technology opportunities using Multi-Attention Graph Link Prediction (MAG-LP), which captures both structural and semantic information from the graph; and (4) evaluating technology opportunities using indicators of technology competitiveness, technology growth, and technology maturity. The efficiency and effectiveness of our proposed approach are demonstrated through its application to Honda Motor Company. This work contributes to a comprehensive understanding of potential R&D directions for the target firm.

records.title: When employees meet gen AI: The double-edged effects of AI attitude on creativity
records.verified_abstract: Existing research has primarily focused on the instrumental attributes of Generative AI (Gen AI), such as its usefulness and usage patterns, in influencing employee creativity. However, there is a lack of systematic exploration of Gen AI attitude—defined as the degree of support and willingness to adopt Gen AI—and their underlying mechanisms in shaping creativity. Grounded in role theory, this study uncovers the dual effects of Gen AI attitude on creativity. On the one hand, Gen AI attitude can reduce creativity through increased role ambiguity. On the other hand, it can enhance creativity by facilitating task crafting. Furthermore, this study introduces creative self-efficacy as a moderating factor, revealing that it mitigates the negative impact of Gen AI attitude on creativity via role ambiguity while strengthening its positive effect through task crafting. These hypotheses are tested through two complementary studies. Study 1 employs a multi-wave survey (N = 591) and structural equation modeling to validate the proposed relationships. Study 2 utilizes a large language model-driven text analysis approach, using GPT to analyze 415 social media texts, further reinforcing the robustness of the findings. The results contribute to a deeper theoretical understanding of how Gen AI attitude shapes creativity, offering new insights into the intersection of technology-related attitudes and creativity.

records.title: Managerial decision-making and AI: A taxonomy of AI collaboration orientations and strategic integration
records.verified_abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) holds significant promise for enhancing business decision-making, yet managers differ in their perceptions and approaches to collaborating with AI systems. Organizations thus face a managerial challenge: how to account for individual AI collaboration orientations to maximize the benefits of human–AI collaboration while addressing fears of replacement. This study develops a taxonomy of AI collaboration orientations among marketing decision-makers, based on survey data from 472 professionals. A person-centered analysis reveals four distinct profiles: AI Trailblazers, who view AI as a strategic partner; AI Strategists, who balance AI insights with human judgement; Pragmatic Adopters, who value efficiency but remain cautious; and AI Skeptics, who express concerns over sense of control and transparency. These orientations are shaped by collaboration preferences, sense of control, explainability, and organisational support. We also find that managers in organizations that promote AI experimentation report greater satisfaction with market performance. This study advances research on AI trust, human–AI collaboration, and managerial technology adoption. The taxonomy offers firms a practical tool to assess and support AI collaboration readiness and to develop adaptive leadership in an evolving digital environment.

records.title: The role of task breadth and cognitive flexibility in generative AI-supported creative idea generation
records.verified_abstract: This paper investigates how, and under what conditions, generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems, particularly fine-tuned large language models (LLMs), stimulate cognitive flexibility and enhance the flexibility pathway to creativity. Drawing on the dual pathway to creativity model, we examine the role of task breadth in facilitating creative idea generation. Through two randomized experimental studies, we found that fine-tuned LLM-generated stimuli significantly enhance breadth of exploration, which is a consequence of cognitive flexibility, when participants engage in exploration within a broad domain (Study 1). In contrast, no significant effect is observed within a constrained domain (Study 2). These findings highlight the critical interaction between generative AI and task structure in driving creativity. Our study contributes to a deeper understanding of how AI systems reshape cognitive processes, providing theoretical and practical insights into the evolving nature of creativity in the era of generative AI.

records.title: Exploring the antecedents and mitigators of user uncertainty in generative AI use: A principal-agent perspective
records.verified_abstract: As generative AI (GAI) becomes increasingly intelligent and autonomous, users encounter new forms of uncertainty arising from the evolving user-GAI relationship. Understanding this transformation and how associated uncertainty can be effectively managed is critical for fostering trust and sustainable GAI usage. Grounded in Principal-Agent Theory (PAT), this study redefines the user-GAI relationships from a principal-agent perspective and develops a nomological framework to explain how key technical characteristics of GAI influence users' perceived uncertainty and continuance intention in general GAI use settings. Using a mixed-methods design, we first conducted an exploratory computational text analysis of large-scale user-generated online content to identify major sources of uncertainty and key GAI attributes, which informed the development of a nomological framework. We then validated and tested the framework through a quantitative survey. Our results show that users’ fear of opportunism and information privacy concerns significantly increase perceived uncertainty, thereby reducing continuance intention. Conversely, GAI accuracy, transparency, and empathy effectively mitigate uncertainty by alleviating these fears and concerns. This study contributes to the literature by investigating user uncertainty within a redefined principal-agent structure and integrating PAT with technological features to build a comprehensive nomological framework. Practically, we offer actionable guidance for designing human-centered GAI systems that emphasize accurate, transparent, and empathic interactions to reduce user uncertainty and support sustained engagement.

records.title: Identification of driving factors in national innovation ecosystems under the PSR framework: Based on machine learning algorithms
records.verified_abstract: To address the challenge of insufficient momentum for sustainable global innovation development, a growing number of countries are elevating the cultivation of innovation ecosystems to the level of national strategy, aiming to secure discourse power and initiative in future international competition. Previously, studies have primarily focused on the conceptualization and evolutionary mechanisms of National Innovation Ecosystems (NIEs), and have extended the indicator systems of National Innovation Systems to evaluate NIEs performance. However, there remains a notable gap in applying ecological theories to construct NIEs indicator systems, as well as a lack of exploration into the driving effects of national macro-level characteristics on NIEs. Addressing this research gap, this study draws upon the food chain perspective and the quadruple helix model to propose a novel conceptual framework for understanding the interactions among actors within the NIEs. Furthermore, we introduce the Pressure-State-Response (PSR) framework to establish a system of driving factors centered on National Risk, National Openness, and National Governance. This research provides a systematic analytical tool for clarifying the interactive logic among multi-level innovation actors. The revealed differentiated driving pathways offer empirical evidence for countries to tailor innovation governance policies.

records.title: Prescriptive technology intelligence for technology opportunity discovery: An LLM-based automated framework for narrating promising technology concepts
records.verified_abstract: Existing technology intelligence approaches have largely remained at descriptive or predictive levels, limiting their capacity to provide specific and actionable prescriptions for technology opportunity discovery. This study introduces the concept of prescriptive technology intelligence and proposes a corresponding methodological framework. We present an LLM-based end-to-end framework that automatically generates narrative technology concepts from technological documents with minimal human intervention. Specifically, the framework constructs a technology knowledge graph and expands it by predicting latent relations and identifying structural technology themes. These components are then integrated and converted into explicit technology concepts using a graph-to-text model, with an LLM-as-a-judge approach further screening and ranking the most promising opportunities. An empirical demonstration using a large-scale dataset of artificial intelligence conference abstracts confirms that the proposed approach successfully transforms raw technological data into actionable R&D directions, thereby effectively facilitating strategic technology planning.

records.title: PATTERN-X: Guiding sustainable innovation in intelligent lighting systems through an explainable AI framework for technology convergence forecasting
records.verified_abstract: Strategic R&D management requires foresight tools that are dynamic, uncertainty-aware, and transparent, yet most existing approaches remain static, deterministic, and difficult to interpret. This study introduces PATTERN-X (Patent Analytics Through Temporal Network Evaluation and Reasoning with eXplainability), an explainable AI framework integrating temporal patent network analysis, Bayesian deep learning, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Using 4167 European Patent Office patents in the Intelligent Lighting Systems (ILS) domain (1981–2024), the framework is empirically validated within the European ILS innovation ecosystem. The study addresses three research questions: RQ1 examines how temporal network analysis can reveal the evolution of technology innovation ecosystems; RQ2 investigates how probabilistic deep learning can quantify predictive uncertainty for risk-aware R&D decision-making; and RQ3 explores how generative AI can translate quantitative forecasts into evidence-based strategic narratives. Addressing RQ1, temporal co-classification network analysis reveals ecosystem evolution from 3 to 16 technology clusters and a shift in centrality toward digital control and vehicle-integrated technologies. Addressing RQ2, a Bayesian LSTM achieves an MAE of 0.89, an 88% strategic hit rate, and well-calibrated uncertainty estimates (PICP = 0.91 against a nominal 95% interval, reflecting a slight undercoverage typical of variational approximations), enabling risk-sensitive evaluation of convergence opportunities. Addressing RQ3, a CPC-guided RAG system generates evidence-grounded strategic narratives with high faithfulness (0.85; κ = 0.82), translating probabilistic forecasts into auditable managerial explanations. Together, these results demonstrate how dynamic analysis, uncertainty quantification, and explainable generative AI can enhance technology convergence forecasting and strategic innovation management.

records.title: From threat to reconfiguration: How content creators reshape occupational identity in AI-driven creative practices
records.verified_abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is disrupting creative work and challenging occupational identities, yet limited research has examined how creators experience and respond to these changes. Drawing on Albert Ellis’s ABC model, this study investigates relationships among GenAI adoption, identity threat, job crafting, and identity consequences. Using a two-stage exploratory mixed-method design with digital content creators in China, we combined BERTopic analysis of 2994 open-ended responses with structural equation modelling of matched survey data from 1698 creators. The findings show that GenAI is widely perceived through coexisting beliefs about threat, opportunity, and the unknown, and that these beliefs give rise to differentiated job crafting behaviours, including approach crafting, avoidance crafting, and identity crafting. Notably, identity crafting plays an important role in fostering a responsible creative identity and self-actualization. This study advances theorizing on AI technological innovation and creative labour by showing how job crafting translates GenAI disruption into responsibility-oriented and meaning-centered identity reshaping. It also offers actionable insights for creators, platforms, and creative communities seeking to support collaborative, sustainable, and ethically grounded human–AI co-creation.

records.title: Exploring lipid nanoparticle design spaces using self-regulating microfluidic machines and multiplexed in vivo biodistribution
records.verified_abstract: Delivering therapeutic mRNA relies on lipid nanoparticles (LNPs). Finding optimal process parameters for new lipid combinations in LNP formulations remains a challenge. We used an automated, self-regulating microfluidic formulation platform developed for poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG)-containing LNPs that actively changes process parameters to meet preset LNP diameters, and now explore how this automated production setup can be expanded to LNPs decorated with poly(2-oxazoline) (POx)-lipids. We also examine how the choice of lipopolymer affects the resulting physicochemical properties and in vivo biodistribution of the resulting LNPs. For that, we tested new LNPs by swapping PEG-lipids for alternatives based on poly(2-methyl-2-oxazoline) (PMeOx) and poly(2-ethyl-2-oxazoline) (PEtOx). For both POx-lipid variants, the platform independently identified optimal production conditions in four or fewer iterative cycles, yielding particles of the preset size and high mRNA encapsulation. Small-angle X-ray scattering revealed that smaller LNPs modified with PEtOx had greater structural surface variety and higher mRNA loading efficiency. When multiplexing these formulations in mice, the PEtOx-containing LNPs accumulated more in bone marrow and liver (and less in spleen and pancreas), compared to those with PEG, indicating trends that the chemistry of the lipopolymer affects the biodistribution of the resulting LNPs. By combining automated formulation and in vivo multiplexed testing, our approach provides a practical way to rapidly plan, formulate, and evaluate large pharmaceutical design spaces to select excipients and process parameters yielding optimal biological performance of LNPs.

records.title: A multi-dimensional indicator system for identifying highly innovative papers: a knowledge absorption, creation, and diffusion perspective
records.verified_abstract: Conventional metrics often emphasize a single aspect of academic innovation, such as citation counts, topical novelty, or disruption, and therefore fail to capture the multi-mechanism processes through which academic innovation emerges and spreads. This study develops a multi-dimensional indicator system grounded in a knowledge-evolution perspective that conceptualizes innovation across three stages: knowledge absorption, creation, and diffusion. Each stage corresponds to distinct, measurable traces in citation networks and textual semantics. Furthermore, the framework integrates citation- and content-based indicators and refines topic-novelty and knowledge-disruption measures through semantic and temporal modeling to reduce granularity and aggregation bias. Empirical validation is conducted using 1940 publications by Price Medal recipients and their cited and citing records (54,045 unique documents). Robustness is further examined through inter-indicator correlation analysis, comparison with citation impact, case validation using top-ranked innovative papers and representative works by Loet Leydesdorff, as well as a cross-field validation experiment. Results demonstrate that the proposed system effectively identifies highly innovative research and captures domain-specific patterns of knowledge generation and dissemination, offering a comprehensive and scalable approach for evaluating academic innovation.

records.title: Contextual patterns of journal self-citation in JCR-suppressed and comparator journals: a multi-dimensional citation content analysis
records.verified_abstract: Traditional bibliometric approaches to journal self-citation focus mainly on aggregate rate-based indicators, leaving the content-level characteristics of self-citation behavior largely underexplored. This study proposes a six-dimensional citation content annotation framework covering citation position, distance, strength, function, depth, and semantic similarity between citation context and cited abstract, and applies it to a comparative dataset of ten journals across five JCR categories: five journals suppressed by Clarivate in the 2024 JCR release for self-citation concerns (suppressed-journal group) and five comparator journals in the same fields (comparator group). Self-citations in the suppressed-journal group are characterized by greater concentration in Introduction sections, shorter citation distance, lower citation strength, narrower citation functions, shallower citation depth, and lower semantic similarity. By contrast, self-citations in the comparator group exhibit greater functional diversity and broader contextual distribution across these dimensions. Discipline-level comparisons further reveal substantial heterogeneity across fields, suggesting that the contextual characteristics of journal self-citation vary considerably across disciplinary settings. Overall, by examining the textual context of journal self-citation, this study provides a content-level analytical perspective for examining journal self-citation patterns.

records.title: The association of eLife’s new publishing model with peer review lexical characteristics and early post-publication scientific impact
records.verified_abstract: The implementation of the new publishing model (NPM), which eliminates outright rejection after peer review by eLife since January 2023, has attracted widespread academic attention. Yet, its broader implications for peer-review practices and subsequent scientific impact remain underexplored. To this end, this study compiled a dataset of 5540 research outputs published by eLife between 2021 and 2024 under the NPM and original publishing model (OPM). Regression analyses adjusting for paper- and author-level covariates and publication-year fixed effects examined the association between publishing model and four measurement domains: lexical characteristics of peer review documents, online attention (views and downloads), citation-based scientific influence, and scientific evaluation reflected in citation contexts of citing papers. The results show that the NPM was not significantly associated with the polarity of published review documents but was associated with lower subjectivity and stronger positive and negative lexical expressions. NPM papers received more cumulative views and downloads but fewer mentioning and supporting citations; proportion-based analyses showed a lower proportion of mentioning citations but no significant associations with supporting or contrasting citation proportions. NPM papers received lower counts of citing papers within the first 12 months, including citing papers published in journals covered by the Nature Index. Most associations were similar in analyses using publication year-month fixed effects, although the association with supporting citation count was no longer statistically significant. Overall, the NPM shows differing associations across peer review and early post-publication scientific impact, including distinct lexical characteristics of peer-review documents, greater online attention, and lower short-term citation-based scientific influence within the first 12 months. These findings provide new empirical evidence on publishing models that move away from traditional accept/reject decisions and inform ongoing discussions on peer review and scientific publishing reform.

records.title: Originated versus imported knowledge: Revisiting the relationship between novelty and academic impact
records.verified_abstract: Knowledge innovation is considered one key driver of scientific impact. However, current studies overlook how cross-field knowledge flows shape novel knowledge creation, and our understanding of its creation patterns and relationship to scientific impact remains incomplete. By introducing a broader scientific context of over 30 million biomedical publications, this study uses biomedical entities and entity combinations identified through automated recognition as proxies for knowledge and quantifies paper impact by citation counts, using Alzheimer’s disease as an empirical case. We classify novel knowledge into either originated or imported based on whether the original source is the focal field, and subsequently analyze its distribution patterns and relationships with impact. The results show that 85.82% of novel entities and 55.84% of novel combinations are imported, indicating the dominance of imported knowledge. Regardless of knowledge sources, higher novel entity proportions are associated with reduced paper impact, and novel combination proportions show an inverted U-shaped relationship with impact, but the source affects relationship intensities. It is also evidenced that originated knowledge is more strongly associated with internal impact, while imported knowledge is more strongly associated with external impact. This study provides new perspectives and more comprehensive observations on the role of novel knowledge in shaping scientific impact.

records.title: Coordination complexity and its impact on disruption: A functional lead perspective
records.verified_abstract: Research collaboration has become the dominant mode of knowledge production, yet the "coordination complexity " inherent in teamwork remain an under-explored constraint on disruption. Prior studies typically treat teams as homogenous pools of diversity, often overlooking the critical coordination interface between the lead roles and its executors. This study introduces a "functional lead" perspective to investigate how coordination complexity affects the Disruption Index (DI). By analyzing 60,662 articles from Nature, Science, PNAS, and PLOS One, we distinguish "functional leads" from "supporting authors" based on self-reported contribution statements, CRediT, and examine four dimensions of dyadic distance: Specialty Similarity (SS), Racial Difference (RD), Academic Age Gap (AAG), and Geographical Distance (GD). Our empirical results reveal that coordination complexity appears to impose a structural tax on disruption. Specifically, SS, AAG, and GD are all significantly and negatively associated with research disruption. These findings suggest that cognitive redundancy (high similarity), hierarchical rigidities (large age gaps), and spatial isolation (remote collaboration) hinder the deep synthesis required to destabilize existing knowledge flows. These findings provide actionable insights for the Science of Team Science (SciTS), guiding funding agencies, institutions, and researchers in structuring collaborations for maximum research disruption.

records.title: Metabolomic Pathways Associated With Blood Pressure Reduction in the Chinese Heart-Healthy Diet
records.verified_abstract:
### Background

Although healthy diets are proven to reduce blood pressure, evidence from rigorously controlled dietary interventions remains scarce, offering limited insight into underlying mechanisms.

### Objectives

This study aimed to identify metabolic mechanisms linking a healthy diet to blood pressure regulation.

### Methods

In this randomized feeding trial, 265 adults with systolic blood pressure (SBP) between 130 and 159 mm Hg were assigned to either the Chinese Heart-Healthy (CHH) diet or a control diet for 28 days. Untargeted metabolomic profiling of serum and urine samples was performed before and after the intervention. Differentially changing metabolites between the 2 diet groups were identified using both linear mixed models and partial least-squares discriminant analysis. Correlation, pathway enrichment, and mediation analyses were subsequently conducted to further characterize metabolites and biological pathways that may plausibly link the CHH dietary intervention to reductions in blood pressure.

### Results

Fifty-two serum and 101 urinary metabolites changed differentially with 2 diets (variable importance in projection score > 1.0 and false discovery rate–adjusted P < 0.05). Among these metabolites, 17 were either associated with changes in SBP (false discovery rate–adjusted P < 0.05) or enriched in pathways prioritized in this study based on prior and present evidence of relevance to blood pressure; 4 met both criteria. Three of the 4 metabolites (ie, 2-octenoylcarnitine, 5-methylheptanoylcarnitine, and (2Z,4E,6Z)-decatrienoylcarnitine) were medium-chain acylcarnitines enriched in fatty acid oxidation, decreased with the CHH diet, and were positively associated with SBP. The fourth, tetrahydrobiopterin, enriched in tryptophan metabolism, increased with the CHH diet and was inversely associated with SBP. Collectively, all 17 prioritized metabolites mediated 33.3% of the CHH diet’s effect on SBP and 47.2% on diastolic blood pressure (DBP; corresponding to 3.3 and 1.8 mm Hg reductions). Nine metabolites enriched in the fatty acid oxidation pathway mediated 17.4% of the SBP and 17.6% of the DBP effects, whereas 3 metabolites enriched in tryptophan metabolism mediated 16.9% of the SBP reduction and 27.7% of the DBP reduction. Changes in dietary nutrients and food components, rather than sodium or potassium, largely accounted for shifts in these metabolites.

### Conclusions

We identified robust, biologically plausible pathways that may help explain how a healthy diet lowers blood pressure.

records.title: ACE-Net: 3D VFM-CNN Fusion with Adaptive Covariance Eigen-Gate for Coronary Artery Segmentation.
records.verified_abstract: Accurate segmentation of coronary arteries from CT angiography is crucial for quantitative stenosis evaluation and surgical planning. This task requires models to capture both global anatomical context and fine-grained local details. While 3D Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) and CNNs are naturally suited for these complementary roles, effectively fusing their heterogeneous feature streams remains a major challenge. To address this, we propose ACE-Net, a unified framework built upon a parallel dual-encoder architecture that couples a 3D foundation model-driven encoder (finetuned from SAM-Med3D) for global structural encoding with a 3D U-Net-based shape encoder for fine-grained local representation. To bridge the feature heterogeneity between the two streams, ACE-Net incorporates the Adaptive Covariance Eigen-Gate (ACE-Gate), which explicitly models interchannel dependencies via covariance analysis and eigenvalue decomposition, enabling adaptive and statistically grounded feature fusion. Extensive experiments on one in-house and two publicly available datasets consistently demonstrate that ACE-Net achieves superior performance and generalization ability, outperforming multiple state-of-the-art algorithms across various metrics. The Code is available at online.

records.title: Adapt: Multibeamformer with Tunable Weight Fusion and Patch-Wise Learning for Ultrasound Imaging.
records.verified_abstract: In the recent past, deep learning (DL)-based beamformers have been employed to accelerate adaptive beamforming for ultrasound imaging. However, most of these approaches are trained to mimic a particular beamformer type for a predefined depth of imaging and require complete retraining to adapt to a new beamformer and depth. In this work, we propose a novel deep learning framework, ADAPT (Adaptive Depth-Agnostic Patch-wise Tunable-multibeamformer), that employs a depth-wise patching strategy for computational efficiency and depth-independent learning. In order to develop a beamformer agnostic framework, the proposed approach first trains identical neural networks separately to derive the individual beamforming algorithm model weights, which are then fused via a tunable weighted averaging mechanism. This provides clinicians with dynamic and adaptable diagnostic perspectives, blending the acceptability of delay and sum (DAS) beamformer with the contrast of filtered delay multiply and sum (FDMAS) beamformer and the resolution of minimum variance (MV) beamformer simultaneously at very low complexity. ADAPT achieves 73 % speedup in training, 94 % reduction in computations and 94 % reduction in activation memory over a model trained over full depth.

records.title: HAGD: Hierarchical Anatomical-Guided Diffusion for Synthetic CT Generation from CBCT.
records.verified_abstract: Acquiring high-quality synthetic computed tomography (sCT) images from cone-beam CT is crucial for accurate dose calculation in the field of adaptive radiotherapy. However, existing sCT generation methods based on diffusion models often struggle to preserve anatomical structures, especially when the anatomical structure of the input CBCT and ground-truth CT differs in shape. To address this, we propose a Hierarchical Anatomical-Guided Diffusion (HAGD) framework that captures both global semantic information and local textural details for anatomical-aware sCT generation. We first introduce a dual-branch encoder to simultaneously extract features from coarse structural masks and fine segmentation maps. Secondly, a hierarchical fusion module is proposed to integrate these multiscale features into the conditional diffusion model, using concatenation or attention-gated fusion. Experiments on the SynthRAD2023 dataset show that HAGD achieves superior performance, with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 56.51 for concatenation fusion and 54.62 for attention-gated fusion improves performance over existing image translation models. These results highlight the effectiveness of structured anatomical guidance in enhancing fidelity and structural consistency of sCT images, thus supporting accurate and robust image translation in clinical radiotherapy workflows.

records.title: Improving Fairness in Vision Language Models for Medical Applications via Max Deviation Penalty.
records.verified_abstract:
Fairness in medical artificial intelligence (AI) tools is essential, as biased model behaviour can lead to unequal diagnostic outcomes and raise serious ethical concerns, ultimately reducing clinical trust. Although Vision Language Models (VLMs) show strong performance in medical imaging, they still exhibit demographic biases, particularly across gender, race, and other sensitive attributes.
Addressing these disparities is difficult due to the utility-fairness trade off, where improving equity often reduces diagnostic accuracy. To overcome these challenges, we propose the Max Deviation Penalty, a lightweight regularization objective that integrates seamlessly into parameter efficient finetuning schemes.
Experiments across diverse medical and general domain benchmarks demonstrate that our method consistently achieves state of the art performance in balancing fairness and utility, surpassing existing baselines enabling fair, reliable VLM adaptation.

records.title: Reconstruction Algorithm Based on Multi-Harmonic Feature Fusion and Enhanced U-Net for Low-Concentration Magnetic Particle Imaging.
records.verified_abstract: To address weak signals and severe background artifacts in low-concentration magnetic particle imaging, this paper proposes a noise-resilient reconstruction algorithm based on multi-harmonic feature fusion and an enhanced U-Net(MH-U-Net). Our algorithm introduces enhancements in both the signal and image domains to improve the reconstruction quality. In the signal domain, the algorithm performs a weighted fusion of the imaginary parts of the 3rd and 5th harmonics, utilizes filtered back projection to preserve highfrequency edges, and employs a grid search to determine the optimal weights. In the image domain, an optimized U-Net architecture driven by a joint loss function is employed for precise denoising. Experimental results demonstrate that our algorithm achieves high structural similarity on the training set, demonstrating a substantial performance improvement compared to the baseline algorithm provided by the official challenge dataset. It realizes MPI image reconstruction under low tracer concentrations, facilitating the biomedical applications of MPI.

records.title: Robust Circle of Willis ROI Extraction in MRA via Adaptive Landmark Detection.
records.verified_abstract: Accurate localization of the Circle of Willis (CoW) is essential for automated cerebrovascular analysis. However, existing approaches often rely on fixed metadata and struggle when parts of the vessels are not fully visible. We propose a landmark-based ROI localization method that detects key bifurcations and applies learned spatial margins to automatically crop subject-specific ROIs. To achieve full coverage of the CoW, missing bifurcations are estimated using anatomical symmetry or spatial offsets. The method achieved accurate vessel localization and preserved connectivity on two datasets: TopCoW (clDice 0.88, Betti0 0.17) and Lausanne (clDice 0.82, Betti0 0.15). By comparing our approach with the nn-Detection ROI localization, our method provides a more accurate and stable ROI localization. The approach is generalizable and independent of explicit ROI metadata.

records.title: Intuitive Gradient Feedback: Continuous Ultrasound Scan Quality from Weak Expert Preferences for Probe Guidance.
records.verified_abstract: Defining scan quality in medical imaging typically requires explicit geometric criteria and time-consuming annotation. We present a rapid method for learning a continuous scan quality indicator for pediatric hip ultrasound using expert intuition rather than predefined metrics. An expert performed 1,885 pairwise A/B comparisons across 480 images (2D DICOM and sampled frames from 3D volumes). These comparisons were converted into scalar quality labels using the TrueSkill ranking framework, with conservative estimates (μ−3σ) normalized to a 0–5 scale. An EfficientNet-B0 regression model trained on these labels achieved a Pearson correlation of R=0.895 and R²=0.798 on a validation set. When applied across frames of unseen 3D ultrasound volumes, predicted scores often formed smooth bell-shaped curves centered near higher-quality planes, suggesting that the network learned image features associated with expert preferences. This continuous quality signal could support real-time probe guidance in point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS), providing intuitive gradient feedback that guides operators toward optimal imaging planes without explicit landmark detection or segmentation. These results demonstrate that expert pairwise comparisons can rapidly generate supervisory signals for training practical scan-quality guidance systems.
